chapters.title: Introductory
chapters.subtitle: Bismilla hir-Rahman nir-Rahim Introductory

sections.heading: What the Flute says
paras: Hear, what the flute narrates about its separations; It says: “Ever since, I was cut off from the forest, men and women cry upon my lamentations. I want a breast that is torne to pieces due to separation from the beloved to which, I can speak of the details of the pains of love. Whoever that goes away from his origin, goes on searching for the days of togetherness with his people. I have cried in all gatherings of the happy and suffering people. Everyone befriended me according to the conditions of his own heart, but none cared to know of my inner secrets. My secret is not far away from me; but it gave no light of information to the apparent eyes and ears. It requires the eyes and ears of the inner spiritual qualities to know my secret, Body is not hidden from the soul; and soul is not hidden from the body. People only look at the body, and nobody cares to look at the soul.

The sound of the flute is considered as the blow of wind, but it is not so. It is fire; and that which does not possess fire gets annihilated. It is fire of love that has caught the flute. It is the enthusiasm of love that has penetrated into the wine. Therefore, the flute becomes a companion of the one who is suffering the pangs of the separation. Its tunes have torn off the curtains of our hearts. No one has seen the poison and antidote together as in the flute; and no one has seen a friend and lover like the flute. It speaks of the paths full of blood and of the affairs of the love of Majnun, who got himself destroyed in his love for Laila.

sections.heading: Two Mouths of the Flute
paras: It has two mouths: One is hidden in the lips of the blower, and the other one cries from the other side, which is visible to you, which creates commotion in the heavens. In reality, it is not the sound of the flute but of the blower. We have also two mouths in similar manner. We cry, laugh and talk from our mouths but it is God only who does all that through our mouths. We are like the flute. God is the blower and sound creator. Those with the inner ears and eyes know but the cries that come out of the visible mouth of the flute as actually the cries of the blower. The commotion that is bought about in our soul by the flute is caused not by the flute but by the blower. The consciousness of this fact comes about in the hearts of those who have lost their consciousness, just as, it is only ears that can take cognizance of the sounds coming from the mouth and no one else. Had the sound of the flute not been effective, the world of senses would have been deprived of the sweetness of love. Many of our days have been simply lost without anything, and many with the pangs of love. Tell the days which pass on simply without impacts, to pass on, as they are of no worth. Their worth entirely depends upon the company of the fair beloved. One who is in love is never satisfied with the sighting of the beloved just as the fish which is never satisfied with water. One without love simply wastes one’s life. The incompetent fellow cannot understand the affairs of the elite; so also, he cannot understand the affairs of those in love. How much ever we may speak to him of this is a waste. Let him go on his way.

sections.heading: Soul gives Euphoria and Cognizance
paras: Wine of its own is not euphoric. It is dependent upon us. It is totally effectless without our drinking. The heavens are in constant motion, but their motion can be realized by us only. Their motion is dependent upon us to be known. It is the wine that gets intoxicated by us; and not that we get intoxicated by wine. Our body is created for our sake and not that we are created for the sake of body. It is our inner soul that has created the body and observed everything. But everyone is not capable of hearing this truth. Fig cannot be the food of mean and humble birds. Our soul is imprisoned in the body which is greedy of gold and silver. Get out of the prisons of body and gold with the support of the might of love.

sections.heading: Not Greed but Contentment
paras: How much water can you take in your vessel from the river? What is the worth of a day out of the whole life? The vessel of the eyes of the greedy can never be filled. It is only contentment that can satisfy their greed. It is only with the contentment with a drop of water, that the oyster gets filled up with the wealth of the pearl. The lover possesses nothing but his garment; and even that he tears off in the madness of love.
Until you do like him and ignore possessions; you cannot be rid of greed and other defects.

sections.heading: Effects of the Madness of Love
paras: Be blissful, O madness of love, you are the physician of all our sicknesses. You are the medicine for our arrogance and search for honor. You are our Galen (the father of the science of physical sicknesses and medicines) and our Plato (provider of the development of mental faculties). Because of you the physical body (as of Hazrat ‘Is and Hazrat Muhammad) went above the heavens, and the mountain sprang up and danced (as it happened with Hazrat Musa. Love became the soul of Mount Tuur; it got intoxicated and Hazrat Musa became unconscious and fell down.

sections.heading: Everything in One
paras: In the high and low pitch of the flute is hidden the secret of existence of all in one (wahadatul wujud). If I clearly speak out of it, there will be great disorder in the world. The flute speaks of great things of the great in its high pitch and of the lowliness of the lowly in low pitch. It is fit only for the flute to spill it out and not for me. Let those capable of understanding it, may understand this through its pitch; and let me not speak for it, as my speaking will cause great disorder in the world. If I had also been held in the lips of the beloved as the flute is, through whose blows it speaks, I also could have done so. But I am like the one, who is away from the friend and his support, even though I have my own hundred supporters.

sections.heading: The Manifest and the Hidden
paras: You cannot hear the stories of the bulbul, when the garden and the spring season are no more. Where can I search for the fragrance of the rose when the garden is ruined, and flowers no more exist. I can find the fragrance only in rose water, in the absence of rose. But that is not a proper substitute. Everything in the universe is like a beloved and is clearly visible but its creator, God is like its lover. In normal course, it is the lover who is in open and the beloved is hidden behind curtains; but here, the beloved that is, the universe is manifest, but its lover the Creator is hidden behind the curtain. And this love of the Creator and the created is so strange that the created beloved appears living, open, visible and active and the Creator is so invisible, as though, dead and non-existing. (It is this strangeness that has confused the world in the understanding of God; and so many religious doctrines have come about. And it has also given rise to disbelief on Him—atheism).

sections.heading: Only with God’s Grace
paras: When the love of God does not take care of His lover, that is, his searcher the man, he becomes like a bird without feathers, and this is a very regrettable state. Our feathers and wings, like those of the birds are the loops of God’s love, which drag our wings and take us toward His abode and put us in love with Him. What can I speak in this matter, as I am conscious of all the affairs before me and on my back, as it is in the lack of consciousness only that one can speak of them and that is possible through the special light provided by Him. His light is on my right and left, and above and below me, and it has held me as the crown does with the head and the chains do around the neck. My love demands that these should be revealed, but this is possible only if the mirror of your heart is capable of observing them. You know that your mirror cannot reflect them as its polish is rusted. Only a clean, clear and bright mirror can reflect the rays of the light of God. First, clean the mirror of its rust and then try to seek His light. Hear what I say with all attention with the ear of your heart so that you may get out of the mixture of the water and clay of the body and provide the way for the soul, and thereafter walk upon the path of enthusiasm.

chapters.title: A king’s love for a Maid
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of a king’s love for a maid and buying her; and her falling ill and her treatment thereof

paras: Hear this story my friends, which is very much the truth of our present circumstances. If we find out our present situations, we shall be enabled to eat the fruits of the present-day world and also of the one to come later.

In the earlier days there was a king, whose kingdom encompassed the territories of this world and of the religion. Once the king went, along with his entourage for hunting. While he was searching for a prey in the hills and forests, he got himself trapped in the net of love. He saw a maid on the way. He fell in love and his soul became a slave of the maid. The bird of his soul became restless and got trapped in a cage. He paid the price for her and purchased her. Thus, he was successful in winning over her, but unfortunately for him, she fell ill. A fellow had a donkey but no saddle to put on its back to ride. With efforts he got the saddle, but the donkey was carried away by a wolf. One had a pot but no water, and when he found water the vessel broke.

The king collected physicians from all sides and said: “Lives of both me and the maid are in your hands. My life is very simple, but the life of my life is very precious. I am wounded and in pains, and she is the medicine for my sickness. Whoever treats and rids my life of sickness is entitled for the treasure of my pearls and coral stones.”

sections.heading: Meaning of God Willing: Insha-Allah
paras: All the physicians replied that they would put all efforts: “We shall ponder well over her sickness and treat her, each one of us is a messiah of the world and we have medicines for all the diseases.” But, out of their pride they did not say: “if God wills “; and therefore, God exposed to them of the helplessness of man.

By not saying: “God willing” is meant by me as blackness of heart. Yet it should not be taken just as verbal statement, as it is a momentary statement. It has to come from the heart. Many people have not said so by word of mouth, but their commitment was with the soul of “God willing.”

But whatever treatment they gave to the patient had no effect; and the sickness increased. The maid became thin like the hair due to her sickness; and the eyes of the king became like the streams of blood, because of his sorrow and tears. When fate starts playing its role, the physician becomes a fool and medicine gets misguided in the matter of treatment. Fate caused the increase of yellow bile with the mixture of honey and vinegar instead of decreasing it. Almond oil, instead of reducing, increased dryness. Laxatives caused constipation and water became supporter of naphtha and caused burning and fire. Tiredness of heart increased, sleep reduced, burning sensation caused in the eyes and the heart became full of sorrows and pains. The impacts of syrups and medicines increased the sickness and caused total dishonor to the physicians.

chapters.title: Failure of Physicians
chapters.subtitle: Failure of the Physicians in treating the Sickness of the maid and the King’s turning his Face towards God, the only King, in Reality

paras: When the king looked at the helplessness of the physicians, he went toward the mosque barefoot. He entered the mosque and fell down towards the niche, and the place of prostration became moist with his tears and he was lost to himself. When he came out of the depths of annihilation, he opened his mouth in praise and supplications. He said, “O God, You have made me a king in the world, but this is a very mean grant of yours. What shall I say to you? You are aware of all hidden matters. All qualifications of myself and the physicians are of no use before Your simple benevolence. You are the provider of refuge to all our needs. Yet I have gone astray from the path for the second time. The first wrong was in having faith in the physicians; and the second one is that I am speaking of my troubles to You, the One who is aware of all hidden things. But You have also said; Though I know all your inner affairs, yet you may speak to Me of your apparent affairs. You have said, ud‘uuni astajib lakum: pray unto Me and I will hear your prayer; (Mumin: 40: 60)

When the king said this from the depth of his heart, the river of God’s grace flooded with force. The king while crying went into sleep and in a dream, he saw an elderly man saying: “O king, hear this joyous news. Your prayer is admitted. If a stranger comes to you tomorrow, take him to be from us. He is an expert physician. Take him to be true and trustworthy. You may see magic in his treatment and the might of God in his temperament.” The king woke up from his sleep after this dream. He had become a slave of the maid, and after the dream he felt himself to be a king. When the day arrived for the promised stranger, sun arose, and made the stars to set. The king sat in the balcony, waiting for the revealing of the secret that was told to him. He saw a man in perfectness and wisdom, who appeared like the sun in darkness. He was appearing like the thin first night moon, from a distance, non-existing yet existing (due to thinness) like imagination, and saintly.

sections.heading: Imagination Exists as Mental Faculty
paras: Imaginations exist in the world as a nonexistence (non-physical). You may consider the world also as a passing imagination existing yet non-existing. The war and peace of the saints is in the thoughts and as per their imaginations. Their pride and disgrace are images only. These imaginations are the catching nets for reflections of the beauties of the garden of God. His mental image that the king had seen in his dream appeared on the face of the stranger. The light of God appears on the face of the saint, which can be seen clearly by you or anyone having a clean saintly disposition. When that saintly person appeared, though from a distance, light was falling all around him from his head to foot.

The king, instead of sending his attendants, himself went before the stranger-guest. When he greeted the stranger-guest, it was as though sugar penetrated into rose petals. Both of them were like the swimmers in the sea and penetrated into each other as though they were two bodies of one soul. One was like the thirsty and the other like water: one was like the intoxicated and the other like wine. The king said: “My beloved was not that maid but you. But in this world, one job gets finished by another. I am obedient to you only just as hazrat ‘Umar was to the Prophet. Like him I am ever ready to be at your service”.

chapters.title: Ill Manners
chapters.subtitle: Request for help to meet the desire to learn good manners and ill effect of ill manners

paras: We seek the support of God for good manners, as the ill-mannered are deprived of the grace of God. The ill-mannered does not spoil himself, but he sets fire to everything from horizon to horizon. Food was being sent to the Bani Israil from the sky in the form of manna and salva, the former as special edible grains and the latter quails (small game birds). [Manna is a gummy saccharine secretion found on a species of Tamarisk, and as per Hebrew tradition a small, rounded thing as small as hoarfrost. (needle like ice crystals) on the ground. For details see Abdullah Yusuf Ali’s exegesis of ayat 57 of Surah Baqarah (2) of The Holy Quran.]

This was received by them without asking and trading. Not being satisfied with this, some among the followers of the Hazrat Musa asked as to why there were no garlic and lintels. The supply of the free dishes from the sky was stopped and the entire community had to use farmland, pickaxes and sickles to procure their own food.

Again, upon the seeking by Hazrat ‘Is (Jesus), upon the demand of his followers: “O God, Lord of ours! Send down for us a table spread with food from heaven” anzil ‘alaina mai ’dadtan min al samaa’i (Quran: Surah 5:114), food in plates was sent for them, free from the sky. Then some un-cultured fellows ignored good manners and started hoarding the left-over food like beggars, though Hazrat ‘Isaa told them: “This supply is forever and will not vanish; and dont hoard it”.

Having suspicions on God’s grants and becoming greedy on a royal dining table amounts to thanklessness. Because of these begging, greedy, shameless fellows, the doors of the grants of God were shut upon them. Heavenly dishes came to be stopped and the dining table provided by God was folded up.

Clouds do not come about for not giving zakat (charity to the poor). And fornication (illegitimate sex) causes diseases from the surroundings. The darkness of sorrows falls upon you is for your rashness and ill-manners. One who shows rashness on the paths of friends, is a highway robber and un-manly. Good manners have brightened the sky: and out of good behavior only, angels became clean and immaculate. Sun gets into eclipse because of bad manners; and because of bad manners, Satan was chased away from the court of God.

One showing ill-manners in the path of the hearing of sacred esoteric sciences from saintly masters, gets confused and sinks into the valley of bewilderment. Stop at this, and tell the left-over story of the king, as whatever else you are talking about has no end.

chapters.title: Arrival of New Physician
chapters.subtitle: Meeting of the King with the Godly Physician he had seen in the Dream, whose Arrival was Informed to him

paras: When the king went closeby to the guest, he behaved like a beggar before him forgetting his kingly status. He spread his arms and embraced him and got him penetrated within his heart and soul like love. He kissed his hands and forehead and made enquiries about his place and journey. While making enquiries he walked with him towards the palace and said: “I have found out a great treasure after a long patience. Patience is bitter, but ultimately provides sweet fruits. You are the light of God and the reliever from narrowness of life, as it is well said that: patience is the key for expansion. Your appearance itself is an answer to all questions and certainly you will solve all problems. You are a spokesman of everything that is in our heart; and you pull out everyone caught in the swamp. Welcome O chosen one and the loved one! Do not go back. Your disappearance will cause death, and open fields will be narrowed. You are the master of the community. One who does not like you will certainly fall into destruction: as stated in the Quran: Let him beware! If he does not, We will drag him by the forelock: Kalla la ’illam yantahi lanas fa’an bil annasiati: (surah 96:15). Thus saying, he took him inside, spread before him the dining table; and thereafter took him inside the female apartment of the palace.

chapters.title: Physician goes Close to Patient.
chapters.subtitle: The King’s taking the physician to the patient

sections.heading: He narrated to him the affairs of the patient and her condition and then took him near the patient. He looked at the colour of the face and the urine and felt the pulse and heard of the symptoms and causes. And he said: “The medicines they have prescribed have not done well but ruined. They were not aware of the internal problems. I seek God’s protection from all the wrongs they have done”. He looked at the patient keenly and found out the secret of her sickness but did not reveal to the king. Her sickness was not due to yellow bile or black bile. The smell of the wood can be found out from its smoke. He realized that she has the sickness of heart. Her physique is healthy, but her heart is sick. The sickness of her heart is caused by love and there is no sickness as the sickness of the heart.
Love cannot be Explained but Experienced
paras: The sickness of the lover is different from other sicknesses. Love is the astrolabe of the secrets of God. From whatever side it may be, it ultimately leads us to God, the King. I may say many things to elucidate and explain about love. If I fall in love, I shall feel myself ashamed of my ignorance, as what all I said is incomplete. Though tongue offers a great exegesis to shed light on love, but the tongueless love is much brighter. The pen has written about everything in full, but when it reached the stage of the writing about love, it split. When its full explanation was required, the pen broke and paper got torne. Wisdom behaved like a donkey caught in a swamp while trying to explain about it. The explanation of love and lovability can be given by love alone, just as the evidence of the sun’s existence is given by the sun itself. If you want to get an evidence of love, you too will have to turn towards it just as you turn towards the sun. Though shadow also gives an evidence of the sun and opposites also can be taken as evidence of things.

sections.heading: Sun, not a Model to know God
paras: But the identification of God can be made only by the light that God Himself sheds upon your heart. Shadow caused by the sun makes you sleep just as a storyteller does. Look at this fact that when sun comes about, the moon gets spilt. The sun is always in a journey and none can match it in journeying. But it is caught in its yesterday and tomorrow. Though the sun is unique in its appearance, but its recognition is dependent upon others; and many other suns like it can also be imagined.

Yet, there is not a sun which has put the upper world in stupor which cannot come into the mind, nor can an example of it be found. There is no scope for taking it even in imagination as there is nothing like it, whatsoever. However, there is another Sun (Shams) from Tabriz, Shams Tabrizi (who gave spiritual inspiration to Rumi), who is an absolute light and is one among the lights of God. When the brightness of the face of this sun in the earth came about, the sun of the fourth sphere of earth hid its face.

Now that I have taken his name, it becomes necessary for me, to say something about his grants. As soon as, I took his name, my soul prepared itself to take his fragrance even from a distance, just as he had smelt the fragrance of Yusuf’s garments inspite of spatial and time distance from him. Yusuf was in a time, centuries apart, and at a long distance of Egypt from him. I have had his companionship for years and benefited from him and I am therefore obliged to say something about him, so that the sky and earth may smile, and wisdom and spirit may become hundred times brighter.

I said to his soul: “You have gone away from me without taking care of me when I am sick of love. Do not compel me anymore as I am already in a state of loss of understanding, and I am in the process of annihilation. I cannot explain about you in full. Whatever a semiconscious man says is unworthy of consideration, whether told spontaneously or with efforts. It is unsuitable on its own. What is said with efforts is still more unconsiderable. But what can I say, when even one vein of mine is not conscious about a friend who is uncomparable to anyone.

“Coming to the praise of God, I say that: praising Him amounts to no praise as it evidences my separate and distinct existence apart from His, which is incorrect. My praising Him amounts to self-praise. But keep the details of this separation from Him for another time. But my soul tells me: “Do feed me. I am hungry. Be fast: time is sharp like a sword. If you delay, time will pass off and I shall remain helpless.”

sections.heading: Sufis, Rinds, Qalandars, as Children of Time
paras: Even sufis who have discarded the world are overcome by time. Some of them are the children of time in the sense that they are controlled by time by thinking of yesterday and tomorrow. They are overwhelmed by their esoteric knowledge. They have no control on their own selves. They speak of their secrets and even exhibit their supernatural powers. Some of them are called Rind, that is, those, who appear to be sinful and of bad qualities, but in their interior, they are pure and noble. They are also called as Qalandars, that is, those who have no concern for normal rules of behavior and even Shari‘at, and instantly act according to the immediate inclinations of their heart. Thus, they are also children of their states, even though they have no concern for time: instant time of a moment and long-range time prolonged for years.

sections.heading: Sufis as fathers of time
paras: But there are sufis who are not children but fathers of time (Abul waqt), who have control on their selves, highly self-composed, who do not expose their state and do not resort to supernatural acts.

I told his soul further: “You are not a sufi of any of this kind. You are not the one to offer any knowledge to the unworthy today and feel sorry for it tomorrow just as a money lender lends and spoils his money”. I further told his soul: “The affairs of the beloved (God) are secret and better they remain as such. Yet, you know this also that, His affairs are told as stories relating to others.”

His soul told me: “Do not be a juggler of words, and do not harass me with confusing statements. Tell me openly, clearly, without hesitation. Tell me about the secrets and hints of the prophets. Informations about the faith are better if clear and well explained. Remove the curtains and come in the open as the beloved should be right before, in the open and not behind. But know this much that all prophets have taught the same thing: No God but Allah.”

I said: “If the beloved comes out in the open, its impacts will be such, which will take one nowhere: neither in the centre nor on the sides. One can make a demand, but it should be in consonance with one’s capacity to bear. A scrap of grass cannot bear the burden of a mountain. The sun, which keeps the entire world bright is suitable in its own place. If it comes a little on our side, it will set fire to everything. You are talking too much. Stop further talks and close your eyes so that the heart of the world is not destroyed. Do not try to create mischief and disturbance in the world. Do not try to enquire any more about Shames Tabrizi.” There is no end to this talk. Go out of it and speak about the left-over story of the king.

chapters.title: Diagnosis in Privacy
chapters.subtitle: The Physician’s Seeking Privacy with the Patient to Enquire about her Sickness

paras: With his discussions with the king, the physician got all known information and became his secret bearer. He told the king: “O king, vacate this house and let all the people go out of the house. Let not anyone hear by keeping the ears on the threshold as I want to ask some questions to the maid”. The king went out, left the house vacant to allow the physician to do what he wanted. Everybody left and only the physician and the patient remained.

sections.heading: Removal of Thorns
paras: The physician asked the maid slowly and politely as to which place, she belonged, as treatment of the people of different places is different. He made enquiries about her relatives and all concerned with her. He kept his hand on her pulse and enquired about all the troubles she underwent.

Because, when a thorn pricks a man’s sole, he keeps his foot on the thigh. With the tip of a needle, he searches the head of the thorn. If he does not get it; he moistens it with his lips. When it is so difficult to find out the thorn in foot-sole, imagine how difficult it is to find out the thorn in the heart. If everyone were to see the thorn in the heart, there would have been no scope for sorrows.

If someone pricks a thorn in the donkey’s tail, it does not know how to remove it. In order to get rid of the pain and burning, the donkey jumps, fells itself, rolls on the ground, raises dust and injures itself all the more. With all that it cannot get the thorn removed. It requires an expert to trace the thorn and remove it. But the donkey jumps and strengthens and sends the thorn deeper. A wise man is required to remove it.

sections.heading: Diagnosis of Sickness
paras: That physician was an expert in removing the thorn. He kept his hand here and there on the patient and tried. As though the maid was a child, he asked her about her past affairs. She openly revealed her secrets upon him about her earlier masters and the people of her place. The physician keenly heard what all she said, and at the same time touched her pulse constantly with all care, so as to know at what name her pulse would jump to conclude that, that person was her beloved.

First, she spoke about the friends of her city and then took the name of another city. He asked her about the place where she lived longer after leaving her own place. She spoke of that city, but the colour of her face remained unchanged and the pulse was as it was. She took the names of her different masters and places, one after one, and also about the favorite foods of those places. She spoke about different cities and houses in which she lived but neither her pulse jumped nor her colour went pale. There was no change at all; and the physician took the name of the sweet city of Samarqand. That moon faced patient took a long, cold sigh and tears started rolling down from her eyes like stream.

She said that a merchant took her to that place, and she was purchased by a goldsmith. He kept her with him for six month and then sold her off. While saying so she expressed all signs of sorrows and burning injuries. Her pulse jumped and her face turned pale indicating her separation from the goldsmith. When the physician heard of this secret, he found out the root of the cause of her troubles and sickness. He enquired the address of that goldsmith, and she said: it was near the bridge in the street of Ghatfar locality.
Then, the physician told her that she got rid of her troubles. “I have understood.

what your sickness is and I shall show a magic through my treatment. Be happy, contented and satisfied. I shall do for you what the rain does to the garden; I take to myself all your sorrows: and you may give up your sorrows. I shall be kind to you as a hundred fathers would be. But be careful, never to tell this secret to anyone, even if the king asks about it. As far as possible, this secret must not go out, and its doors are never to be opened upon anyone. If your secret remains within your heart, you will very soon meet your object.”

The noble Prophet has said: “He who hid his secret met his object very soon”. When a seed hides itself in the soil, it comes out as a green plant in the garden. If gold and silver were not hidden, they would not be taken care of by the mine.

sections.heading: Promises to be Kept
paras: With the kindness and promise of the physician the maid got rid of her fears. True promises appeal to the heart and false promises cause anxieties. The promise of the generous is a treasury of grants and that of the incapable is a torture to the soul. Promises should be kept up: and if you do not keep up, you become cold and immature. Promise should be kept with all heart and soul so as to see its grace on the doomsday.

chapters.title: Cause of Sickness Diagnosed.
chapters.subtitle: The Physician’s Finding Out of the cause of Sickness and Revealing it to the King

paras: When the kind physician found out the secret and the truth of the sickness of the maid, he got up and went to the king and gave him a little information about it. The king asked him as to what should be done then, and the reason for such a sorrow coming so late (as she was not sick when he bought her). The physician said that the goldsmith should be called as a means of the treatment for sickness. He said: “Send a messenger to him to inform him of the matter and make him take interest in the grants and rewards from the king. Call that goldsmith from that distant city and make him greedy of money and royal apparel so that your beloved maid may be pleased because of him, and all troubles may come to end. When that poor fellow sees gold and silver, he will leave his home for their sake.”
Gold makes wisdom mad, and particularly a poor man gets disgraced for it. Though gold actually brings about wisdom, but for this purpose, a wise and noble man is required.

chapters.title: Search for the Maid’s Beloved
chapters.subtitle: Dispatch of Messenger to Bring the Goldsmith

paras: The king heard the physician and accepted his advice with full heart: and said that he would pass orders as per his decision and obey him in all matters. Then, he sent two capable, efficient and experienced messengers to Samarqand. They went there and apprised the goldsmith of the happy message and said: “O expert master craftsman, you are well known in the cities for your intricate workmanship. Our king has chosen you for making jewels as you are considered to be very efficient in this job. Take this dress of honor, gold and silver from the king: and upon your coming to him, you will be provided with a special status and nearness to him.”

sections.heading: Money makes one take Risks
paras: When he looked at the gold, silver and dress of honor, the goldsmith was very pleased and preferred to depart from his city and children. With great joy, he took to the journey, ignorant of the fact that the king was after his life. He sat upon the fast Arabian horse and put on the royal dress in exchange for his blood. How sorrowful, that one goes on journey in great pleasure and voluntary proceeds towards death. His thoughts were upon power, honor and leadership, and the angel of death was telling him: “you may go over, all these things are waiting for you.”

When the goldsmith came over to the palace, the physician brought him before the king with all respect and honor, so as to burn him as the flame of the candle from the city of Taraaz, (which was renowned for its bright candles). The king also looked at him with honor and handed over gold to him, asking him to make bracelets, necklaces, anklets and waistbands. And also, various types of utensils in large numbers worthy of use in the gatherings of the king. The goldsmith took gold and busied himself in his work, ignorant of his tragical end.

Thereafter, the physician told the king to give over the maid to the goldsmith so that she may be pleased with him and the fire of her heart is extinguished with the water of the goldsmith’s company. The king gave over that moon-faced maid to him and got them married, who were both anxious to live together. For six month they lived together, upon which the maid completely regained her health. Thereafter, the physician provided a special syrup for him which he drank in her company and he slowly started going lean with a strange sickness and losing his charm as a result of which the lady started slowly losing her interest in him, and as he became ugly, pale and unappealing, her love completely become cold.

sections.heading: Beauty and wealth cause Hardships
paras: Love that goes after colour and charm is not love, and ultimately results in disgrace and shame. How good it would have been, if beauty had been permanent so as not to face cruelty later. If the love of worldly things had been lasting, it would not face disgrace. Blood started flowing from his stream-like eyes; and his face itself became the enemy of his soul. Feathers of the peacock are its enemies. Many great kings met their death because of their pomp and pageantry. When the goldsmith’s condition worsened and his body melted and became thin like the scrapes of the sharpened pencil, he said: “I am a deer for the sake of the navel of which, its blood is flowed down by the hunter. I am that wild fox for who’s fur they wait for long, catch and cut off the head. I am the elephant which is killed by its master for the sake of ivory. One who killed me for the sake of one inferior to me, does not know that my blood would not go waste. The trouble that has come upon me today will be upon him tomorrow. The blood of a man like me will not go without showing results.

sections.heading: Love of World and Love of God
paras: Though a wall puts a long shadow, but later the shadow returns to itself. This world is like a hill, where our sound returns to us as an echo. He said so and died and went underground and got rid of the pains and sorrows of the maid, because the love with the dead does not last long as the dead will not come back to us.

Love of Everliving God subsists in the inner eye of the soul and always remains fresher than a flower. Fall in love with the One, who is everlasting, who is capable of freshening you with a life-giving liquor. By adopting His love all prophets got honors and nobility through His love. Do not say that you cannot go up to that great King, as great jobs are not difficult to perform by the graceful people.

chapters.title: Killing, not for Personal Gain
chapters.subtitle: To explain that the Killing of the Goldsmith was upon a Godly Direction and not with Evil Intentions

paras: The killing of that man at the hands of the physician was neither for any expectation, nor out of any fear. He did not kill him for the sake of the king, but it was upon the receipt of an inspiration from God. A boy’s throat was slashed by Hazrat Khizr, the secret behind which cannot be understood by the lay people. One who receives revelation and address from God speaks of certain things which are perfectly correct. It is perfectly proper for One (God) who grants life, to take life. A person, who takes away someone’s life as a representative of God, does so, with the hand of God. Therefore, keep your head before Him like Hazrat Ismail and get killed happily and joyously with the sword, so that your soul may remain happy forever like the soul of the noble Prophet with Unique God. If the beloved kills the lover, the lover takes this killing as a cup of the drink of joy.

sections.heading: Goldsmith’s Killing: for Hidden Reasons
paras: The king did not kill him to meet his desire. Be sure of it; and do not involve yourself in unnecessary arguments. You suspect that it was to meet his personal ambitions, but it is not so, because cleanliness does not go with the dirty. This difficult effort of piety and that cruelty were to remove the impurity from silver by putting it into fire. It was to make a test of good and bad, just as gold is melted to remove its impurities. Therefore, give up the mistake of making wrong suspicions and read in the Quran: Avoid suspicion as much (as possible); for suspicion in some cases is sin: Ijtanibu kath(s)iiram minnazhzhanni: inna ba’dhazhanni ith(s)mun: (Hujurat: 49:12).

If his act was not upon a direction from God, he would not be a king but a wild-tearing dog. The king was free from passions, greed and desire; and what he did was right, but if appears to be wrong. Though Khizr damaged the boat in the river, but that damaging had a hundred right results behind it. Inspite of Hazrat Musa having all the light of knowledge and expertise he could not know the matters hidden behind Hazrat Khizr’s act. When that is so with Hazrat Musa, why to beat behind the bush. The king was a red flower, and do not consider him to be bloody. He was full of wisdom; and do not call him mad. If spilling the blood of a Muslim was done by him, I would be an infidel for taking his name. Empyrean (‘Arsh) shakes upon the praising of a hard-hearted fellow and the pious get into suspicions. He was a king, and a very well-informed king. He was an elite and especially gifted by God.

A person killed by such a king will be granted a throne and the best of the rewards. If he takes one life, he protects a hundred lives; rather he gives so much that you would not even imagine of. Showing cruelty to a special person for the general good of all is permitted by the law (shari’at) also. Therefore, stop at this, and proceed further. If the king had not seen something good for the goldsmith in killing him, why he, being full of generosity and kindness, would have resorted to cruelty? A child shivers at the thought of being pierced with the needle for bloodletting, but his loving mother gets pleased at it.

You consider the acts of God upon your own short-sighted speculations, but if you think seriously, you will see many faraway events of gains, and good results. Come close to me: I shall tell you a story. Perhaps, you may gain something of what I have narrated:

chapters.title: Story of Parrot becoming Bald
chapters.subtitle: Story of a Merchant and Parrot and Spilling of Oil by the Parrot in the Shop

paras: A merchant had a parrot with a pleasing sound, well speaking and green colored. It used to take care of the shop and speak with other merchants on interesting matters. It was very wise in talking with others and also with other parrots.

The merchant had left the shop and gone to his house one day, and the parrot was watching the shop. Suddenly a cat jumped into the shop to catch a rat and the parrot panicked. It jumped into the middle of the shop and by doing so felled the bottles of rose oil. The merchant returned from his house and sat down joyously and contented in the shop. He saw the shop full of oil and the textiles oiled and greased. He got wild in anger and kicked the parrot so hard that the hairs of its head pulled out and it became bald. It stopped talking for some days and the merchant felt very sorrowful and ashamed. He used to scratch his beard and say: “How sorrowful, the sun of my grants has gone behind the clouds. It would have been good if my hands were broken at that time, when I had struck upon the head of the parrot.”

He started to give alms and offerings to the poor so that with their blessings the parrot may start talking. After three days and nights, he was very much worried and anxious, and sitting in extreme desperation in thousands of sorrows and pains, worrying as to when the parrot would open its mouth. He had showed many strange objects to it to put it in surprise so as to make it speak; but it was of no use. He talked to it differently every now and then so that it might speak out in surprise. He showed different kinds of pictures too, and that also had no effect.

Once, a darvesh wrapped up in blanket passed that way whose head was completely bald and plain like a plate and the outer side of a trough. Looking at him, the parrot called him and asked him as a wise man would say: “O bald man, what made you to join among the bald people? Perhaps you had also felled oil from the bottle.” People laughed at this, that the parrot considered that darvesh also as one like itself.

sections.heading: Different Pronouncements of our Writings
paras: Do not consider the acts of the noble people according to your standard. When you write the word “shair,” it appears the same to mean “lion” as well as “milk”. Its spelling and shape is the same but meanings entirely different. “Sheer” (milk) is something which man drinks and “shair” (lion) is that animal that eats the man.

sections.heading: Confusion caused by Similarity
paras: The entire world is in confusion because of some kind of similarity of appearance. Very rarely one distinguishes the elevated saintly man of the level of “abdaal” (one who has converted his vices into virtues) from other men appearing like abdaals. The unfortunate fellows do not have eyes that would see and recognize such great men. Both good and bad appear the same to their eyes. Many considered themselves as at par with the prophets and declared themselves to be like them. They considered the saints as similar to themselves and said: “We are men; and they are also men. Both are obliged to eat and sleep.”

With the blindness of their eyes, they did not understand that there is a great difference between them. Beetles eat from the same place, but some have piercing, injuring stings and others make honey. Both kinds of deer eat the same grass and drink the same water, but one produces musk and the other one only dung. Two kinds of canes drink water from the same pond; one is hollow, and the other is sweet with sugar. There are hundreds and thousands of such examples before you, with a distance of seventy years journey between them.

One eats and excretes filth and another eats and becomes a light of God. Another eats and increases his miserliness and jealousy, and yet another eats and becomes one with the light of the One and Only God. This land is clean and fertile, and that land is barren and bad. One is a clean person like the angel, and another is a devil and beast. Two waters appear to be the same, yet one water is saltish and the other is sweet and clear. It is only those with a taste and experience, who differentiate between these for their saltiness or sweetness. Only one with a sense of taste realizes taste. One who has not tasted honey cannot understand the difference between honey and wax.

sections.heading: Magic and Miracles
paras: Looking at magic as similar to miracles, some people consider both as tricks and designs. Magicians came to fight with Hazrat Musa, with clubs similar to his. But there is a great difference between Hazrat Musa’s club and their clubs. There was the grace of God behind Musa’s club and God’s wrath behind others. Infidels possess the character of monkeys in their quarrels and this is a hidden calamity in their hearts. Whatever a man does is done by the monkey when it sees a man regularly doing it. It thinks that it has done like what man does without realizing the difference between the actual and imitation.

sections.heading: Mumins and Munafiqs (Faithful and hypocrites)
paras: The faithful man acts as per the command of God, but the infidel does only for the sake of opposition and puts dust upon his own head. A hypocrite also joins for prayer along with the faithful. There is a great difference between them. One prays to offer his submission to God, the other one to compete with him. Both the faithful and the hypocrites are on the winning and losing sides respectively in the performance of salat, fasting, hajj and zakat. Ultimately, it is the faithful who will win, and the hypocrites will lose. Though, both of them are engaged in their affairs but they are faraway from each other and are as distant as Merve in Khorasan and Rayy in Iraq. They are going towards their appointed places and function according to their names. If you tell a mumin that he is a mumin, he gets pleased; but if you call a hypocrite as munafiq, he gets excited and wild. The name of mumin is lovely because of its nature; and the other one is hatable and inimical because of its content of troubleshooting and mischief.

sections.heading: Words are not Letters but Meanings
paras: There is no nobility in the alphabets mim (m), vaw (o) mim (m) and Noon (N) of which the word mumin is made. It is just a word of identification, and nothing else. If a hypocrite is called as such (munafiq), it hurts him as it is ignoble. It pricks into the ear like the sting of scorpion. If this word does not relate to hell, then why does it taste like hell. The viciousness of a name is not because of its letters, just as the bitterness of the sea water is not due to the vessel in which it is filled. Letters are like vessels and the meanings are like water. The ocean of words is God, the One who possesses the “Mother of all Books” (ummul kitaab), and the protected tablet (Loh-e-Mahfooz). The bitter and sweet seas go together and in between them is the barrier of Barzakhul laa yabghiyaan: as stated in the Quran: Marajal Bahraini yaltaqiyaan. Bainahumaa Barzakhul laa Yabghiyan (He has let free two seas, flowing together (side by side). There is a barrier between them. They do not encroach (one upon the other); (Surah: Rahman: 55:19, 20). Therefore, know that both of them are from the same source; and forget both and go toward the source.

sections.heading: Seek Verdict from Heart
paras: In order to test true gold and its counterfeit there is a need for touchstone, without which it cannot be valued. Whoever is provided by God with a touchstone in the heart, will certainly be able to separate doubts from certainties, as what is stated by the Prophet, Istafti qalbaka: (seek the verdict from heart) is known to him alone, who is full of honesty. This seeking is not required for the common man. He can go by what the scholars of religion say. If a scrap falls into the mouth of a living man, he will not get rest until it is removed from the mouth. Even a scrap going into the mouth of a person, out of thousands of morsels of food that he eats, can be detected by him. Understanding of this world is a ladder for the life here; and also of the next world. Find out the health of this world from the physician; and of the other world from a saintly person, who is a lover and beloved of God. The health of the senses of this world is from the upkeep of the body, but that of that world is from the crushing of the body.

sections.heading: Crushing of Body to Enrich Soul
paras: The king of the soul crushes the body and with the crushed body, he builds up a new (next) world. That soul is very prosperous which, with its attention toward the next world, gives up its property, wealth and country. In order to get the great treasure of the spiritual elevation, a searcher destroys his house (body) and with the attainable treasure of spiritual attainments, reconstructs and rehabilitates it very much. He closes the source of water to clean the channel of the stream, and then lets clean water in it to flow. He drags the arrow that has pierced his flesh and causes a wound which is later filled up with fresh flesh. He captures the fort in possession of the infidel (devil), destroys it and builds in its place hundreds of new bastions and walls, just as warriors do.

sections.heading: Very Little known of God
paras: No one can speak of all the functions of God. This much is said here only out of necessity. Sometimes, He is visible through His lights in one manner, and sometimes, through its opposite in the form of its reflections. The search for Him results in more and more wonders. Even those who have fully understood the secrets of His truth are wonderstruck, unsettled, inebriated and mad, and out of self-control. There is a wonderment that causes doubts; and there is another that causes involvement; and the perfect, feel involvement. Their wonderment is not of the former type where they get doubts. They are on His back side, but for the latter type His face is right in front of them involving them within it. In one case their face is toward the Friend (God) and in the other, their own face is the face of the Friend (God). You should look at the face of both of these great men with great honor. By doing so, there is a possibility of your also getting informed of the secret and truth of the Friend. Looking at such knowing persons also is a kind of worship, which results in the opening of the doors of fortune.

chapters.title: True Knowers and False Claimants
chapters.subtitle: Difference between the True Knower of Truth and False Claimant; and of the truthful and the Liar

paras: As there are many satans with human faces, your hand should not be given into the hand of everyone. Bird-catchers produce sounds of the birds to cheat the birds. When the birds hear the sounds of the bird of their flock, they come down from the air and get trapped in the net spread by them.

Similarly, some mean fellows steal the words and phrases of the saint in order to play tricks upon simpletons. The real saints have the task of spreading light and warmth of faith upon the people, and the mean fellow’s resort to cheating and shamelessness. Just as beggars make models of lions with wool to entertain people to collect money, these mean fellows call Musailama Kazzaab, the Liar, as Muhammed and cheat. Musailama was a liar and so he was called as a great Liar (kazzaab). [He had made a false claim of prophethood, enrolled some simpletons as his followers, made an army of them and ruled some parts of Yamama, a province in Arabia. Hazrat Khalid bin Walid had attacked and killed him during the reign of Hazrat Abu Bakr]. But how could he be compared with the Prophet, who was named Oolu al bab, the man of wisdom. He was the seal of the bottle of the wine of Truth, which was pleasing like musk, but the seal of the wine of untruth is dirty and foul.

chapters.title: Story of Fanatical Jewish King
chapters.subtitle: Story of the Jewish king who killed Christians due to Fanticism

paras: There was a cruel king from among the Jews, who was very inimical towards Hazrat ‘Is and Christains. It was during the days of Hazrat ‘Is’s life, but he was so devoted to Hazrat Musa as though he was his life and Hazrat Musa, was his. The king was squint-eyed and would see two numbers of a single thing; and in his path towards love, he saw Hazrat Musa and Hazrat ‘Is as different, though both stood for the same thing — Love and regard for God.

sections.heading: Excessive love and Wrath make one Squint
paras: A wise counselor told him to get into his house and bring out a bottle from inside. When he entered the house, he saw a single bottle appearing to him as two. He asked the counselor as to which one was to be brought for him. The counselor told him that there was only one bottle and not to see more numbers than that and give up his squint behavior. The king replied: “Do not pass remarks on me”. The counselor told him to smash one out of the two. When he smashed the one, both the bottles vanished.

Man becomes squint both in love and wrath. There was one bottle and it appeared two to him. When he smashed one, the other one also was not there. Passions and wrath make a man squint-eyed and take away the soul from the right paths. When man is occupied with selfishness, beauty and art get hidden from his sight; and hundreds of curtains fall on the eyes in the path of the heart. When the judge settles on a bribe, he cannot find the difference between the cruel and the victim of cruelty. The king, out of his fanatic love for Judaism became so squint, that only God’s protection and peace could save the people from him. No justice can be expected from such persons. He killed hundreds of thousands of faithful people because of his fanatical support for the protection of the religion of Hazrat Musa.

chapters.title: King’s Mischievous Minister
chapters.subtitle: Story of a King’s Minister’s Mischiefs and Tricks to cause Friction between Christians and Zoroastrians

paras: A king had a very treacherous, misguided minister, who was such a trickster that would twist and put a knot on water. Christians could protect their life only by hiding their faith from the king. He told the king: “O king, the one in search of mysteries, do not kill them and give up bloodshed. Do not kill them anymore as it is not beneficial, as religion has no fragrance, no musk, and no ambergris. It is a secret that is hidden behind a hundred wrappings. It is with you in appearance, but its inside is against you.” The king asked him as to what his design was to meet with the situation and what was the treatment for this treachery: “I want to see that there is no Christian in the world, either in the open or in secret.”

The minister said: “Cut off my ears and hand and pass a bitter order to split my nose and lips. And then bring me under the scaffold and keep me held up there until someone comes to recommend for my release. Do all this in the public square of the city where royal announcements are made. Thereafter, send me away from the city, so that I may raise hundreds of mischiefs. When the Christians start taking me as their man, their condition will be totally ruined. I shall create such trials and turmoils among them that even the Ahriman (devil in the Zoroastrian mythology) will get shocked at my craftiness. What I would do with the Christians cannot be explained.

“When they take me as sincere and their secret bearer, I would spread a net of another type. I shall cheat them by all designs and spread over them hundreds of tricks and frauds to such an extent that they would spill their own blood on the ground. This much only, I can speak about.”

chapters.title: Minister’s designs to kill Christians
chapters.subtitle: The Minister’s Design to Cheat the Christians

paras: He continued: “Then I shall tell them that I am a Christian in secret. God knows this secret. The king came to know of my faith in Christianity and out of his hate for Christianity, resorted to take my life. I had thought of hiding my faith and show myself as a man of the king’s own faith. The king came to know of my secret, and what I had been telling became a lie before the king.”
The king said: “What you say is like a needle hidden in bread. I have fully understood and seen what your design is through the hole of my heart. Now, there is no need for you to tell me.”

The minister continued: (I shall tell the Christians). “Had not the spirit of Jesus been with me, the king would have cut me to pieces as he does with the Jews. I am ready to give my head and life for Jesus and consider all troubles as his hundreds of thousands of benevolences upon my soul. I have no hesitation whatsoever to offer my life for Jesus. I am very well aware of his religion. I see this with great concern that this clean religion is getting spoiled upon reaching these crude, ignorant fellows. It is a great grant of God and Jesus upon us that we are the leaders of this true religion. We were freed from the clutches of the Jews and Judaism, eversince we have worn the thread hanging down in our necks carrying the holy cross with it and determined to defend it. O people hear this from me that this period is the period of Jesus only. Know the secret of his religion with all care and attention. This king is very cruel and irreligious. He does not understand the difference between friend and foe”. [The minister was talking so much about the Christians, but his heart was with the king.]

He further told the king: “O protector of the world, have patience, so that I may destroy them right from their roots. When they would develop faith in me and my sincerity, they will take me as their leader, bow down their heads before me and pray to me to lead them.”

When the minister spoke of these designs to the king, the king got rid of all worries about him. The king did all that he was told to do, and people were unaware of the design. The king disgraced him before all the people in the gathering, and all people, men and women, became aware of this disgrace. And he was chased away toward the Christians, where he started his missionary work. When the Christians found him in this wretched condition, they wailed upon him.

chapters.title: Envy: Root cause of Evils
chapters.subtitle: Collection of the Christians before the Minister and his Revealing of the Secret

paras: “O young men take note of this: All these things come about because of envy. Hundreds of thousands of Christians assembled in batches in his street. He would explain to them in private about the esoteric aspects of Gospel, its connection with the cross and prayers. And also, about the acts and statements of Jesus with elucidations. Though apparently, he was a preacher of the fundamentals of faith, but deep inside his words were like the whistling’s of the bird-catchers to trap the birds in their nets.

sections.heading: Human Soul: Main Target of Devil
paras: It is upon this understanding that companions of the Prophet used to question him about the treacheries of the devils of the nafs (human soul). [The human soul is distinct from animal soul. As against humans other creatures have only animal soul, which comes to end upon death. So also, with man. But apart from the animal soul, man is bestowed with another soul, which is referred to a human soul by Avicinna and Alghazali, which does not end with death. It continues to exist without body and out of the body. So long as it is in the body, all actions, thoughts, and feelings of man are controlled and possessed by it. All questions about deeds and misdeeds of man after death, all pleasures of paradise and tortures of hell are meant for it. During the lifetime of man, consciousness, conscience, sense of honor, guilt, disgrace etc, peculiar only to man as against other living beings, are cognized by it. This is a very elaborate subject of study, which can be found out in Alghazali’s ’Ihya-ul - uluum in the chapters - understanding of God, wonders of the heart, cognizance of nafs in particular, and references and inferences to it generally in almost all chapters. Wherever the word “heart” is used in this book, means nearly the same and not the lump of flash which pumps blood –Translator]

The human soul secretly gets mixed up with hidden desires of selfishness in the performance of worship, and sincerity in the actions of heart and the performance of noble, religious, pious acts. The noble companions of the Prophet would not ask him about the excellences and values of prayers, but about the searching of hidden defects in them. They used to understand the treacheries of the soul in threadbare analysis and its very minute aspects and differentiate very lucidly as one would differentiate between a sweet-smelling flower and foul smelling (karfis) grass. These were explained by the close companion: Hazrat Huzaifa bin Yamaan, to Khwaja Hasan Basri (death 728 AD) one of the founders of distinct Islamic Tasawwuf. Consequent upon this, his preachings, lectures and narrations of Islamic aspects become great and pleasing. His elucidations were so delightful and exhaustive that other enquirers, analysts and elucidators of the reports of the companions used to be flabbergasted.

sections.heading: Insinuations and Traps of Devil
paras: (Returning to the narrative of the minister): All the Christians offered and gave over their hearts to him. How strong is the strength of blind followership! They sowed the seed of his love in their hearts and considered him as the direct representative of Jesus. He was a hidden and accursed one-eyed Dajjaal (Antichrist) [who would come to cheat and rule the world, who would be killed by Jesus on his second coming.]
O God, the Best of the supporters, hear our complaints and give support to us.

O God, there are hundreds of thousands of nets and grains and we are like the hungry, greedy, helpless birds about to be caught. We get trapped in a fresh net every now and then, even though we are smart like the falcons and seemurgh, (an extra ordinarily sized bird which is believed to live in the Caucasus mountains, whose feathers have thirty different colours). You released us from the trap many times, yet we go toward some kind of trap or the other.

We collect wheat grain in a bag and lose the collected grain soon. When we think over the loss, we feel that it is due to the treacheries of the rats, which have caused holes in our bags, through which our collected wealth gets ruined.

sections.heading: Rumi’s Specific Advice on Insinuations
paras: O my dear, first eliminate the mischief of the rats and thereafter try to collect the grains. Hear this statement from the leader of the leaders: “No salat is complete without the total inclination of the heart towards it.” What is required first in our acts is the elimination of the insinuations of the devil. The devil’s insinuations in our good acts are like the rats which spoil our prayers and good acts for forty years [Up to forty years of age a man passes through the period of ignorance and irresponsibilities of childhood, boyhood, and youth then uptill when wisdom and sense of responsibility are not mature, and much of what is collected gets lost, or polluted or damaged. It is after forty years that man fully matures in most of the aspects of life — Qazi Sajjad Hussain.]

Why do our sincere and truthful efforts get collected into the lots of our collections? Why do we still remain empty handed? What happened to the wheat collected by us for forty years? That was spoiled by the rat hidden in us. Many lights of enlightenment came about in our heart, like sparks emitting from red hot iron. These are received and absorbed by our mad heart. But there is a hidden thief (Satan) sitting in our heart who puts his finger at the source of enlightenment and pulls it out. He extinguishes the sparks instantly so that a lamp may not burn on the sky of our heart. O God, if your grants happen to be with us, there would be no fear of that mean, hidden thief. There are no causes of any worry if You are with us on every one of our steps, even if there are thousands of traps.

sections.heading: Souls Temporarily Released
paras: Every night (during sleep), You release our souls from the body. Likewise, You may uproot the tablets of the writings of insinuations from our hearts. When the souls get freed from the cage of the body every night during sleep, they become free of the commander and the commanded.

This happens in the case of prisoners in the prison. They get into sleep and forget about imprisonment. Officers of the government sleep without the anxieties of the administration of the state. Nobody has any worry about the calculations of profits and losses during sleep, nor of this man and that man (or enemies and friends).

sections.heading: Companions of the Cave
paras: But one, who has understood God remains carefree of everything even when he is awake. It is about such of them that God has said: “they are asleep”: hum ruqud. [This is stated about the ‘Companions of the cave’ who were a group of noble men who during the time of Emperor Decius (Dacianus), hid themselves in a cave, where they slept for a long time. About their sleep, the reference is to ayat18 of Surah Kahaf: Tahsabuhum aiqazhun, wa hum ruqudun: You would have deemed them awake, while they were asleep.]

Do not ignore the fact of their long sleep. Think over its esoteric meaning. A man in sleep remains unaware of all that is happening in the world. He is like a pen in the hand of God. He does not act himself; everything is done by God. One who does not see the hand, looks at the movements of the pen and thinks that it is the pen itself that is moving, of its own.

chapters.title: God Kills and gives Life
chapters.subtitle: Example of the Gnostic (well aware of God). exegesis of: Allahu Yafawaffa al anfusu hiina mautiha: It is God that takes the soul (of men) at death: (Surah Zumar: 39:42)

paras: Gnostics, who are well aware of God, get rid of all anxieties even when they are awake which others get during sleep. This situation cannot be understood by all. Therefore, to give a little information about this, God has made the common people understand this through sleep, which makes them go totally out of the control of the senses, when they do not see and hear, and get rid of the impacts of the five senses. Their souls in such situations remain away from this observable material world of senses and go into another world with a vast empty field without dimensions, which cannot be exemplified.

sections.heading: Explanation of Non-material World (Barzakh)
paras: The world in which we are living is one of six dimensions of back-front, right-left and top-bottom. These dimensions are absolutely required to keep matter as it is. Otherwise, the matter we see here would be different. But that world is a world of no dimensions, where no material can exist. That is the world of quiescent, dormant non-material existence. This is also called Barzakh, which is a barrier between the lower-material- visible world of our bodies and the higher spiritual world.

The soul during sleep enters into that world and gets into complete rest without any concern for the material bodies including the material of man. This departure causes great relief to the body and after this, when it returns, man wakes up and once again gets involved in the material world through his body with senses. [After death, the soul remains here till the doomsday].

sections.heading: Gnostics remain Untroubled Throughout
paras: The gnostics who keep themselves away from the greed of the world, inclinations towards it and the tensions of gain or loss, become free of all tensions throughout life just as a bird flown away from the cage. The common men get this relief so long as they are in sleep, up to the time when the sun, the Turkish solider of the day with its golden shield comes forward to behead the Hindu (thief) of the night.

Every soul has its inclinations toward the body; and every body carries the burden of soul. Just as the bird-catcher whistles and drags the bird to the trouble-giving-net, your body calls back your soul, upon waking up to make arrangements to meet the troubles of life. This happens when the light of the morning appears, when the golden vulture of troubles comes flying in the sky. The cleaver of the daybreak comes out of the darkness of night like Israfil, as if blowing his trumpet for doomsday, to wake up all dead, bringing together all men, to perform their daily acts once again. The sleeping men are taken towards various places of troubles for the day. Thus, he takes all the souls back to their bodies and makes them active again. Thus, every sleep is a temporary mini-death.

sections.heading: Sleep: Sister of Death
paras: Sleep is also called as a sister of death, as sleep snatches away the saddle of the horse and makes it unusable. It ties its legs with a long rope of the night and releases it during day. Then, it takes the horse to the field to bring the vast grassland under the burden of its hoofs. It would have been very good if the soul were kept under the protection of the sleep for a longer time as it happened in the case of the Companions of the cave; or as Hazrat Noah was kept protected in the Ark; so that this flood of wakefulness and consciousness be away from the eyes, ears and heart. Yet there are many persons (saints) like the Companions of the cave around you in the world, but you are not aware of them. They are together in friendship with each other in pleasure, in the cave which is also pleasing to them all. But your ears and eyes are sealed. You cannot see them. Now, you may ponder why these curtains are tied before us and why our eyes and ears are sealed!

chapters.title: Doubts on Laila’s Beauty
chapters.subtitle: The Calif’s Question to Laila and her Reply thereon

paras: The Calif asked Laila: “Are you the same person for whom Majnun has gone in distress and become mad? You are not more than any of the other beauties!”

Laila said: “Please keep quiet, as you are not Majnun. If you had the eyes of Majnun, you would have found this and that world as worthless. You are conscious but Majnun is unconscious. Consciousness in the path of love is bad. Whoever is conscious and awake (in the affairs of the world) is in fact, more unconscious and in sleep. His wakefulness and consciousness are worse than sleep.’’

Wakefulness is better than ignorance and lack of consciousness. An ignorant man is semiconscious; it is certainly better for him to be wakeful. This wakefulness ought to be in the affairs of God. If it is not so, such wakefulness is like that of the one confined in prison. For the whole day, a wakeful person keeps his soul engaged in useless thoughts of profit, loss and fears of decline. These engagements are neither clean, nor cleansing nor strengthening. They do not provide a path to lead the thoughts toward higher matters of mind and soul. But the man in sleep is one who is not interested in material gains and losses, but engages in higher matters of mind, develops hopes in them and discusses about them in his mind. He is better than the conscious, awake fellow.

sections.heading: When Consciousness causes Loss
paras: The wakeful and conscious fellow in worldly matters does not get overwhelmed and loses consciousness, as it happens in the case of Sufis, who enter into the state of wajd. That is; they get intoxicated by waves of unsolicited, spontaneous thoughts, which cause loss of self-control, making them go out of physical control, resulting in dancing, shouting, crying and temporary madness.
He does not get this kind of state and spiritual elation, but gets more and more of thoughts which add more and more to his confusion.

Even when he goes into sleep, he sees a devil in the form of a hoor (heavenly, beautiful maiden) and makes love with her and puts his seed of generation into her unfertile soil; and wakes up, forgetting what all he had seen through his thoughts in dream. He feels a weakness in his head and mind and dirt in his body. Fie upon his hidden marks upon his apparent marks.

sections.heading: Shadow Taken as Real
paras: A bird flies in the air and its shadow falls on the ground as if flying on the ground. A foolish hunter becomes a hunter of that shadow and runs after it, catches it and gets tired. He does not find out that he is going after a shadow, without knowing as well, the source of the shadow. He starts shooting arrows at the shadow and loses all his arrows and empties his quiver.

Similarly, the man of the worldly greed runs after the shadow, loses all arrows and wastes his life. By running after the shadow, he sets fire to all his possessions. If the shadow of God (in the form of world-discarding- saintly people) falls on him, he gets protected from the shadow of his useless thoughts, just as a baby is protected by its wet nurse.

chapters.title: Obedience to Saintly Guides
chapters.subtitle: Encouragement to Obedience to Saintly Guides Jealousy of the Minister

paras: A godly man is a shadow of God upon earth. He lives with and for God but is dead for this world. Hold on to him soon without any fear and doubt so that you may be protected from the troubles of the next life. God’s statement: “has spread the shade”.

Madda alzhilla: speaks of the existence of His friends like His shadow, who are the proof of the light of God, just as sun’s shadow is the sun’s proof as stated fully in the Quran: Alam tara ilaa Rabbika kayfa maddahz zhill! wa lauw shaa’a laja-‘a-lahu saakinan: (Have you not seen how Your Lord has spread the shade. And if He willed, He could have made it still. (Al Furqan: 25: 45).

This speaks of a very esoteric matter, difficult to comprehend. Therefore, do not enter into this valley of comprehension without a guide. Otherwise, speak out like Hazrat Ibrahim: “laa uhibbul aafiliin: I do not love things that set”. This is what Hazrat Ibrahim had said when initially, upon seeing the star, he had said: “This is my Lord: Haaza Rabbii.” When the moon appeared, he exclaimed: “This is my Lord: Haaza Rabbii”. When he saw later, the sun, he said: “This is my Lord. This is greater”. And when the sun set, he said! O my people! Lo! I am free from all that you associate (with God).”  (Surah-An’aam:6:76,77,78)

Just as by remaining in the shadow of the sun, you find out the sun, hold on to (Shams), the sun upon earth, that is, the lapel of Shams Tabrizi (Rumi’s guide) to know the esoteric aspects. He is as bright upon the earth, as sun is in the sky. If you do not find out the path toward him; you may enquire with Ziaul Huq Hisamuddin (Shams Tabrizi’s disciple, and beneficiary from Rumi, upon whose suggestion this Math(s)navi was written).

sections.heading: Jealously, an Obstacle for Success
paras: If jealously catches hold of you (in proceeding toward them), know, that it is from Iblis (Satan) who is the master of it. He felt himself ashamed of Adam’s elevation, in spite of Adam being made of clay, and himself made of fire, fire being superior. This made him jealous of Adam considered inferior, but elevated to higher position by God. That is to say, he carried on an unnecessary battle against the good fortune of Adam, which is the main feature of jealousy. In the path of seeking guidance from the noble, saintly gnostics, jealousy for them is a narrow-hard-to-cross path as they are humble and poor in appearance, having discarded worldly attainments. Many people do not go to them out of jealously. That man is very fortunate who does not have the feelings of jealousy. Think over that our body is a house of jealousy. The entire family of this body gets the impacts of jealousy. Mind, limbs, eyes, ears, mouth — all participate in jealousy.

sections.heading: Jealousy Destroys Nations
paras: Jealousy destroys houses, families and countries. Royals, nobles, great and wise who are brave and respectable, like falcons among birds which hunt birds in the sky, become mean and disgraceful like crows, which live upon filth and rotten flesh of dead animals. Though jealousy starts from the heart and pollutes the body, body can still be protected and kept clean of arrogance, ill will and pretention, with the help of God, as body has the potential to keep itself clean, as many a times, victims of jealousy of others do not suffer, and the jealous always suffer, of their own. When God said to Hazrat Ibrahim: “Purify My house: Tahhir baitia”: (Hajj: 22: 26) referring to the Ka‘abuthllah, there is a great stress for cleaning. This was a house made of mud, but it was a treasury of light. It was like the strange, frightening model of a creature (Talisman) kept on treasuries to cause fright. Cleaning it also means removal of these frightening objects from it, and also of the dirt of other vicious feelings from the hearts of men which include jealousy, since heart is also a place of God. If you develop treachery and jealousy for a clean-hearted person, it will recoil upon you and blacken your heart. Become the dust of the feet of the people of God and put it on the head of the feelings of jealousy, just as I have done.

The Minister of the king became a lowly, mean fellow out of his jealousy and to meet its ends, he got his ears and nose despoiled unrightly, on the hope that, with the sting of his jealousy, his poison may reach the lives of the oppressed Christians.

Whoever gets his nose cut off out of jealousy, becomes the loser of his nose and ears and loses the capacity to hear. Nose is an organ which feels the smell to go to his destined street. It is its smelling capacity that is of value and not the nose itself. One who cannot smell the smell of truth is a noseless fellow. And smell is that which takes to the righteous path of religion. One who smells and offers no thanks to God for this grant is a rejecter of grant as if, he destroyed its worth. Be thankful and become obedient to the grateful ones. Become totally devoted to them and live only for them and forget your own affairs before them as if, you are not alive, or you are dead. Do not commit dacoity like the minister and do not prevent others from offering their worship.

chapters.title: Wise Christians find out Treacheries
chapters.subtitle: Realization of the minister’s treachery by the wisemen of the Christians

paras: That infidel minister became a religious preacher and mixed garlic in the sweets with his tricks. Those with a taste of understanding used to feel both pleasure and bitterness in his talk. He used to speak of points mixed up with lies and truth like mixing poison in gulqand (rose with sugar). Therefore, it was necessary for the people not to fall into the treacheries of his good talk as underneath each statement, there were a hundred vices.
