paras: Man is nothing but seeing (observing), and his material body is nothing but skin and flesh. And seeing is, in fact, nothing but seeing the friend (God). If one cannot see one’s friend, it is better for one to go blind. And similarly, a lovable person who does not last long, is better, if he is far away.”

When the Roman ambassador heard of these entirely new points, he got all the more anxious to see Hazrat ‘Umar. He went in search of him after leaving his horse and luggage there itself. He was searching for him everywhere in extreme anxiety and excitement thinking, can there be such a man also in the world, who is so hidden, as the soul is. His desire increased moment by moment, so that he might become his bondsman. Certainly, one who searches, at last meets his object.

chapters.title: Greatest ruler of the time sleeping on grass
chapters.subtitle: The Roman Ambassador Finds Hazrat ‘Umar Sleeping Under A Date Palm

paras: A bedouin lady looked at this stranger and made enquiries and said that: “Hazrat ‘Umar was sleeping under a date palm, away from all creations. You may go and see the shadow of God sleeping under the shadow of God”. He went nearby and stood at a distance, looked at Hazrat ‘Umar and started shivering. The sight of that sleeping man created fright in the ambassador and also at the same time a feeling of pleasure.

sections.heading: Love and Fear Together are Rare
paras: Love and fear are the opposites of each other, but he found these two within himself. He started telling himself: “I have seen kings and I have been composed and joyous. There has never been any fear and fright before them, but this man has made me nervous and frightened. I have gone into the bushes of lions and jaguars, but those places did not cause any fear in me. I have participated in so many battles like a lion howsoever dangerous the situations were. I have caused many injuries to others and got myself injured, but here, what I see is that every part of my body trembles. What has happened to me? Definitely this fright in me is caused by God and not by man. This is certainly not caused by this man in shabby clothes. Whoever fears God and remains pious can cause fright in the hearts of men and jinn’s.

For an hour he stood thus with due respect with folded hands, Then Hazrat ‘Umar woke up and sat. He offered his respects and salutations. The Prophet has said: First there should be salutations and then other talks”. Hazrat ‘Umar responded with his blessings and called him before him, made him sit beside and consoled him. Whoever fears God remains in peace and in turn gives consolations to those in fear. The food for those in fear is “do not fear: Laatakhaf”; and this cannot be said to one, who has no fear. He does not need any advice or lesson from you. Thus, Hazrat ‘Umar removed the feelings of fear from him and got him delighted.

chapters.title: H. ‘Umar’s Elimination of Doubts
chapters.subtitle: Hazrat ‘Umar’s Talks to The Ambassador and His Questions. [Read the following very carefully and more times as it contains very esoteric matters. Read 3 to 4 times and digest the message – Translator]

sections.heading: Maqaam (State) and Haal (situation)
paras: After this, Hazrat ‘Umar talked to him on very subtle matters of the attributes of God, Who is the best of the companions; about the graces of God upon His friends, so that they may know the facts of their state (Maqaam) and that special situations (Haal), by following the instructions, first by obedience to the apparent commands of do’s and don’ts of Shariat, and performance of regular prayers. He said: esoteric “situations” are like the exhibition of the beauty of brides, and “state” (Maqaam) is like living in her company. Her decorations and beauty are things that everyone can see, and even slaves can see. This is special situation (Haal). But other than the groom none can go nearby to the bride and he remains alone with her (Maqaam). Those in Haal (special situation) are like the general observers of the beauty, who are all in common, but those who are closeby to her are the ones in the state (Maqaam). There are many people of Haal (special situations) among the sufis and those of state (Maqaam) are very few. The situations of the sufis of Haal become known to the people at large; but the sufis of state (Maqam) remain hidden from them.

sections.heading: Original Place of Soul
paras: Then, Hazrat ‘Umar spoke to him of the various mid-stations of the heart in its journey. There was a time upon it, when it was free from the prison of time in the form of pure grandeur and domination. It was lonely there, and from there it came into the world of matter, got mixed up with it and became one of the world of nasoot (Material world). This is the world of creation and time, where they both, time and creation (space) go together. Before entering into the material world, it was in extremely carefree and happy conditions and in flight. Each of its flight was larger than the expanse between many horizons. It was far away from hopes, desires and ambitions. That was the state of purity and dominion of God, from where come all things – material, moral, spiritual, commands, control and administration of the universe.

Hazrat ‘Umar found this stranger in an accommodative mind ready to know the secrets. Hazrat ‘Umar was a perfect master; and the seeker of knowledge was enthusiastic to learn. The rider was smart and the thing to ride upon was ready. The master found that the pupil has the capacity to learn. He sowed the clean seeds in a clean land.

sections.heading: Soul’s Coming Down on Earth
paras: The stranger asked: ‘O, leader of the Muslims, why did the soul come down from the elevated heavenly world to the lowly earth. How these uncountable birds came about in a simple cage? He said:” God issued the spell of “kun” (Be) upon it, and “narrated the means of becoming. Those non-existents that have no eyes and ears became active and vigorous upon the recitation of this spell. The non-existents swiftly sprang forward and leapt into existence with great pleasure into the space (as in bigbang?).

“After this, He cast another spell upon the existents, which had come into existence earlier, which spell was sent in a fast manner just as two horses are used by a traveler to reach the destination early. He cast a spell on the nonliving body when it became a living being. He told the sun to become bright and it did so. Again, He cast another spell in its ear which frightened it so much that a hundred eclipses came about on its face (sunspots?).

“He said something in the ears of the flower which made it laugh and bloom. He said some pleasurable words to the ruby, and it became happy and bright. We do not know what he said in the ears of earth, that it was silent and waiting (for some things like wind and water to activate it). It is not known what he said to the clouds that they spilled water as the tears of their eyes collected in heavy loads as if from the goatskin.”

sections.heading: Creation of intelligence
paras: When a man is confused as to what decision he should take, God considers him as blind so as to be in two equally weighty objectives to this or the opposite of it. Then guidance comes to him from God and he gets inclined towards one side and he adopts that one and gets rid of the confused state. If you do not want to be caught in the ‘to do or not to do’ situation, do not plug cotton in the ears of the soul to avoid proper direction from God. Remove the cotton of insinuations from the ear of soul, so that the voice from the heavens may come to your ears. This will help you to get rid of the riddles and be in a position to understand the clear statements and the points that are told in symbolic ways and hints.

sections.heading: What Is Inspiration
paras: Thereafter, the ears of the soul became the places capable of receiving inspirations. What is inspiration? It is the speech of the hidden senses. Ears and eyes of the soul are different from the ears and eyes of senses (physical eyes and ears). Ears of wisdom and eyes of speculation also do not possess it. (Inspirations are the speech of the inner, hidden senses as distinct from the normal physical senses of hearing and seeing which exist all the time, except during sleep and unconsciousness which are related to the body or brain.) Seeing and hearing of certain things by the soul are entirely different from those by physical senses. So also, those of wisdom and intellect. (Interpretations)

sections.heading: Impacts of Inspirations
paras: So long as I was confined to intellectual understanding, the doctrine of fate and predestination was quite satisfying and I was contented, but when I received inspirational knowledge from inner senses, my contentment was lost, and it caused disturbances in my soul and took me to the field of love of God. Love replaced wisdom and intellect. One who has no love continues to be in the zone of fate and predestination. One in love goes beyond the zones of fate and predestination. That is, he becomes free and holder of his own fate. Then comes the connection with God, and not with fate and predestination. And love with God goes on increasing and the connection also increases, and the prayers offered to God come from love and not as matters of obedience to his commands. This worship is bright like the moon and not semi-bright or dark like the clouds. Even if it is considered as fate, it is no fate as understood by common men. Nor is it of the mischievous commanding of self. It is voluntary, total submission to God and merger of himself into God and loss of free will.

sections.heading: Fate and Free Will
paras: Fate is understood only by those, the eyes of whose heart are opened by God. Hidden events to occur in future are clearly presented before them; and consideration of the past is not at all of any importance for them.

Free will (their own authority to act as against fate) and predestination of the inspired people are entirely of a different type. They are like the drops in the oysters. Other people are like small or big drops. The inspired are drops in the oysters as both small and big pearls. The navels of other people contain only blood, but the blood in their navel becomes musk. Do not call them only as copper, as when it enters into their alchemic heart it becomes gold. Free will and predestination were only thoughts in the mind, but when they entered into the inspired, they became the light of the Majesty of God.

Bread kept on the dining sheet is only a lifeless material, but upon entering into the body it becomes a happy-active-soul. Upon the dining sheet it sees no change, but when impacted by the digestive system, which is like the water from the fountain of paradise (salsabiil), it gets changed into soul. This is the power of the animal soul, which acts similarly in other animals also.

sections.heading: Soul of the Soul
paras: In the matter of possession of animal soul, man is similar to animals. But man has another soul – the human soul, which is the soul of the animal soul. [The soul referred to earlier which receives inspiration and acts under its impacts is the human soul, which is the soul of the animal soul. Great impacts and values referred to in previous lines relate to this human soul. Only humans possess double soul – animal soul and human soul and it is human soul which attains high spiritual levels. Details of this matter can be found in chapter 1 of volume III of Ihya-ul-ullum: wonders of the heart by Hazrat Imam Ghazali. You must read, read and read and meditate to understand this.—Translator]

Bread is the food of the body. This should make you think as to what the food of the soul would be. Man, who is made of flesh, survives with the power of life; and in this flesh are included his physical heart and brain. With the combined power of these powers of flesh and life, he has the power to tear off the oceans, mountains and mines. The might of the soul of Farhaad, the hill breaker, (for the sake of his beloved, Shireen), tore off the hill. The might of the soul of the soul can be seen in the tearing off of the moon, as was done by Prophet Muhammad. If the heart opens the mouth of the bag of secrets, the soul will attempt to run towards the throne of God, which would create turmoil in the minds of the common people, which would, in turn, create turmoil in the world. If my tongue also reveals this secret, it will start fire and burn out the world.

chapters.title: Acceptance of guilt by H. Adam
chapters.subtitle: Hazrat Adam’s attribution of wrong as his own saying “O lord! We have wronged our own souls: Rabbanaa zhalamna anfuasa (A‘raaf 7:23), And of Iblis saying to God: O My lord! Because you have put me on the wrong: rabbi bimaa aghwaitini! (Al-Hijr 15:39)

sections.heading: Difference Between Meanings and Words
paras: Look at both the acts of God and our own acts. Our act is right before us. It is quite clear. If the act of man is not before us, we cannot tell to anyone as to why he did so. We cannot hold him responsible at all. But the originator and creator of our acts is God only. Therefore, our acts are the creation of God. Yet there is a difference. That our act is within our control or because of our own free will; and its reward is sometimes helpful to us like a friend, or inimical to us like a snake. Man is bound by circumstances and circumstances are not in his power. A speaker of words, either considers the words or their objectives. There are different circumstances. He cannot dominate over both of them at the same time. If he is attentive to the circumstances, he will be away from words. He cannot look at the front and back at the same time. When you are looking at the front, you cannot look at the back. When soul cannot encompass the words and connotations together, how can it be the originator of both? Know that, God encompasses everything. He is not prevented from doing an act while doing another. (He can do both acts together and many acts together). While doing an act He does not remain inattentive to other things. God has enthralled our souls. He cannot remain unaware of what He has created.

sections.heading: Shelter Behind Fate
paras: Satan was asked as to why he did not prostrate to Hazrat Adam along with other angels. He first boasted of his superiority as born out of fire, when Hazrat Adam was made out of mud; fire being superior to mud. And then he said to God: I did so, because you have put me on the wrong; bima aghawaitini (surah al Hijr;15;39), thus speaking of predestination. Everything is done by God Himself. Thus, he refused to own his mistake behind the shelter of predestination.

sections.heading: Shelter Behind Free will
paras: But on the contrary, when Hazrat Adam was asked as to why he went to the forbidden tree, he took the mistake of his disobedience upon himself saying: Our lord! We have wronged our own souls; Rabbanaa zhalamnaa anfusanaa (Surah A’raaf 7:23). That is: he took the act as one of free will. He was well aware of the subtle difference between free will and predestination, unlike us. He took the responsibility of the wrong upon himself as a token of respect and honour for God; and by doing so he had a great harvest of benefits. After his repentance, God asked Hazrat Adam whether He had not created hardship and inclinations towards offences in him. And whether his disobedience was not a matter of fate and predestination; and if that was true, why he does not speak of it. Hazrat Adam said: “I feared. I did not give up the respect for Your Lordship.” God said: “Yes, I too maintain a regard for You.”

One who honours, receives honour. One who presents sugar gets other sweets. Pure things are for the pure people. Keep your friend happy and do not make him unhappy. The Quran says: Alkhabiisatu lilkhabiisiina, wa alkhabiisuna lilkhabiisati; wal taiyyibattu lit tayyibiina, wa altayyibuna liltayyibaati: Women impure are for men impure and men impure are for women impure. And women of purity for men of purity, and men of purity for women of purity. (Noor: 24:27)

O my Heart! Cite an illustration to clearly understand the difference between predestination and free will. A hand shivers of its own, due to disease and you shake your hand voluntarily. Both these movements are caused by God, but both cannot be considered as one. The former is a result of predestination (sickness), and the latter of free will. You feel concerned with your voluntary shaking, but a sick man does not feel so. You cannot see a sick person regret about its impacts upon others, as he knows that he has no role in its being done. It is predestination for him. You should not make yourself as one holding on to this kind of predestination (of helplessness).

sections.heading: Rational and Spiritual Conclusions
paras: This is a rational argument, but reasoning is not always on the right side. It can lead to wrong conclusions also. It is only the weak (minded) who resort to it. It may be as precious as pearls and coral, but the spiritual interpretation and understanding are entirely different. The state of the spiritual interpretation is different, and so also the composition of its wine.

So long as there was an intelligential interpretation, there was no difference between H. ‘Umar Bin Khattab (Later calif ‘Umar) and ‘Umar Bin Hasham (Abu Jahl) the staunchest enemy of H Mohammed, who was later killed in the battle of Badr. Whereas ‘Umar bin Khattab came towards the spiritual interpretation, his counterpart, ‘Umar Bin Hasham became Abu Jahl (father of ignorance). From the point of view of wisdom and senses, he was perfect, but from spiritual point of view, he was ignorant.

Consider the sensual and intelligential arguments as the causes or impacts of conclusions. Intelligential interpretations are like the conclusion of the existence of fire upon seeing smoke. This is observational conclusion. And also, of the existence of cause when an effect is seen. This is a mental process.

The spiritual conclusions are strange in realization, and stranger in their impacts. When the searcher of spiritual light receives its light, its cause and effect get mingled up and cannot be differentiated. There will neither be cause and effect nor the denier and seeker. All get mixed up resulting in a light that needs no space to pass through and which cannot be blocked by any opaque body. It is a strange light, which only its recipient can see, and he does not need any supporter or guide just as a man with bright eyes is not in need of a stick to support or another man’s hand to help him to walk.

chapters.title: God is with you Everywhere
chapters.subtitle: Exegesis of “He is with you wheresoever you may be”: wa huwa ma‘akumu ainama kuntumu (Hadid: 57:4)

paras: Once again, we shall revert to the earlier narrative. Rather, where had we gone out of it? The narration of predestination and free will has been holding us. Let us see some more of it. If we are in ignorance, we may have to consider it as a prison made by God. At no time, we are away or separate from Him. And if we attain knowledge, it should be considered as a large palace with His court. In our sleep, we are lost in Him and when awake, we are engaged in the narration of His activities. When we cry, we are like the clouds full of clear water that is about to rain; and while laughing, we are like the lightnings of the clouds. When we are in anger and fights, we are like the reflections of His wrath; and when we are in peace and seeking excuses, we are the reflections of His mercy and benevolence. We are like the letter ‘alif’ in this world of turns and twists, which does not possess any dot or curve at all.

If you become like ‘alif’ possessing nothing, you will become a unique person in this confusing path. Try to keep away everything other than God from you and set apart this destructible world. There is no end to this talk my son; come let us talk about the matters relating to the Roman ambassador.

chapters.title: Why souls Imprisoned in Bodies
chapters.subtitle: The Ambassador’s questioning with Hazrat ‘Umar about the reasons for involving the souls in the body of mud and water

paras: When the Roman Ambassador heard about these things from H ‘Umar, a new light kindled in his heart. Many questions and doubts went out of his mind and he understood that the occurrence of everything is due to the command word: ’kun’. He had no more doubts about the concern for right and wrong. He stuck onto the fundamentals and ignored the branches and started putting some questions to H ‘Umar.

He enquired with H ‘Umar: “What was the secret and wisdom behind imprisoning the pure, holy, subtle, immaterial soul in the polluted mud. Clean water is hidden in mud, and clean soul got muddled with body. Please tell me as to what was the secret behind it? What is the good of imprisoning the bird in the cage”?

sections.heading: Air becomes Words and Meaning
paras: H ‘Umar said: “You have started a strange debate. You are trying to imprison the meanings in words. Not only that you have imprisoned the free going meanings in words, but you have even bound the air in words. Free air that is given the dress of sound (voice) is imprisoned in words and this has great benefits for man. You get the benefits of this act of converting air into words, yet you are unaware of all the benefits. It is God who is the creator of all these benefits, without whose benevolence, there would be no benefits. When we are aware of so many benefits, God is aware of all the benefits. By imprisoning soul in the body there are hundreds of thousands of benefits and again hundreds of thousands of benefits in each of these benefits. The blow of air as a breath resulting in voice in the form of the words which you bring out of your mouth, which is like the word ‘kun’ (Be) by God, is the soul of all souls. When your words have meanings and results, how can this word ‘kun’ be without meanings and results? Think over.

Your speech is a petty part of a part of the entirety of speech. When it performs such great acts as you see in everyone and everywhere and every time, think over, how cannot the entirety of speech remain without causing impacts and imparting benefits? Your speech apart, you are a petty part of a part, and your work causes such impacts and benefits, then, why do you embolden yourself in passing remarks on the entirety and the Whole, who is the Creator of everything. You should not talk when your talking is of no use. And if you feel it is useful, you should give up meaningless remarks and be thankful for the gains. You put a question to me and got the answer. My answer was your object, when you put the question. If you find my answer to be beneficial, which is in the form of words, you may see meanings in the words of God. There is no harm even in putting a question which gives no benefits. But it is wrong in putting even a beneficial question, if it is not to elicit answer but as a punning remark. There should be thankfulness to men who help, and to God, with humiliation as a man with a yoke around his neck would do, and not with sour and quarrelsome face. If a sour face is considered as a symbol of thanksgiving, there cannot be a more thankful thing than vinegar. However sometimes, sourness also helps in dealing with some circumstances. In such a case it should be mixed with sugar, as vinegar is mixed with sugar to make the medicine of sikanjabin to treat certain ailments of the liver.
Explaining all these things through poetical verses cannot be done without creating confusions, as it is not possible always to hit the stones accurately on the object.

chapters.title: Name and Fame are Chains
chapters.subtitle: To Explain the Hadith(s): “One who desires to sit with God, should sit with men of tasawwuf”

paras: After reaching at this level of learning, the Roman ambassador, became a king of knowledge, and devoted to the authority and might of God. He was out of control with one or two cups of the wine of knowledge of God; and he completely forgot his ambassadorial duties. When flood comes into the rivers, it becomes a sea; and when seed enters into the farmland, it becomes a plant. But when the flood entered into the sea, it got annihilated; and clouds changed into sunlight when hit with the sword of the sun. When bread developed connections with Adam, it got converted into life, lively and well informed. When wax and dry wood sacrificed themselves upon fire, they became bright light in the darkness of the night. When antimony entered into the eyes, from a stone it became eyebright and protector of the eyes.

sections.heading: Lessons from prophets and saints
paras: One who got out of his self, got connected with a living saintly man. Alas, for the one who became a companion of a dead-hearted man and himself became dead and lost even his later life. When you do not get a perfect saint, you should enter into the protection of the Quran, in which ease, you sit along with the souls of prophets. There are narrations of the life and situations of the prophets in the Quran, who are the fishes in the clean water of the great Lord. Even if, you are only a reader but not the follower of the Quran, you will get the opportunity of seeing the prophets and saints and getting influenced by them as their souls are free from the influences of the materials. If you read and act according to the Quran, from the lessons of the life and activities of prophets, your soul will feel the narrowness of the body in which it is held, as if in a cage. It will be foolish if a bird which is imprisoned in the cage does not think of getting released from it.

sections.heading: Fame and Publicity: A Chain to Feet
paras: Such of the souls that are released from the cages are of the prophets and they are disciplined guides. They will be telling you from the elevated world of spirits about the ways of escape from the cage, and also that they have been released from the cages only through these ways and there is no other way of escape. The way is: make yourself humble and weak, so that you may avoid publicity, as becoming famous is a strong chain, which prevents you from going forward. In this connection, you may hear a narrative, so that you may know of the helpful wind in your journey on the ocean. Hear this narrative as an illustration so that you may learn the means of understanding of the inner secrets through the apparent clear things.

chapters.title: Message sent by Caged Parrot to Free Parrots
chapters.subtitle: Journey of a merchant to India for Trade and sending of a message by his Parrot to the Parrots of India

paras: There was a merchant who had a parrot, which was very beautiful and imprisoned in a cage. After making arrangement for his journey towards India, he asked every one of his slaves and maids as to what he should bring for them as gifts. Everyone expressed a desire for something, and he promised each of them. He asked the parrot about its gift to be brought from India.

sections.heading: Pang’s of separation from friends
paras: The Parrot said: “When you see the parrots there, tell them about me that I am anxious to see them, but as per the decision of heaven, I am in a prison. It has sent its salutations to you and seeks justice from you and guidance and methods from you”. It continued: “Is it good that I should give up my life here itself or slowly die in my anxiety to be with you? Will it be alright for me to remain in this hardship of prison while you are enjoying life in greenery and upon the trees? O my friends, is it just that I should remain in prison and you should be in gardens? O my friends, please remember this desolated bird also in your green fields in some mornings. Do remember our days of friendship and love. Do think of the rights of friends and companions. Thinking about the friends gives great relief particularly when it is full of love, as between Laila and Majnun. O my friends, you are having fine drinks along with your beautiful friends, while I am drinking the cups of my own blood. Drink a cup of wine in my remembrance too, if you feel like doing some justice in my case. Or, if you cannot do so, you may spill a mouthful on the ground in the remembrance of a far-off friend who is eating dust in a dry land full of dust. Oh! What a tragedy? What happened to those promises and swearings to maintain relations?  What happened to the promises that came from your sugary lips?”

sections.heading: Separation from God
paras: If the separation of the servant is due to his negligence, why do you also be bad with him, as he has been bad with you? What difference will be between your act and of the servant? O God, the sound that comes out of Your anger and attack is much pleasing than the melodies of musical instruments. The punishments imposed by You are much better than the wealth of the world, and Your revenge is lovelier than my life. When the fire of Your anger itself is so pleasing, I wonder to know how joyous and pleasing Your light may be. When the sweetness of Your oppression is so pleasing, who can penetrate into the depths of Your subtleties and purity? It is difficult to see the benevolence of Your oppression. If it gets revealed, one who is crying in grief will burst into laughter. It is well known that the troubles that a faithful man gets, are actually an expiation to release him from greater difficulties. I cry out of fear so that He may look into my sincerity and take pity on me and reduce my troubles.

sections.heading: Love for Opposites
paras: I am in love with both His mercy and wrath and I myself wonder how I love both the opposites at the same time. I feel that my love is not for His mercy and wrath, but for God Himself from whom both these opposites originate. It is impossible to remain without love for the originator of both these qualities. I am afraid, if I go away from these thorny bushes and enter into a pleasing garden of flowers, I shall then also cry like the bulbul. The bulbuls are wonderful birds that they keep their mouth open to swallow the garden of flowers along with thorns. But my case is not like the one of bulbul, but of a fiery crocodile for which all unpalatable things are palatable and pleasing. Both good and bad from the beloved are pleasing for a true lover. When I have committed myself to God, I should be like Him to love everything, good and bad, as He is all in all and the whole. He is in love with Himself and He Himself is love.

chapters.title: Different branches of Wisdom
chapters.subtitle: Quality of the Birds with wings of the Wisdom of God

paras: [In Surah Fatir, 35:1 ‘With wings’ is specifically referred to as a specialty of angels with two, three and four wings. Angels are generally considered as creatures with physical features with spatial qualities: Abdulla Yusuf Ali says: “the grosser ideas which men have of angels must be dismissed from our minds. They are beings expressive of qualities or powers which may be typified as wings. We need not suppose that angelic wings have muscles and features like the wings of birds: (page 1152, The Holy Quran). Rumi’s reference here as ‘Birds with Wings’ in reference to the ‘Wisdom of God’ is very significant. Man’s wisdom also requires to be taken as angelic qualities in him. —Translator]

Matters relating to the birds of the soul are similar. There is nobody who is deprived of these birds. There are souls which are humble and sinless but are as mighty as Hazrat Sulaiman with his armies. (H Sulaiman had the armies of men, jinns and birds).

When such a soul, inspite of its weakness on one part and might on the other, cries without any complaints but thanks, there occurs a great turmoil in all the seven heavens. God sends a hundred messages and messengers all the time; when he says ‘My lord’ once, God says sixty times. ‘I respond to you’.

sections.heading: Apparent Straying’s of Saints
paras: A person with such soul is better placed in his wrong commitments than in his obediences. Apparent statements of infidelity from him are fresh dealings before which faithfulness becomes out of date. [As happened in the case of H. Bayazid Bistami who said: “Subhaani Ma A’zam shaani” I am glorious and clean. How great is my splendor?]. Every one took it as a claim of infidelity that he is claiming parity with God, Who alone is glorious. Such a state is not permanent]. Such a person has an ascension every moment, and every moment he goes high and higher in realization. God keeps a crown upon a crown that he has already worn.

sections.heading: Laamakaan explained
paras: His body is on the earth, but his soul is in the Laamakaan, which is a place beyond space and time, which is immutable, from which all things including space-time and the contents therein come about. That is the highest level to which any soul can go. This is a world of spirits including the spirit of God. This place is beyond the comprehension of anybody, which, even people of very high learning cannot comprehend because the comprehension about it is spiritual and not intellectual, and that too as a special favor from God.

Space and all the things in it (Makaan) and the zone beyond it (Laamakaan) are under the command of God just as the four streams of paradise namely of water, honey, milk and wine are. These streams are also not spatial and material but holy, subtle and spiritual, which are also incomprehensible through intelligence.

Now, you may shorten the explanation about this matter and divert your attention from this. No more talks of it, as God alone knows all. Therefore, my friends, I return from here to the narrative of the parrot and the merchant on the way to India.

chapters.title: Message Passed On
chapters.subtitle: The Merchant’s Observing Parrots in A Forest and Passing on The Message

paras: The merchant took the message given by his parrot, promising to pass it on to the Indian parrots. When he entered into the boundaries of India, he saw a few parrots in the forest. He halted his carrier and called them out and passed on his parrot’s salutation and message. One of the parrots shivered, fell down and lost its live.

sections.heading: Mischiefs of The Tongue
paras: The merchant felt sorry for passing on the message and said to himself: “I became the cause of the death of this animal. Perhaps this parrot is the relative of my parrot. Perhaps they have one soul in two bodies. What a wrong I have done? Why did I give this message? With this nonsense, I burnt an innocent life. Our tongue is like a stone, and the mouth is like iron. Whatever that comes out of the tongue is nothing but fire. Do not strike stone with iron unnecessarily, not even as an imitation, and for fun and fame; because there is darkness all around with lots of cotton. Any spark coming out of this striking cannot be prevented by cotton”.

Those communities are cruel which have stitched their eyes and set fire to the world with their words. One statement is enough to destroy the world. It can convert dead foxes into lions. This includes those scholars without hearts, who speak of the secrets to boast of their learning, before senseless people resulting in mischief. And also those mischievous, who like foxes, speak of the intricate aspects of religion and misguide ignorant masses, who start roaring like lions out of the pleasure of their misunderstood claims.

sections.heading: Souls Are All Alike To Start With
paras: Souls, by their very nature are capable of giving life to the dead with their blow of breaths as H.’Ia did. At one time they can cause injury and at another time apply the balm to cure. If the curtains are lifted from the souls, every soul can be like that of H. Ia. The human body is a curtain for the soul. It is a very sweet thing like sugar to talk about these matters, yet it is better that one should have self-control and avoid the craze to reveal all these matters, which also gives great sweetness to the speaker’s soul. Wise people use their wisdom to have patience on all these desires, and immature people speak out of all this, and enjoy the talk like children enjoying sweets. One who maintains patience gets elevated to zones above the heavens and one who enjoys the sweetness of talking returns to the place, from where he rose up.

chapters.title: Hands of the competent
chapters.subtitle: Explanation of The Statement of Shaikh Fariddudin Attaar, May His Secrets Be Clean

paras: “You are a man of senses, O wise man. You drink blood from out of dust; But if a man of heart (soul) drinks poison, it becomes honey”

sections.heading: Competent Hands: Loved by God
paras: A man of heart does not meet with any loss, even if he eats clearly visible poison, for the reason that he is no more sickly and has attained full health without any need for regimen. But other than him, say a student, is still under trial, and helpless, and he requires to be under regimen. The noble Prophet has said: “O seeker of knowledge, do not ever claim parity with the perfect guide”. It is also attributed to the Prophet having said: “If you do not want to undergo loss, never disagree with the master”.

Do not enter into fire, if you are like Nimrod who created fire for H. Ibrahim and took it lightly after seeing that it has not caused harm to H. Ibrahim. Before trying to enter into fire, first become one like H. Ibrahim. Do not jump into the river if you do not know swimming, simply on the assumption that you know swimming. One, who dives into the sea with his expertise, brings forth pearls from its depths. He protects himself from any loss; rather gains profits. A perfect man can convert dust into gold. But an incompetent fellow converts gold into dust. The hands of the incompetents are the hands of satans and ghosts, (as both of them are nonphysical entities). By mistaking them as real, which itself is a misunderstanding, one will be a victim of cheating and fraud.

But a truthful, competent person becomes a loved one of God. His hands are like the hands of God in the performance of any act. When the darkness of ignorance comes before him, it becomes the brightness of wisdom; and on the contrary, when knowledge goes into the possessions of the imperfect, it becomes worthless and injurious. Whatever food a sick man takes, becomes sickly. Even if a perfect man resorts to infidelity, it becomes a useful thing like a pious religious act. O soldier of the infantry (foot soldier) do not go to fight with a horseman. Be careful and take a back step so that you may not get your head broken.

chapters.title: Honoring: Precondition for Progress
chapters.subtitle: Honoring of the Magicians to H. Musa by Asking Him to Put His Staff First

paras: Magicians, during the reign of Pharaoh came before H.Musa with pride to contest against him. Yet they considered him to be honorable and gave preference to him by considering him to be a man of commanding status and asked him to put his staff on the ground first, if he so liked. But H. Musa said: ‘No, O magicians, you may do so first and show your skill and craftiness’.

This much of honor they showed to him was very much, that they accepted the authority of H. Musa and got deliverance. But, for their having competed with him, they got their hands and feet severed. They got honored for recognizing H. Musa’s great status but lost their hands and feet for yet competing with him inspite of knowing his great status.

sections.heading: Hearing: A Precondition for Talking
paras: Eating anything of his choice or taking any wisdom from any source is permissible for a perfect man. But, as you are not perfect, do not eat like him and avoid listening to others than your master. You are like the ear; your master is like the tongue. Both of you are not alike. Saying is for the master and hearing in silence is for you. God has given command to the ears to hear and to remain silent while hearing the Quran: wa izaa quri’al Quranu fastimi’u Lahu wa ansitu: when the Quran is read, listen to it with attention, and pay heed: (A’raaf: 7:204).

So long as a child is on milk, it remains silent for a long time and hears everything as though his entire body has become an ear. He keeps his lips stitched and resorts to learning from the speakers. Until he does not learn in full, he does not say even one of the learned things. And if he talks, it is all nonsense. If he has no ears, (by birth) he only babbles, and remains dumb for his whole life. A fellow born deaf, who never hears any sound, remains dumb and never even tries to talk. All this is for the reason that hearing is necessary before talking. The path to talking is through the ear. You should do everything according to its technique. You should enter the house through the door. You should seek your provisions for life through the required means.

sections.heading: God Alone Talks without Hearing
paras: The talking which is not through the ears (before hearing), is none other than the one of God, who is independent of everything. He is the originator and needs no teacher. He is the provider of all and is not in need of any provision for Himself. All others engaged in some hard work and in talk are dependent upon some teacher and are in need of something as a model.

sections.heading: How to Learn Without Teacher
paras: If you are not aware of all these points, go into some ruined place, put on the woolen garment of the dervishes and resort to crying and weeping, as this method also provides certain things. You may see that H. Adam got rid of his punishment by shedding tears. Tears are very effective relievers for the repenters. It is to shed tears that H. Adam came upon the earth, to weep, cry and mourn. If H. Adam came down from paradise and the seven heavens in order to stand on one leg first just as the trainees of the saintly people are made to do near the place of footwear as a punishment for committing mistakes.

sections.heading: Follow Your Father’s Steps
paras: If you believe that you are from the back and waist of physical H. Adam, and you are, as such like him, and also about his spiritual gifts and his acts of honor to God, be like him along with others, (other groups of men). Prepare your tasty food with the fire of the heart and water of the eyes and keep yourself fresh just as the garden keeps itself with the heat of the sun and the water from the clouds. You are with a heart, very fragile like glass. You do not have taste to know the worth of water of the tears of the eyes. You have entangled your feet in slush like the donkeys; and you are pouncing upon bread to eat as though you saw bread for the first time; and are ever busy in eating and filling your belly. If you empty your belly of bread, you can fill it up with gems of the light of God. Keep the baby of your soul away from the devil’s milk and then make it a companion of angels. So long as you are in darkness, unhappy and disturbed, you may think that you are like the co-drinkers of milk along with the devil.

sections.heading: Eat Food from Legitimate Means
paras: The morsel of food that increases the light of the soul and capacity to achieve perfectness comes by carrying on permissible professions. Consider that oil as water that puts out your lamp immediately upon its being poured into the bowl of the lamp. The morsel of food obtained from permissible means increases knowledge and intelligence. Love and softness of heart come with a morsel from permissible means. You may consider that morsel to be from illegitimate means, which increases jealousy, treachery, arrogance and recklessness. You do not see maize seedlings sprouting from seeds of wheat; nor you see a mare giving birth to a baby donkey. The morsel of food that you eat is the seed of which, thoughts are its fruits. Morsel is like an ocean and thoughts are like the pearls. A permissible morsel put into the mouth increases the inclination towards worship and strengthens the will to go toward the next world of life after death. It creates attentiveness in your heart and light in your eyes. There is no end to this talk, O great man! Continue the narrative of the parrot and the merchant.

chapters.title: Merchant’s report: Subtleties and intricacies of Love
chapters.subtitle: Narration by the Merchant to His Parrot about What He Saw In India

paras: The merchant completed his business and returned to his place with great pleasure. He had brought gifts for all slaves and granted some mementoes to each of the maids. The parrot asked him as to where was its gifts and asked him to speak about what all he saw and heard. The merchant said: “What can I say? I feel ashamed. I am biting my own hands and chewing my fingers, as to why I carried that message full of nonsense with my own lack of wisdom and with wrongs”.
The parrot asked him; “O master, what did you feel ashamed of? What was the matter that was the cause of your sorrow and remorse?”

sections.heading: Tongue: Cause of Troubles
paras: He said: “I spoke of your lamentation to a flock of parrots. One of them felt so much pain that its gall bladder burst; it shivered, fell down and died. I felt ashamed as to whether your lamentations were worth telling about, but what was the good of feeling ashamed after telling it? Consider the statement made by your tongue as an arrow shot out from the bow. That arrow will not come back. A flood has to be avoided before it comes. When its water passes above the head, it spreads all over; and it lays waste the entire land. There is no need for any surprise in this”.

sections.heading: Man Acts: Results Are by God

The results of acts are already decided, and their impacts are not in the hands of people. Acts and their results are all created by God, without anybody’s participation, even though they are related to us. X shoots an arrow towards Y, and it strikes Y as a jaguar does with its prey. Pains catch a person for a long period of the year and these pains are created by God and not by man. X dies out of shock immediately after shooting the arrow. Inspite of this, Y continues to suffer till his death. In such a case, you call X as a killer only because of his initial act, but the consequences are beyond his means. Yet, X is held responsible for the pains of Y, even though all these are the acts of God. In similar manner one’s earnings, efforts, plannings and cohabitation with wife are all creations of God and His decisions.
Natural Process Can Be Reversed
paras: Doors of effects are shut, and they do not occur if a friend of God feels ashamed of the causes made by him. God’s friends are those who are well aware of the essence and attributes of God, obedient to all His commands and avoiders of the acts prohibited by Him. Such friends (aulia) have the power to make the shot-out arrow come back. Doors of God’s actions are open for them. They can make the spoken words as unspoken; and avoid the effects of spoken words, as if there is neither the burning coal nor the meat to roast. They can wipe off and nullify the effect from the hearts of all those who have heard the spoken words. O great man, if you want to know of any argument or evidence on this matter, read the ayat in the Quran: Maa nansakh min aayaatin aw nunsihaanaati bikhairin aw mith(s)lihaa: None of our revelations do we abrogate; of course to be forgotton, but we substitute something better or similar. (Baqara: 2: 106) And, read the ayat: But you chose them for a laughing stock until they caused you to forget remembrance of me, while you laughed at them: Fattakhuz tumuhum sikhriyyan hattaa ansowkum zikri wa kuntum minhum tadhakun. (Muminun 23:110)

And read in the creation of the power of forgetfulness of these ayats; and understand it well. They are capable of making one remember and forget; they have command on the hearts of the people. When God closes the path of thinking, and makes the people forget what they have learnt, they cannot do any work inspite of being experts in performance. The ayat says that they laughed at the competent persons and also made them forget.

sections.heading: Masters of the Heart
paras: Officer of the city is a king of the bodies of the people, but the men of hearts are the kings of your hearts. Acts are the branches of knowledge and the means of knowing is the pupil of the eye. It is only through it that man sees things and learns about them. So also reading is through the pupil. But people see the pupil as very small in size, they consider it as unworthy, and nobody sees its greatness. Similar is the case of aulia (friends of God) who remain unknown to the people, but their jobs are very great. I cannot tell everything about them, as greater aulia who are the centres of other aulia, have prevented us from saying about them.

sections.heading: God Causes Memory and Forgetfulness
paras: As people’s forgetfulness and remembrance are from God, He responds to their callings. Hundreds of thousands of good and bad thoughts are brought out by God from their hearts every moment. During the daytime these thoughts are put into their hearts. They fill the oysters of the hearts of the people with pearls. Their souls take cognizance of all thoughts and insinuations of earlier days of their disciples under the guidance of God. With their influence, your profession and wisdom remain with you, so as to keep the doors of the means of livelihood open to you. Professions and character are the materials of journey towards God, which are lost by you upon your death, which come back to you on the doomsday. A goldsmith’s profession is not possible by the blacksmith. Their good conduct cannot reach those who reject their worth. Whatever face and character are dominant in you will be those upon which your achievements will be decided on the doomsday. Professional expertise and thoughts remain dormant during sleep at night, and in the morning, they return to the persons with their good and bad qualities. Like the trained pigeons, they carry the messages from other cities and places to the masters. Whatever things you see in the world are bound to go towards their origin. Parts go back to the whole to join it.

chapters.title: Death upon News of Death
chapters.subtitle: The Parrot’s Hearing of the Other Parrot’s Affair and Itself Dying, and the master’s Mourning

paras: When the parrot heard as to what happened to the other parrot, it also shivered, fell down and died. When the merchant saw this, he lost his self-control and threw down his cap on the ground. The parrot’s changed color and condition put him in great grief, and he tore the lapel of his shirt and said: “O parrot with the beautiful forehead! What happened to you? Why did you fall down and die? What a tragedy, my sweet-tongued bird, my friend and secret bearer has gone. So regrettable that my bird with sweet tunes, the consolation of my soul and my paradise is no more. If H. Sulaiman had such a bird, he would not have engaged himself with other birds. The bird I had purchased at a low price has left and gone away from my sight very soon.

sections.heading: (There are many subtle, esoteric points below which require deep thinking or meditation)
paras: “O my tongue, you are wholly responsible for this loss of mine. However, what can I say about you, as you only are talking all that I am talking. You are fire as well as the heap of freshly harvested grains. How long do you want to set fire to it? It is you alone who cause the collection of grains and you only set on fire. Without anybody’s knowledge our soul complains to you about certain things, as it is bound to act upon what you have committed to do, even if it is against the soul’s wish. You possess uncountable treasures; and you are also the cause of involving us in incurable diseases. You are the one to whistle like birds to lure and fool the birds to catch them in the net. And it is you only to make lamentations of the lovers to give relief during their separation from the beloveds. You only carry the message of friendship to the friends; and you only are the Satan and darkness of infidelity. You do not remain in silence any time, and so you do not keep anyone in peace. You always keep the arrow of enmity in the bow ready to shoot at me.

“Now you have flown my parrot away from me in death. At least now, you may stop grazing in the meadows of cruelty. Either give me an answer as to why you did this or do justice to me or give back to me the causes of my happiness. What a tragedy that the light that could put an end to my darkness, the morning that could brighten my day, my bird flying pleasurably, flew away to the longest distance from my nearest, has been lost forever.

sections.heading: Man, Always in Sorrows
paras: “Man, ignorant of realities is always in sorrows and becomes accustomed to them. Read the Surah Balad from Laa Uqsimu to Fii kabad, in the Quran: (90:1-4) which reads: I do call to witness this city: and you are a free man of this city; and parent and child; verily We have created man into toil and struggle: Laa Uqsimu bi haazal balad; wa anta hillum bi haazal balad; wa walidin wa maa walad, laqad khalaqnal insaana fii kabad.

“O my parrot! I was devoid of sorrows because of your face, and from your stream, I used to come out in full cleanliness. I am crazy in my desire to look at you, and it is not possible now. I cannot see you anymore. I can do so only when my soul gets out of me and enters into the world of souls where your soul has already gone. It is all God’s decision, and we have nothing to do before it. There is no heart which is not shattered into a hundred pieces by God’s commands. His great honour is that He is away from everybody, which cannot be explained by any number of arguments and counter arguments. How sorrowful, my tears are forming a river by sacrificing themselves upon my beautiful beloved. O my parrot, my wise bird, the bearer of my thoughts and secrets! You had been granted by God to me, but I was not grateful to Him. Every morning, you were the first to remember God and thank Him, and I followed you thereafter.”

sections.heading: Burn Yourself for God’s Inspiration
paras: That parrot whose voice is from the inspiration (wahi) of God, which was in existence well before all existences. That parrot is hidden in you, but you cannot see it, but you can see its reflections upon all these and those things. Those reflections are destroying your pleasures, but you are happy with these destructions and consider these destructive cruelties as just and proper and hold on to them. Through these follies you have burnt your soul for the sake of the body and tried to brighten your body through the burning of the soul. But I have burnt myself completely in my love for God; and anybody desiring to burn his rubbish body like me, may borrow fire from me.  One who is already burnt is not of any use for setting fire. Therefore, go in search of one who has the capacity to get burnt by fire. What an unexplainable tragedy! My soul is completely hidden now, just as the moon is hidden behind the clouds. It is not possible to explain about the love of God that I possess, as the fire of the heart has increased many times. The lion of my separation from God has become terribly wrathful and in search of blood. How can the one who is both smart and intoxicated at the same time even in his consciousness, be like the one who still holds the full cup of wine in his hand and not yet drunk? It is impossible for me to explain about God’s love in any condition of consciousness, or forgetfulness or in an admixture of both”.

sections.heading: Messages without words
paras: An intoxicated lion, which is totally out of control of himself, becomes more expansive than the expanse of the forest. I try to find out the rhythmic words for my verses, and my beloved tells me not to go to find anything other than the beloved. It tells me: take rest and sit comfortably, O searcher of rhythmic words! There is no need for you to find out words to please me. Your sitting before me in silence itself is a great wealth and praise for me. When your thoughts are totally engaged with me without the need of words, what is the worth of words that you are going after. What is the worth of sounds of spoken words. Sounds are nothing but the frames of the grapevines. The frame for grapevine is not the object, but only grapevine and grapes are. I wipe off the letters, words and sounds, so that I may talk to you without all the three of them.

I shall speak to you of that inspiration which was kept hidden from H. Adam, which was not told to H. Ibrahim, which even Jibraiil could not know. That which was not spoken to Jesus. God, the Absolute Truth has not said of all this to maintain his aloofness and individuality. That is referred to the Quran as: “fa awhaa ilaa ‘abdihi maa awhaa”: So did God convey the inspiration to His servant. Conveyed what he meant to convey: (Najm 53:10). [This conveyance was without the intervention of Jibraiil as at it was with other prophets. This was a direct conveyance by God to H. Muhammad as a special inspiration. Such a conveyance was not done to other prophets]. There is a word ‘MAA’ in this ayat which speaks of stressed positivity in one context and means negation in some other context. But as far as I am concerned (Rumi), I am neither in the positive sense nor in the negative. I am rather without my own existence. I have annihilated myself in God. I have found my existence in annihilation, as I have wrapped up my existence with annihilation. Only in annihilation, I have found out myself.

sections.heading: Self Destruction Gives Other Gains
paras: Put up a dam to avoid a flood, as otherwise it will cause disturbance and destruction. This advice is for you, but I am not afraid of my ruination as I know that imperial treasures are found only in the ruins, (which I have already found out). One who is already sunk in the Absolute Truth (God) desires that one should sink still more, like the tides of the ocean which rise high and go low. You should not think of receiving God’s radiance directly without any intervention as it would cause ruination as it happened with mount Toor, which upon God’s direct radiance got shattered to pieces. He will not bother to know whether it is better for him to be under the sea or above it. Whether it is better to be an arrow or a shield. O my heart! You would be one stuck with insinuation, if you make a difference between pleasure and pain.

Fulfilling of desire may give the pleasure of sweetness, but failure to meet the desire also becomes desirable and sweet. Both have the same impacts. Every star of such failed person becomes a ransom for a hundred crescents, as a true lover is always bent at his waist like the crescent. It is permissible for him to ignore everything of the world as if it is a massacre. We have obtained the price of our love and the award of ransom for murders caused to our body; and we run to get defeated in the game of the betting of our life.

sections.heading: Beloveds Too are Lovers
paras: All kings bow down before and obey their obedient, faithful servants; and beloveds love their lovers. All kings, in fact, are the slaves of their slaves as they know that their kingship is with the help and support of their ministers and servants; and they being experts in certain fields give the most suitable advice. Taking their advice and following on it is nothing but obedience to them or slavery. One in extreme obedience to another has no concern for oneself as though one is dead. In such a situation the other person who is obeyed also gets so much involved as though he is dead for himself. Thus, both sacrifice each other for each other. That is to say: the people are dead for the dead ones. A hunter searches for the prey and gets involved in the job of hunting so much, as if, he has been hunted and taken over by the fun of hunting. He thinks of nothing other than hunting. It is only in total search of involvement and commitment that he catches his prey, as otherwise, merely casual attempts to catch the prey lead to no success. Thus, the game of hunting hunts the hunter.

Similarly, the beloveds also love the lovers and are devoted to them. Thus all beloveds are captivated by the lovers. The beloveds become so much committed to the lovers. Thus, if you see a man in love of someone, think that, he is also loved by that someone. They are both related to each other in love, and both are lovers and beloveds of each other. If the thirsty are in search of water, water also is in search of the thirsty. They cannot meet their object and purpose of their existence without each other. Water from the ocean becomes vapor and then clouds and then falls as rain, and then forms rivers, rivulets and streams, and moves about here and there to meet the needs of those in thirst. Thus, when someone falls in love with you, bear with his love and be quiet. If he offers his ears to you to hear, you may also offer your ears in entirety to hear him all the more. Remember that God loves you; and take Him in your heart and devote yourself fully for Him.

sections.heading: Lover’s life is in Death
paras: The life of the lovers is in their death. Unless you lose your heart absolutely as though you are dead for the beloved, you cannot capture the heart of your beloved. I did everything to win the beloved’s heart in every pleasing manner, but the beloved was not amenable and went on dodging. In all humility I searched with all efforts, but my beloved hid from my sight in all manners and avoided to be seen. I said: “my life and wisdom are sunk in you”; but I was told: “go away; do not try your magic spells on me. I do not know what you think of me. You still consider me as different and far away from you, that you want to see me from a distance. What do you think of me? Am I that far from you, that you want to see me away from yourself?  What kind of love is this? You consider me to be worthless and want to buy me at a low price”.

God’s graces upon you are so many that they are considered cheap, and not recognized as worthy grants but given away as cheap commodities, just as a child gives away a pearl in exchange of a piece of bread.

sections.heading: Unspeakable Knowing
paras: Dive into the ocean of love, as the love of all earlier and later men of love is sunk in it. What all I have explained is cursory and if I speak of love in detail, tongues and wisdoms will catch fire. When I say the word ‘lip’, it means the lips of the river which are so long and away from each other containing so much of wealth in between them. When I say the word ‘Laa’ (no), I do not mean ‘none’ but I mean ‘nothing but God’. What else is there in the universe other than God? I have tasted the sweetness of gnosis of God; and this has made me bitter-faced, because sweetness created greater curiosity and added to the bitterness of my ignorance. Though what I know is very large but what I do not know is comparably much larger. I look at my ignorance and feel dejected and bitter. In fact, I prefer to remain silent, not because of not knowing but because of knowing too much. Also, our sweetness is hidden behind the veils of bitterness both in this and that world. What all I have said so far is not worthy of being put into every ear. What I said so far is one among the hundred secrets received from the knowledge from “me (God) alone, ie., ilmi- ladunni.”

sections.heading: Explanation of Knowledge “from God’s own presence” (Translator’s note)

[Ilmi Ladunni, knowledge from me (God) alone is a very special knowledge that comes directly from God. As stated in the Quran: wa allamnaahu min ladunna ilman: whom we had taught knowledge from Our Own Presence (Kahaf: 18:65). This is the special knowledge that was given by God to H. Khidhr during the days of H. Musa. There is a narrative full of many mysteries and esoteric matters. To put it in an economy of words: H. Musa met Khidhr and desired to be with him, a person whom God had taught knowledge from His Own Presence; and wanted to learn from him. With reluctance, he agreed on the condition that he should not ask him about any of his acts. It would not be possible to have patience in what he would see!
paras: On the way, Khidhr scuttled a boat he had used, and H. Musa questioned him on it, and Khidhr was not happy. Again, they proceeded; he found a young man whom he killed. Again, H. Musa expressed his surprise and begged pardon. They proceeded further and went to a village, where the people were not hospitable even upon their asking, quite contrary to eastern traditions. Here Khidhr set aright a wall that was about to fall. Again H. Musa commented. Then Khidhr told him: “You cannot be with me anymore as you make comments upon my acts out of your ignorance. However, I tell you the reasons for my acts which are beyond normal understanding. I scuttled the boat to spoil its shape, as after us, there was a king to follow our way and upon seeing a perfect boat could confiscate and deprive the poor boatman of his means of livelihood. As it was scuttled the king would not confiscate it being of no use and worth for him. As for the young man I killed; he was a very mischievous outlaw and about to kill his parents. I killed him on authority (either from God or he had special authority from ruler of that country to kill). And the act was setting erect the wall about to fall, was to protect it from falling as underneath it is a treasure, which would be looted upon the wall’s falling down. This treasure was kept there by a pious man for his children, who are yet young and take possession later when they grow older. And Khidhr concluded that such is the interpretation of those things over which you were unable to hold patience: zaalika taawiilu maa lam tastatii ‘alaihi sabran” (ibid :82)

H. Musa having been brought up in the Pharaoh’s palace was well aware of all secular knowledge that a member of royalty would get in those days. Plus, he had received knowledge from God on the Mount Tuur. But that was also related to worldly matters like politics and fight with a tyrant (Pharaoh), organizing a demoralized oppressed community (Bani Israil), taking them out of Egypt to protect them and their progeny from further troubles by Egyptians, giving them a law to organize themselves and conduct their affairs and so on. Neither was he in need, nor had the time to devote to the esoteric sciences like gnosis of God and inspiration from God on such esoteric matters. He came to know of another source of special knowledge that is ‘ilmi ladunni’, knowledge from God’s Own Presence that was given by God himself directly from His Own Presence, in Khidhr’s company for a short time.

Some Muslim sufis do claim this special knowledge from God’s Own Presence, as Rumi has claimed to possess when he said in the last sentence of this chapter saying: “What I said so far is one among the hundred secrets received from the knowledge from Me alone, ie, Ilmi Ladunni. Rumi’s claim to receive this knowledge is explained earlier in explaining the meaning of ayat: Fa awhaa ilaa abdihi maa awhaa (Najm: 53:10), which was given only to H. Muhammad and not to, H. Adam, H Ibrahim, H. Isa and not even to Jibraiil. Rumi got this knowledge from God’s Own Presence by annihilating himself in Him and others also can get by annihilating themselves in God — God knows best –Translator]

chapters.title: Maintain dignity and self-respect
chapters.subtitle: Exegesis of Hakim Sanai’s statement (May his soul get comfort from God): “It is of no concern if you are misguided by a pious or impious statement. So also, of a mark, good or bad, that takes you away from the friend”. And the meaning of the Prophet’s statement: “Sa‘ad is highly self-respecting, and I am more self-respecting than him, and Allah is more self-respecting than me, consequent upon which He has prohibited all open and hidden vices

paras: [Sa’ad bin ‘Ubaadah, a companion of the Prophet, upon hearing about the laws of evidence, procedure and punishment for fornication said: “If I see my wife indulging in fornication, I shall instantly kill her and I shall not have the patience to search for four witnesses to prove the offence”. The quoted statement captioned above relates to his statement –Qazi Sajjad Husain]

sections.heading: Maintain Self-Respect and Dignity
paras: The entire world maintains self-respect for the reason that God has the highest self-respect of all. He is like the soul and the world is like the body, and body accepts good or bad qualities from the soul. A man going for salat, having the nische as the place of object for his salat, may be considered as one of defective faith. A person in charge of the private chamber of the king but indulging in private trade is unsuitable for that job. It is a matter of regret and loss for the companion of the king to sit at his door. One, who shakes the king’s hands and kisses them in honor, will be sinful, if he kisses his feet. When you can hold the hand, it does not suit you to go around the feet. It is sacrificing his head for the king that is manly for him and not touching his feet. It is a sign of bravery and dignity. Though keeping the head on king’s feet is a mark of extreme servitude, but as against the acts of bravery and dignity, it is wrong and disgraceful. The king will feel it dishonorable if he sees one going after his fragrance, instead of seeing his face in closeness. God’s dignity is like wheat grains and the collected stock of fodder is a matter of wealth for men. Consider the dignity of God as the root of all honors and the honor of creatures is only a branch of it.

I shall stop the explanation of this matter and resort to complaining of the pains caused by that Dear One with ten hearts, that is, God alone, Who is the root of all dignity and self-respect. I cry on this for the reason that He gets pleased with our cries from both the material and spiritual worlds. Why should I not shed bitter tears and get into the circle of His lovers. [It is reported in the hadith(s) that God loves two kinds of drops that fall from the eyes — one kind of drops that fall from the eyes in His fear and the other: the drops of blood that fall from the eyes in a field of jihad — Qazi Sajjad Hussain.]

sections.heading: Pains in Love are Pleasures
paras: Why should I not become dark like the night which has no hope of the day: and myself having no scope to see His bright face even in the light of the day? My soul cries upon His displeasure as He likes my crying and I sacrifice my life for the Beloved who gives me pain. I am in love with my own sorrows and pains to please that great unmatchable King who has caused them. I convert the dust of sorrows into the eyeblack for my eyes so that these two eyes, which are wide and large like oceans may become so bright as to be filled up with pearls. The tears that the people shed for Him are in fact pearls, but they mistake them as tears. While complaining to the soul of my beloved, I am not actually complaining, but only narrating the details. My heart says that I am sorrowful, but I laugh with a weak resentment, because I am not sorrowful, but I am happy.

sections.heading: I, We, You and He are All the Same
paras: You are the honor of the truthful. Do justice to me as you are the chief of the gathering and I am only one among those present at your door. There is no difference between the chief of the gathering and the place of gathering. There is no scope for difference in ‘we’ and ‘I’ in You, as You are above them, just as the soul in man and woman is the same and the difference is only in the bodies; and You are the soul of all. Bodies of men and women are temporal and souls of both merge into You forever, when their bodies are gone. You have made us as ‘I’ and ‘we’ to play your own game and bet upon. When you make ‘we’ and ‘you’ as one, You become the pure beloved embracing us within Yourself. All these are only possibilities till they join and become one, in togetherness. And ultimately, what happens is the joining together of all in One beloved: The One and the Self-existing. All these are in their places; but O Commander of ‘kun’ (be), bring them all together with this command! O the One, whose understanding is beyond words and explanations.

sections.heading: God’s Lover Obliged to Worldly Phrases
paras: The physical, bodily eyes cannot see You. So long as we are engaged in the feelings of pleasures and pains, we cannot even imagine You. Even the heart that is engaged in these feelings is incapable of seeing You. One who is imprisoned in pleasure and pain of these temporary things can remain alive only in these two. The evergreen garden of love is everlasting, wherein there are many other fruits along with those of pleasure and pain. Love is superior to these two conditions and it remains green and fresh, on its own, without any concern for pleasure and pain. I have become so forlorn that I cannot express my love other than through the feelings and phrases of the lovers of the worldly beauties. O my beautiful one! Give the charity of your beautiful face and once again explain about all parts of the heart which got separated from each other upon the impacts of love. The beloved through the coquettish styles has caused fresh imprints of love on my heart. I have surrendered totally to the murderous attitude of the beloved and given permission to finish me off. I went on telling: “Do kill me, I sacrifice myself for you”; but the beloved avoided continuingly. I question my beloved”. Why do you run away from the lamentations of the humble sufferers, and why do you pour more sorrows on the hearts of the sorrowful. O my dear, every morning that appeared from the east, found you bright like the sun rising from the east. Why do you plead excuses with your lover, when the price of the sugar of your lips is so high that none can buy it and it remains only with you. You give a fresh life to this age-old-world, which has lost all its charms. Do hear the cravings of this lifeless and heartless body of mine and give life to it.”
All along, O Rumi, you have been explaining about the beauty and styles of the flowery beloved. Now you may say something of the pangs of separation of the bulbul which has gone away from the flower.

sections.heading: Love of God is Different
paras: Our enthusiasm is not related to pleasures and pains; nor our consciousness connected with our thoughts and imaginations. It has an entirely different condition, which is rarely to be found. Do not lose hopes as a result of the peculiar condition of yours, as God is great and full of might and means. Do not take the model of the love of temporal, material, physical beauties which man usually does. Do not remain entangled in the station of cruelties and graces of this worldly love and beloved. This matter should not be speculated in respect of God and love of God, as He is everlasting beloved and love. Cruelties and graces, pleasures and pains of the worldly love are newly created by God and such things get annihilated and they return to Him, as He alone is their inheritor, who alone is the Everlasting and Self-subsisting.

sections.heading: Temporal Love and Spiritual love
paras: For the whole night, I was engaged in these discussions which never ended, and morning arrived. It is during the daytime that I have to write this Math(s)navi with the support and encouragement of Husamuddin to whom I am highly obliged. I had forgotten him all along and therefore, I seek his pardon. Love alone is the seeker of the pardon from the absolute and entire wisdom and the real life (God). Love alone is the life of life and brightness of the pearls. Light of our morning receives light from You only, through the wine supported by You that we take as a morning drink. When the grants of God keep me in such conditions of inebriation and euphoria, what is wine for me that would intoxicate me. You should know that the exciting power the wine has, is the charity given by us to it. It begs to us to get revealed. On its own, it has no power of any kind, and only when we drink, it can show its worth. Not only wine, even the sky is compelled to be in rotation without a moment’s relief. It has no will of its own. It is envious of our consciousness which works and rests upon our will and wish. Wine gets intoxicating quality and intoxicates because of us and not otherwise. This body is created by us and for us and by our soul and not otherwise. We are like the honeybee which does everything and our body is wax made by us. Our soul has made our body with different parts just as the honeybee makes its hives. Enough of all this, my dear sir, tell us as to what happened to that man who lost his parrot in death.

chapters.title: Any Work Better than Laziness
chapters.subtitle: Return to the Narrative of the Master Merchant

paras: The merchant in the fire of pain and cries was making hundreds of talks of the earlier stated kinds. Sometimes talks opposite to each other, sometimes senseless and sometimes lovely; and also, mad and artificial sometimes, like a sinking man trying to catch any straw available to him, hoping that something may give him support in a dangerous situation. Out of the fear of the head sinking, he waves his hands and legs vigorously. Such a situation makes a friend anxious either to oblige him by supporting him or to show him pity. In such a situation of difficulties, it is always better to put effort instead of cool surrender.

Inspite of God being absolutely unconcerned with whatever may happen, God does not remain idle, and keeps engaged in work. This aspect of God and engagement in work is very strange to our understanding just as the grumbling and groaning of a healthy person. The groaning of the sick is natural; yet there are persons who groan inspite of being healthy. God’s keeping engaged in work every day has been stated as: kulla yowmin huwa fii shaanin: every day in new splendor does He shine (Rahman: 55:29). Therefore, you should also be engaged in work of cutting and pealing of something or doing something or other till the last breath. You should never be idle. There is every possibility that there may be at least some moment, when God’s grants may come over to you. Every man and woman in work is being watched by the ears and eyes of the Master of your life through the windows of your life around you. Again, I say, there is no end to this talk; therefore, say about the merchant and his parrot.

chapters.title: Parrot’s freedom from Prison
chapters.subtitle: The Merchant’s taking Out of the Parrot from the Cage and Throwing Outside, and Parrot’s flying off

paras: Thereafter, the merchant removed the dead parrot out of the cage and threw it outside. Instantly the parrot flew off to a high branch of the tree. The parrot flew off in such a manner as the sun runs from east to west. The merchant was taken to surprise at this act of the bird and found out a secret of the bird hitherto not known to him. He raised his head above and said: “O my nightingale, give a share of your act to me. You learnt from what the other parrot did and shut our eyes from your trick. You played a trick with us and set us on fire and brightened yourself in its light”

The parrot said: “The other parrot taught me the trick by its action and to give up talking and be victorious. It gave the message: it is your pleasing voice that has put you in the cage. It showed itself as dead to give a practical lesson. Your sweet tunes are pleasing the common folk and elite. Be dead like me in order to get freedom. If you become a grain, bird will pick you up.
