Eliminate the feelings of false pride, greatness of character, arrogance and high claims from your heart so that you may get deliverance. False pride itself is very bad and, from the destitute, it is all the worse. The day is cold, full of ice and clothes are also wet. How long you want to project yourself of greatness and twist your mustacheos. Your house is like the house of spider built of cobweb. Wa inna awhana-albuyuti labaitul ankabuut: the frailest of all houses is the spider’s house: (Spider: 29:41). Since when have you brightened your soul with contentment? You have only learnt a few words about contentment.

sections.heading: Contentment: Everlasting Treasure
paras: The noble Prophet has said: Alqina ‘atu kanzun la yanfidu: contentment is a treasure that never gets exhausted. What is contentment? It is a treasure. You do not know the difference between treasure and sorrow. Contentment is an ever-flowing treasure. Do not you, boast of it. You are only an ever-flowing pain and sorrow. Do you not call me as your wife and speak of being a counterpart? Such togetherness is seen only in a couple of pigeons which fly together. I am your counterpart only in justice and not in treacheries. Why do you go along with the king and the noble lords, when you are only pricking the flies in the air to drag blood from their veins? You pounce upon the dogs for bones, and cry and sigh like a flute with empty stomach. Do not look at me with hate and contempt, so that I may not speak of the conditions of all and every nerve of your body. You consider your wisdom to be greater than mine. Then why did you choose me as your wife. Do not pounce on me like the ill-natured wolf. Your wisdom is full of shame. It is better to be without wisdom than to have wisdom like yours.

sections.heading: Snake and snake-charmer charm Each other
paras: As your wisdom is a net for humans, it is not wisdom, but snake and scorpion. Your cruelties and treacheries can be understood by God alone. We can only pray to God that the hands of your wisdom may not fall on us. You are a strange combination of the snake and the snake catcher together. You are a dishonour to the Arabs: you are a snake as well as a snake-catcher. If the crow were to be aware of its ugliness, it would have melted like ice due to the heat of its own sorrows and ugliness. The speller of magic-formula reads it as an enemy of the snake. But this is reciprocal as the snake-charmer recites the formula on the snake; and the snake also spells a formula on the charmer as a consequence of which, he takes fancy for snake-catching and proudly demonstrates his skill. The snake’s spell is silent. Had not the snake made a net of its magic on the snake-catcher, he would not have indulged in snake-catching. The magician casting spells on the snake out of greed for money and fancy, does not realise the magic spell of the snake at that time. The snake tells him: “O snake-charmer! Look carefully, you have considered your spell, but consider my spell too. You take the name of God in your spells to catch me, so as to disgrace me with the cries of the mob witnessing the fun of my actions. You should know that I was caught by the name of God and not by your designs. How regretful for you to use the name of God as a trap. God’s name will grant justice to me from you as I have offered my body and soul to God; so that for the injuries you have caused to me, God may cut off your jugular vein and kill you or put you in prison like me”.
The woman thus spoke harshly to her husband in records upon records.

chapters.title: Poverty and Riches are Relative
chapters.subtitle: Husband’s Advice to the wife, not to look at the Poor with contempt and not to look at the Affairs of God by considering Herself to be Perfect; and not to Speak ill of the Poor and their Poverty because of her own Poverty [Translator’s note:  Basically poverty and riches are mental attitudes. A billionaire considers a millionaire as poor, and a trillionaire considers a billionaire as poor. There is no limit to riches and so also to poverty. Poverty as meant by the Prophet can be taken as the minimum to keep one maintain oneself in health and happiness by one’s own efforts in a self-respecting manner, a model of which was the Prophet himself. The first four califs of the Muslims followed this model. (H. Umar ruled over a geographical territory comprising of an area from Palestine to Iran and Egypt which no other ruler prior to him had. Wealth was pouring in his capital, which was distributed to all. But he lived on frugal dry bread with a single curry and wore patched garments and lived in a small house. He followed the Prophet and his predecessor, H. Abu Bakr and was followed by the next two califs H. Usman and H. Ali. They all lived in that poverty of which the Prophet was proud. Subsequently also many Muslim kings and emperors lived like this in poverty in their personal life. While sitting in the courts and darbars only, they wore imperial dress and in personal life they ate simple food and wore simple dress. Some of them eked out their livelihood by writing the Quran like professional scribes and doing some petty jobs; and ate food prepared out of these earnings. The aspect of pride for them was their poverty, which also they did not speak of, as it would amount to Riya (ostentation: showiness). Well known in this aspect are all the rulers of Slave Dynasty, Muhammed bin Tughlaq and Aurangzeb in India, and Umar b. Abdal Azeez in Iraq. Many kings like Ibrahim Ad-Ham and Baba Fakhruddin discarded kingship and became Darvishs. These names are given only as examples of the well-known, otherwise, most of the Muslims rulers had been as such. They are the well-known followers of ‘Al faqru fakhri’ of the Prophet. A voluminous book can be written on this aspect and to explain in verse: “Poverty has thousands of honours and designs hidden in it –Translator]

sections.heading: Wealth to Hide Defects
paras: The husband heard these remarks from his wife patiently and then looked at her and said: “O my wife! Are you a woman or a father of sorrows? Do not find fault with me. Poverty is a cause of pride. Wealth and gold are like a cap for the head; whoever wears it, does so to hide his baldness. Whoever has beautiful tufts and curly hair appears more handsome without the cap. A truthful man is like good sight. It is better for him to keep his eyes uncovered than to cover them. At the time of selling the slave, the slave merchant, removes his clothes to show that he has no defects. Why would he undress him if he has defects? On the contrary, he would cheat the buyer by keeping him fully dressed. He would tell the buyer that he feels shy of showing his good and bad qualities. He would run away from you if I undress him. The slave merchant himself is full of defects from his ears to feet, but he has wealth, and wealth is a hider of defects. But a greedy fellow does not look at his defects. Thus, greed has become a coordinator of the hearts of the greedy. Even if a poor man speaks of things as valuable as a gold mine, his words will not fall into the ears of the buyers and his goods will not see the path of sale.

“Affairs of the Darvish (poor) are beyond the scope of your understanding. Do not look at them with contempt. Some of them are those who hold on to the doors of the rich. Their object is worldly. They are not the real Darvishes. There are others who hold on to the door of God and their object is other-worldly. Their job is different from the worldly jobs. There are grants upon them from God at every moment. They are beyond the needs of wealth and property. They get a large earning from God of Majesty. God is equitable and the equitable do not inflict pain upon the weak. He gives wealth and materials to one and keeps another one in the fire of poverty. [ He knows who should be given what, and acts as such. He has given a heart inclined toward wealth for some. He gives them wealth. And some other’s heart is happy in deprivations and he keeps them in poverty. This is equity (adle);  giving to what one needs. And justice is giving the same to all whether they need or not. Giving the same to all will not keep the world going smoothly and in progress. That is His majesty]. One who thinks about this as unjust burns oneself in the fire of one’s misconceptions about God, because of narrow and incomplete knowledge of the world. Poverty does such great things, which wealth does not do. The Prophet’s saying “my pride is in my poverty”: “al faqru Fakhri” is neither a gossip nor meaningless. It has hundreds of thousands of honours and designs hidden in it.”

sections.heading: Fangs Are Snake’s Enemies
paras: The husband continued: “In your anger, you have given me so many names. You have called me as one of snake’s nature and as snake-catcher. But you should know that if I catch a snake, I pluck its fangs so that it may be saved from its head being crushed. It is out of the fear of its fangs that people kill it. That is to say, its fangs are the enemies of its life. I make this enemy of man a friend through my magic spells. I do not recite these spells out of greed. I have completely smashed my greed. I swear upon God! I do not have any expectations from the people. I have a world of contentment in my heart. You see such things of your makings from the top of a guava tree. Get down from it so that you may see things in their true perspectives. [Guava tree refers to a story narrated in the fourth volume of the Math(s)navi. A woman of bad character promised her paramour to have sex with him being watched upon by her husband. She took her husband to a garden asked him to remain below a guava tree and said she would climb the tree to pluck fruits and throw down for him. When she was atop, she shouted at and cursed him for having sex with a stranger woman. He was surprised and denied. Then she told him to climb and called her paramour and had sex with him. When he shouted and expressed anger and resentment, she said: nothing of that kind has happened. There appears to be some magic spell in this tree that whoever climbs it, sees such acts being done, down below under it.] When you swirl around and become dizzy, you see your house swirling, even though it is you who are swirling.”

chapters.title: Man sees What he wants to See
chapters.subtitle: To Explain that man sees things appear to be moving to him, which are within the Zone of his Existence. So much, that He sees the sun Blue with blue glass, and red with Red glass. When the colours, vanish Brightness appears white and becomes one to show the things in better Clarity

paras: Abu Jehal looked at the Prophet and said: “You are ugly inspite of being born in the family of Bani Hashim”. The Prophet said: “You are right, even though you talk too much”. H. Abu Bakr Siddiq looked the Prophet and said: “You are the sun full of brightness, not just for those in the east and west but for all and everywhere”. The Prophet said, “You are right my dear friend; you are free of this worthless world.”

Those present said: O leader of the world! How do you say as ‘rightly said’ to two opposite versions? The Prophet said: “I am a mirror well-polished by the hand. Turks and Indians see in me as they themselves are. One who has a mirror before one, sees one’s own good and bad features, within the mirror”.

sections.heading: Contentment Cause of Pleasure
paras: With this the husband continued to say to his wife: “If you consider me to be greedy, it is better that you get out of this feminine guess. A Darvish is certainly greedy of graces of God. One who has this greed cannot be greedy of worldly things. You may test the impacts of voluntary poverty (faqr) for two days so that you may see two times of contentment. Have patience with poverty and give up these sorrows as there is a God-given honour in poverty. Do not be sour like vinegar and see that thousands are sunk in this ocean of honey with their contentment. Look at the hundreds of thousands of people who are mixed up with this bitterness (of deprivation) like flowers in gulqand (a tasteful fragrant mixture of rose petals and honey). How regrettable! Had you been considerate, you would have been an explanation of the affairs of my heart. These matters are like milk in the breasts of life and they cannot flow out unless they are suckled with efforts.

sections.heading: Grants Created for Seekers
paras: “When one is thirsty and crazy of knowledge, even a master as bad as dead, will refresh and speak out. If the hearer is fresh and smart, hundreds of dumb mouths start talking. It all depends upon the seeker of knowledge. When a stranger comes at the door, women hide themselves behind curtains. And if a relative comes, women get pleased and remove their veils. The face that is made good-looking, pleasing and beautiful is for the eyes that look at it. The high pitch and low pitch of the musical instrument are not for the deaf. God has not made the musk fragrant without a purpose. It is for the smelling of a healthy nose and not for one who has no sense of smell. God has made the pleasing tunes of the flute for the purpose of man to hear and not for the devil. God has made the sky and earth, and created light and heat in between them. This earth is for those made of matter and the sky for the non-material beings to reside. Man, who lives in this lowly world is opposed to the dwellers above. Yet, there are those who are ready to buy houses in both these places.

sections.heading: Better to be Away from Quarrels at Home
paras: “O the one hidden behind the curtain! Have you ever beautified yourself for the sake of the blind? I may fill the whole world with pearls, but what can I do, if you do not have a share in them? O my wife! Give up these quarrels and attempts to deviate me from my path; and if you cannot give them up, give me up. There is no place in my heart for a fight even for good against bad, as my heart is devoid of such feelings and it runs away from both fights and peace. Do not strike your stings on my wound and do not cause injury to my body, which has no concern for itself. If you keep quiet, it is alright; if not, I shall give up everything and run away from the house. It is better to be bare foot than to wear the short-sized shoe. It is better to go on a journey than to engage in quarrels at home.”

chapters.title: Man and Woman, Made for Each Other
chapters.subtitle: The wife’s becoming considerate and Seeking his Pardon upon his Talks

paras: When the wife found that he was harsh and hard, she started crying. Crying, after all, is a design of women. She said: “I had not thought that you would be like this. I had expected something different from you”.

She started to be humble and said: “I am just your dust; and not the wife. My entire body and whatever I have is yours. Commanding and controlling are entirely yours. If my heart went out of my patience on poverty, it was not for myself but for you. You are the balm for my pains. I do not like to see you in destitution. All that I did and said is not for me. This crying and shouting is for you. I swear upon God, my very life is for you. It thinks of sacrificing itself every moment for you. How good it would have been if your life upon which I sacrifice mine, been aware of what is there in my heart and not in my words. Now that you think of me like this, I feel disgusted of my body and soul, as you feel that I have sought for wealth for my sake. It is not so. I throw dust on gold and silver, if you have to deal with me in this manner. You live in my heart and soul, yet you are now so unhappy with me. Be unhappy with me. You have every right for this. But my soul seeks pardon of your happiness.

sections.heading: Wife’s Resentment with Love
paras: “Recall those days also to your mind when I was like an idol and you were an idol-worshiper. This humble maid has brightened her heart to be in consonance with you. If you say that something is cooked, I shall say something more, stressing that is roasted. I am like a leaf of Palak; you may cook me in whatever manner, in whatever dish of your choice: in sour dish or in sweet dish. Earlier, I spoke of infidelity, but now I have become faithful and I am standing in wait to obey your command. I could not recognize your royal attitude, and out of my arrogance, indecently ran towards you like a donkey. I have now made your pardon as my lamp. I repent for my wrongs and give up my objections. I keep before you the sword and shroud and bow down my head so that you me cut it off.

“You speak of separating yourself from me. You may do anything to me but not this. There is something hidden in you which seeks your pardon, which always recommends my case every time, even in my absence. The recommender which is within you is your good nature. If is in the hope of its recommendation that I have committed that sin. Have mercy upon me in silence. O angry one! Your good nature is heavier than a hundred maunds of honey.”

sections.heading: Women Win by Humility
paras: In this manner, she was softly speaking of all this with her whole heart and then fell with her face down before him. When her cries and sighs went beyond limits, her husband’s heart melted. How could he maintain his patience and discomfort, as even without cries she was a pleasing beloved? From out of this rain of her tears, a spark came and fell on his heart. He was a slave of her beautiful face. Imagine what happens when a free man becomes a slave. What will happen to you if a proud person before whose pride your heart trembles, starts crying before you? What will happen to you when the beloved with whose coquettishness you feel like losing your life, starts submitting to your love in a humble manner? What happens, when one whose job was nothing but shedding blood, bows down his head before you? What a profitable dealing it would be? What will happen if a proud one who was always showing a stiff neck to you, suddenly starts behaving in very good manners with you? Quran says: Fair in the eyes of men is the love of things they covet; women and sons. Zuyyina lilnasi hubbu alshahawati minan nisa’i  wa albaniin…i (Imran: 3:14). How can anybody get freed of what has been made fair and loveable by God? When He has created woman in order that man might dwell with her (in love), as stated in the Quran: And made his mate of like nature in order that (man) might dwell with her in love: wa ja‘ala minha zawjaha liyaskuna ilaiha (A‘araf :7:189). When she has been created to dwell with him, how could H. Adam remain away from her.

sections.heading: Even Rustam, the son of that old women and greater in strength than H. Hamza (the Prophet’s uncle who was known for his bravery), was a prisoner at the command of his old wife. That great personality with whose words the world swooned (the Prophet), used to say: kallimini ya Humaira, “speak to me, O humaira”, to his wife.
paras: Water is dominant upon fire because its dominance puts it out, but when it is hidden behind the curtain of the pot, loses its dominance and gets dominated by fire and boils. When the pot came in between, fire annihilated it by converting it into air (steam). Though, apparently, you are dominant upon woman, but deep inside, you are dominated by and devoted to her. Love and closeness are the qualities of men; but other animals have very little of these qualities and therefore, their love is also lesser.

chapters.title: Women dominate over Men
chapters.subtitle: To Explain the Meaning of the Hadith(s): Women are Dominant upon wise men and the Ignorant Men are Dominant upon women

sections.heading: Women are God’s Reflection
paras: The Prophet has said: “Women are very much dominant on the wise and kind-hearted people. Yet there are many crude men who are dominant upon women as they lead their life in crude and ill-tempered manners. They have very little softness, mercy and love in them as animal instinct is dominant in them. Love and kindness are qualities of man; anger and passions are animal instincts. Women are not just beloveds of men, they are the reflections of God, as they give birth to men and women and bring them up, just as God creates and sustains the creations.

chapters.title: Reciprocity in Love
chapters.subtitle: Husband’s Acceptance of the Wife’s Pleadings, which were about the means of Livelihood, and considering her Objections as a direction From God

paras: It is an accepted fact by all wise men that whatever is moving is with a mover. The turning of a spindle by an elderly woman can be taken as a model of turning around of the sky.

The husband of that woman felt so ashamed for all that he said, just as the cruel fellows feel of their cruelty at the time of their death. He said: “My dear, why did I become an opponent of myself? Why did I kick my own life, and misbehaved”?

sections.heading: Husbands Regret After Rebuke
paras: When fate comes to play its role, wisdom and sense are lost. No one except God knows about the fateful event as to when, how and in what manner it comes. When it comes, it shuts the eyes so that our wisdom will not know even about our head and feet. That great leader of the pious people, H. Ali, has said:” When fate comes, eyes become blind”. When after playing its role, fate passes off, man starts cursing himself and bites his own hands. He tears the curtain of darkness that had hidden things from him and feels sorry for his acts.

The husband said to his wife: “I am ashamed of myself. Had I behaved like an infidel, now, I repent for it, and become a muslim. I have wronged you. Please take pity on me: and do not remove me from your mind once and for all. When an old infidel feels regret, he seeks pardon of it as though he becomes a muslim. I have committed a sin; please forgive me for it. Accept my excuses and hear this: God’s court is full of mercy and grants; all the things in existence and those that have not come into existence and are in the world of non-existence are in love with Him. But faith in Him, and infidelity and rejection of Him are all the lovers of that greatness. Both copper and gold are the slaves of his chemistry.

chapters.title: God made both Musa and Pharaoh
chapters.subtitle: To Explain that Both H. Musa and Pharaoh Follow the Path shown by Him. Poison and Antidote, darkness and Light; and Pharaoh’s Lonely sitting with God, are God’s own Making

paras: Both H. Musa and Pharaoh are obedient to one truth. Apparently, H. Musa is on the right side and Pharaoh on the wrong. H. Musa used to cry before God even during the day; but at night, Pharaoh also used to cry before God saying: “What is this yoke around my neck, my God. Had there been no yoke around the neck, why would anyone arrogate to himself: I am all in all and the wisest, upon his ego. You have made Musa bright like the moon but made a black face of my life. You have brightened Musa but surrounded me with dust. My star appeared to be brighter than the moon, but what can I do when it is eclipsed. Till then, people beat the drum of my kingship and lordship, but the same people, now clap for me that I may be freed of the eclipse (as was the belief of some people that they could ward off the evil effects of the eclipse by clapping). They used to beat upon large gongs to honour me calling me “Our Lord”. But now they shout to protect and free me as though I am an eclipsed moon.
“I am just a king (Pharaoh), but how regrettable that people with the beatings of drums say that I am a great Lord.”

sections.heading: All are Made and Unmade by God
paras: “We are all the slaves of one Lord, but Your axe goes on creating splits on the trees of Your forest. Then you put a patch on the splits of some branches and reset them, and some others are made to fall and go waste. Branches have no control on the axe handle; and every branch undergoes its impacts. With that great authority of Your axe, may You be pleased to set aright the wrong results”.

After saying this, Pharaoh said to himself in his heart: “How strange? I remain in saying “O My Lord” for the whole night. I become humble and moderate in my loneliness; but when I go before Musa, why do I become something else?”

Colour of the counterfeit coin is ten times brighter than that of the genuine coin, but when it is brought before fire, it loses its polish and becomes black. Pharaoh’s brightness was artificial and worldly, and when it faced the spiritual heat of H. Musa, it became dark. The reality is that our heart and body are obedient to God, Who makes them smart and wise in one moment; and in the other moment makes them worthless like dust. In a moment, He makes us like the moon and in the next moment, He makes us black. Who else than God can do this? When He tells me to become a green farm, I become green; and when He says that I should become ugly, I become yellow. At the command of ‘kun’ (be) to the bat in the field of games, we run in the world of existences and the world of non-existence.

sections.heading: Colourlessness to Colours
paras: Basically, all are the same as colourless objects. When the colourless got into the prison of colours, one Musa entered into a fight with another Musa. It is the colour that has put them into conflict. If you re-enter into the world of colourlessness which you originally possessed, you will see that both Musa and Pharaoh are at peace. They are both doing their jobs as allotted to them. They do not have to play any role on their own.

sections.heading: You may raise an objection to what I said and say: Colour is a reality. It cannot be changed by words, by calling it colourless or colourful. Your saying that colour comes out of colourlessness is very strange. A colourless thing cannot get colour on its own. Similarly, there cannot be an oppositeness in colour and colourlessness. If God, the Absolute and Independent, Himself is allotting different jobs to different creations, and men are kept in opposition to each other enabling them to do their respective jobs, why does He not do things on His own. This speaks not of his absoluteness but of possibilities. That is, absoluteness is changed into possibility.
Oil and Water Do not Mix
paras: I say: Oil seeds grow and develop with water. But ultimately oil becomes an enemy of water. When oil has been made from water, why they are opposite of each other. So also, flowers and thorns are in the same plant. Yet they are opposed to each other and people also debate about them. Or it may not be an opposition to each other, but there is some particular object in it. Just as the auctioners and middlemen pretend to be at loggerheads with each other; or simply saying this is not this and that is not that. Or there are confusions in this. Confusions about the objects and about the means of searching. If you want a treasure, you will have to go to the ruins, as cities got destroyed along with materials in the houses. By treasure you mean the materials of riches, which is a confusion about the object of search. I say: “they are not real treasures. But they give us a lead that just as treasures are found in ruins, which are far away from the cities, so also the spiritual treasures of the soul are also found in seclusion, away from the cities. By considering the material things as treasure and going in search of them, you are actually losing real treasure. They are of no worth in comparison with spiritual treasures. It is through the spiritual treasure that you will understand what I said earlier about colour coming out of colourlessness and colourlessness out of colour.

sections.heading: Destruction, More Certain, But Avoids You
paras: Further, you go on constructing buildings and there is existence and also its opposite in them. Both are not lasting. They will remain for sometime and then decay and fall off. Here also you can see a conflict between two opposites— coming into existence and going out of it. This is easy for you to understand. This does not, however mean that existence hates nullity; but only that nullity rejects its permanent existence, because everything has ultimately to be nullity. Do not think that you want to avoid nullity. No: it is not so. It is rather that, nullity keeps itself away from you. Though apparently, it calls you towards itself projecting itself to be everlasting and you accept it, but in reality, it chases you away from itself, just as you chase animals with a stick. This is how the chased animals feel that they are being sent away. But actually, they are sent towards their sheds.

There are people who are like flowers in burning fire (like the friends of God) and yet there are people who are in pain and sorrow in the garden. These matters are like the thieves wearing shoes with reverse marks on their soles: (front markings towards the back and back markings of the heels towards the front so as to mislead the observers of the markings to feel their forward trip as return trip). Therefore, try to understand the hate of Pharaoh for H. Musa from H. Musa’s point of view.

chapters.title: Loss in both the Worlds
chapters.subtitle: Reasons for the Deprivation of the Hard-hearted of both the Worlds: khasira aldunya wa alakhirata. They lose both this world and the hereafter: Hajj: 22:11 [Translator’s note: From the time of Ptolemy (second century AD) to 1687 for 1500 years nobody thought as to what holds the celestial objects (sun, moon, planets, except earth) in the space because, earth was taken to be at the centre. Only their motions were taken into account in circles attached to their respective spheres around the earth. The idea of earth being at the centre was given up by Copernicus in 1514, which was not openly announced. Instead of earth, sun was taken as at the centre, which was later boldly declared by Kepler and Galileo in 1609, yet nobody thought as to what holds these celestial bodies in space. Only in 1687, Newton came out with the idea of universal gravitation which holds the bodies together in space, according to which each body was attracted by others. Yet, Newton was not totally satisfied and doubt persisted in his mind as to why they do not fall down on a single point, which he expressed in a latter four years later to another leading thinker, Richard Bantley in 1691. The slight conjecture was that their remaining in constant motion was holding them in their respective places. (A brief History of time: Stephen Hawking page-2 to 6)

paras: A philosopher had believed that the sky is like the egg and the earth is like its yolk. One person asked him as to how the earth is settled at the centre of the vast expanse of the sky, just as a chandelier, which neither comes down nor goes up. The philosopher said that this is due to the pull of the sky from all sides because of which it is held up in the air from the six dimensions (of back-front, right-left, top-bottom) just as a round structure made of magnet holds iron in the centre. The other philosopher said that the clean and clear sky cannot pull the dark earth towards itself. But rather, pushes or chases it from six dimensions so that it may remain in the midst of fierce winds.

It was as late as in 1915 that Einstein came out with the general theory of relativity to say that space-time communicates the gravitational force through curvature or warping to hold objects in their respective places, gravity being a property of space which also controls their motions. (Ibid page 33).

Consider what is discussed between the philosophers (scientists, rationlists) about the earth’s remaining suspended in the centre of the sky like a chandelier without going up or down. One said: Sky is like an egg holding the earth as yolk within it. Another said: Sky pulls or attracts the earth from all directions like an iron sphere held in the centre of a structure of magnet. Another disagreed and said: Sky is too great to attract earth. It pushes or chases it away from all directions. You may see how what is said by Eienstein is already told.

This shows the extent of scientific curiosity, study, knowledge and discussions during or prior to the days of Rumi (1207 – 1273) in the world around him, the Muslim world. Consider also that at that time, Europe was in the Dark Ages (5th century to 1000 A D) and Middle Ages (Dark Ages dragging upto 1453). This verse is casually taken to refer to some philosophical/spiritual/moral matters, because Math(s)navi’s purpose is not exposition of scientific knowledge of the physical world but to propagate moral teachings. Many other such scientific facts are cited in the Math(s)navi elsewhere which are appropriately explained — Translator].

sections.heading: Spiritualists needed for Guidance.
paras: As per this, with the chasing away by the men of perfection with their kind nature, the lives of the Pharaohs fell into misguidance. And with this chasing away from this world and that world, they remain in misguidance, without any support from this and that. You raise your head before the servants of the Lord of Majesty, as they are unhappy with your (vicious) existence. They have kahruba with them (a gum that pulls towards itself even the minute bits of grass). When they show it, it drags the minute bits of your existence towards itself. When they hide their Kahruba, it makes even your obedience rebellious. Just as the grade of your animal soul is of a prisoner and follower of your human soul, the status of man is as a follower at the hands of the friends of God. The noble Prophet was called as His obedient servant while others were addressed as ‘My devotees’ in the Quran when He said: ‘Yaa ibaadi’ (Zukhruf : 43:68).

You are a camel, and your wisdom is its driver, and it drags you toward all directions with all its might. The friends of God are the wisdom of wisdoms, and all other wisdoms are like the camels, driven by their nasal ropes. Look at them with an idea to seek wisdom. You will see that there is one guide and hundreds of thousands of followers. Consider them as guides as the phrase camel-drivers does not suit to their status. Consider them to be the eyes that look at the sun which others cannot do. This world is in darkness and stagnation, waiting for the sun for light and is thus dependent upon the day. It is very strange that the sun is hidden in a particle or the pupil of the eye as though a lion is wrapped under the skin of the sheep. Similarly, the soul which is as great as the sun is hidden in the body.

sections.heading: Prophets are Perfect and Guides
paras: This sun of the soul is a river hidden under a layer of grass. Someone mistaking it for grass and stepping upon it, you will drown into the river. You should be very careful in this matter. Doubts and good hopes in your inside are a great grace of God for your guidance. Every prophet that came in the world was alone but had six hundred worlds with him. In other words, he had an entire community of followers. They took the greatest and highest world of spirits in the control of their hands and wrapped it up with an ordinary mark of their own. Foolish people considered them as weak individuals, without knowing that the companions of the Lord cannot be weak. They said that a prophet is just no more than one. It is a pity for them that they could not have a far-sight to see them in full. It is only the perfect who look at the far-off results. One should always be away from ignorance. Now, for this purpose, you may hear the well-known narrative of Prophet Salih. Yet again, do not confine yourself to words. Go beyond the words and seek the meanings, for the reason that one who looks at the apparent does not look at the distant-final-result. You will lead a peaceful life if you look at the distant end.

chapters.title: End of the Mischievous and Cruel
chapters.subtitle: Consideration of the H. Salih’s she Camel as mean by the Enemies of H. Salih. When God wishes to destroy an army, he makes its enemy appear deficient and lowly. Wa yuqallilukum fi a‘yunihum liyaqdhi yallaahu amran kana ma f‘ulan: And He made you appear as contemptible in their eyes that God may accomplish a matter already enacted (Anfal: 8:44)

paras: The she-camel of H. Salih was a camel to look at; but the harsh community, out of its ignorance cut off the tendons of her legs. They had become her enemies for the sake of the water in the stream, becoming blind of the grants of food and water. She drank water from a natural rain-fed stream, but they prevented God’s water from the thirsty. The body of H. Salih’s camel was like that of the good people; and she became a hunting ground of the mean, vicious people. See how those people were dealt with by the she camel of God, about which H. Salih had told his people: A she camel of God, so let her drink: Naaqatu Allahi wa suqyaaha (Shams:91:13). The police officer of God’s destructive forces destroyed an entire well-organized city as a retribution for the killing of a she camel.

sections.heading: Soul and Body Differentiated
paras: The soul of H. Salih is like a camel and the mischievous misguided self is like the cutters of the tendons. Soul is like H. Salih and body is like the camel. Soul is in great pleasure of meeting with God, and body is in the pangs of hunger. H. Salih’s soul was one to be affected by troubles and the wound was caused on the she camel and not upon him. H. Salih’s soul was not one to be put to torture; and God’s light is not a tasty morsel for the infidels. God has attached the soul to the body in an invisible manner so that they may trouble the body and fall into trials. Being ignorant, they try to torture the soul, which is nothing but torturing God, as it is connected with God, just as a pot of water is connected with the stream. God has attached it to the body so that it may protect the whole world. Nobody can have a victory on the soul, as any injury inflicted on the body is like one on the oyster and not on the pearl. You may become the body of the camel of a godly person, so that your soul may become a colleague of the soul of H. Salih.

sections.heading: Warnings: Step by Step
paras: H. Salih told his people: “As you are jealous of the camel, you will face a calamity from God after three days. After three days, from God, the life-taking dagger will come like fire which has three signs. The colour of the faces of you all will be altered, which will be different from each other. All your faces will be coloured like saffron on the first day; and red on the second day; and black on the third day; and thereafter will come the calamity from God. If you want a sign for this warning from me, look at the camel-foal that is running away towards the hills. If you can catch it, it means, you can save yourself, or otherwise the bird of hope flies off from the net”.

When they heard this from him, they all ran behind the camel-foal like dogs. But none could reach it and the foal was lost in the hills. In like manner, the clean soul, which hates the body runs towards God, the Benevolent Lord. Then H. Salih told them:” You have seen that the judgement of God is confirmed, which put an end to the chance of any hope. The foal of the camel is like the heart of one to whom you should serve and show gratitude. If your heart is cleansed, you will be rid of the calamity or otherwise, you lose all hopes and get frustrated”.

sections.heading: Warnings Before Calamities
paras: When they heard this frightening warning, they started waiting for the consequence. On the first day they saw their faces having gone yellow and started taking cold sighs in hopelessness. On the second day their faces became red and they lost all hopes, and expectations. On the third day, their faces became black and what H. Salih had warned about came to be established without any doubt. When all of them lost hopes, they fell down on their knees. The trustworthy Gabriel has brought down in the Quran details of the meaning of falling down on the knees. He brought the fact about the Th(s)amud people Fa akhazat humul rajfatu,faasbahu fi daarihim ja th(s)imiin: So the earthquake took them unawares, and they lay prostrate in their homes in the morning (A‘raf:7:78).

You must sit with folded legs whenever you have to take lessons from your teacher as the teacher will find you in full attention. The Th(s)amud people waited for the next consequence of getting hit by God. The waiting period was over, and the city was destroyed.

H. Salih left his secluded place and went towards the city and found it in dust and smoke. He heard the lamentations of the parts of their bodies. There were cries and there was none to hear. He heard cries form their bones. He saw their eyes shedding tears of blood falling like hailstones. When their cries went beyond limits, he found them to be like the messages of warnings; and lessons to increase his wisdom. H. Salih felt grieved and started crying. He was crying over those in cries. He said: “O community people, you had organised your community life on injustice. I have been ashamed before God by you. God had ordered me to have patience upon your cruelties, advise you and make you know that you will not do all illegalities for a long time. I submitted to God: that love has come to end because of the troubles they have caused. The milk of advice rises from love and clear-heartedness. They had caused so many harms to me that the milk of advice completely dried up in me. God told me, I shall grant you the feelings of concern for them and keep a balm on your wounds. Then God cleaned my heart as clean as the sky and swept away your cruelties from my mind. I was engaged in advising for the second time and started telling you in kindness with examples sweet like sugar. I have extracted fresh milk and mixed it up with honey and sugar. Earlier these examples acted like poison on you. You were all, head to foot, from the land of poison. There is no need for me to grieve as grief has fallen upside down. You are a recalcitrant community and personified grief. No body cries when grief comes to an end. No one thinks of shaving his head when the wounds of the head are healed”.

sections.heading: No Mourning on Mean Fellows
paras: H. Salih turned to himself and said: “You are mourning for their destruction. Do not do so. They are not worthy of being mourned at.” Truthful reader of the Quran, read it correctly and tell me how I can lament upon the community of rejecters as H. Shuaib has said: Fakaifa aasa alal quwmin kafirin: How shall I lament over a people who refuse to believe (A‘raf: 7:93). H. Salih consoled himself very much but felt a kind of crying in his eyes as without any cause mercy fell its light upon him. Tears were falling and H Salih was in surprise for the tears that were coming from the river of generosity without any effort. His wisdom was asking as to why this grief for the tyrants and whether it was justified? For what are you crying? For their acts? Or upon an army of mischievous fellows with their hearts full of meanness? Or upon their rust-sticken hearts or on their snake-like tongue full of poison? Or upon their sharp teeth like those of dogs, and their breaths? Or on their mouths and eyes full of scorpions? Or on their war mongering, their contempt for others and their cruelties? Be thankful to God that He has put an end to all this. Their hands are crooked, their legs are crooked, and their eyes are mischievous. Their love, their friendship and their anger– all are crooked, they had all gone wrong by following the steps of their elders and their wrong words. All these had put resentment in the mind of that wise saint, H Salih. They were not prepared to take the advice of this saintly elder, H. Salih. They had all become senseless like old donkeys, because of their becoming the ear and tongue of each other. God has brought down his servants from paradise to make them see the end of the dwellers of hell.

chapters.title: Togetherness and Separation Everywhere
chapters.subtitle: In the Meaning of: He has let free the two bodies of Flowing water, Meeting Together; but Between them is a Barrier which They do not Transgress. Marajal Bahraini yaltaqiyan: Bainahuma barzakhul la yabghiyan (Rahman: 55:19-20) [Translator’s note: These two ayats, 19 and 20 of surah Rahman: 55, speak of the barriers between water bodies both on land and sea. Oceanic currents are caused like barriers. Cold water particularly in the Antarctic region being heavy sinks and pushes up the water below. So also, in other regions. This brings about a cyclic motion. 71 Percent of the earth’s surface is ocean. The pushed up warm water moves towards the Antarctic land and a cycle is continuously formed. There is a barrier of temperature between those waters. They do not mix up but move. Further there is a great Gulf stream, which is larger than any river on land, called the river in the ocean, 50 miles wide at the start and half a mile deep at a speed of 4 miles an hour. One starts from the Newfound land in the north Atlantic and moves towards England, then southwards up to the shores of North Africa and then turns towards west up to the Caribbean. Another one starts from Antarctic on the western coast of South America in the Pacific Ocean, moves north up to Peru and then turns west side; a branch of it reaches up to Indonesia and another to the Indian ocean; and the other branch goes towards the eastern coast of Australia. They have great impacts on the temperature of the oceans and also on the coastal regions. Then, there are other currents also in the seas in east to west and west to east directions and in straight line across the Equator.

paras: The west to east clockwise movement is in the northern hemisphere and counter clockwise in the southern hemisphere are due to what is known as Cariolis and the movement in straight line along the Equator is due to the absence of Cariolis effect. These facts became known in the 19th century onwards as the exegesis of these ayats, which spoke of them in the Quran revealed in 7th century.

Abdullah Yusuf Ali further explains about the passing of river waters into the sea in a distinct manner for long distances in the sea and very distinctly visible in the case of Large Mississippi and Yangtse-kiang rivers. And also, of tidal rivers that get sea water for several miles and remain distinct with their qualities up to their estuaries at high tides.
Here, Rumi refers to the qualities of various things which lead to unity, creations being in pairs, and the phenomena of good and bad – Translator]

sections.heading: Barriers between Other Things
paras: You may see people of the hell and paradise living together. Yet there is a barrier between them, which they do not transgress. Those of the light and fire are together, but there is a large mountain like Qaaf between them. They appear to be one but there is a coastless ocean of fog between them. Similarly, in the mines, gold is mixed up with mud and between the mines there are hundreds of forests and populated places. Beads and pearls remain together in a string like a guest for one night. Men and women with beautiful and ugly faces, and good and bad habits live together. This can be seen by anybody if he wants to know. Half of the oceans consists of sweet, bright and moonlike part like (ice caps, glaciers and icebergs) the other half is bitter like snake poison– bitter in taste and black in colour like coal tar. Both these push each other from above and below continuingly like the waves of the sea.

sections.heading: Differences between Intangible Things
paras: Fights are caused among men due to narrowness of mind and sight; and with broad mind and sight, peace comes about. These are the actions of the bodies, with the participation of their respective souls. Those with the light of goodness raise the waves of peace to eliminate jealousies from the hearts of the people. The waves of those of fire are their opposites and bring about wars by bringing up and down of the feelings of love. Love pulls the bitter ones towards sweetness, as it is based upon goodness; but enmity makes the sweet bitter. There is no connection between sweetness and bitterness. Sweetness and bitterness cannot be understood and seen instantly by the eyes. They must be seen through the window of the ultimate end. The eyes that cast themselves at the ultimate end see the right. But the instant sight is misguidance and wrong.

sections.heading: Different Grades of Observers
paras: Many a times, it so happens that many things appear as sweet as sugar, but they have poison hidden in their sweetness. A wise man finds out the struggle between good and bad in them from a distance; another one smells them upon coming nearer; and the third one touches, finds out and rejects. One finds out upon smelling, while another only upon touching them with his lips and teeth. In this case mouth rejects before its being sent down to the throat, even though the devil goes on telling to swallow. The sixth fellow finds out upon its reaching to the throat; and the seventh one swallows and feels ashamed of it after its entry into the body. The eight fellow feels its injurious effect while defecating, after it has already caused harm to his liver. The ninth fellow comes to know of its injurious effect after a long time; and the tenth fellow only after his death, in the grave. When he is provided with further time in the pit of the grave, he gets the visibility to see on the day of resurrection.

sections.heading: Different Durations of Time for Different things

For the grainy sugar and lump of sugar to come into this world, a particular duration is fixed out of the ever-passing time. It requires very many years for the ruby to get colour, lustre and brilliance from the sun. It takes five to seven years for a tree to become fortunate and honoured by bearing fruits. Vegetables become ready for food in two months, but the red rose comes about after a year. This is what God has said about the period of time in surah Al An‘am: 6:2. It is He who created you from clay, and then decreed a stated term: Huwaallizi khalaqakum min tinin, th(s)umma qada ajalan: (Al-An’am:6:2)
paras: I have heard this. I pray that each hair of yours may become an ear to hear. And what all you have drunk is a life-giving water and may it become an antidote for the poison. Do not call what I say as mere words but call them as life-giving water. They contain a new soul in the bodies of words.

sections.heading: Different Impacts of the Same things
paras: You may hear another point on this, my friend! It is very clear as well as hidden like the soul, requiring deep thinking. At one place it is like the poison of snake from among the possessions of the ever-pleasing God, creating confusions about God’s authority and fixing of times. And at another it is medicine; at one place it is rejection; and at another it is acceptance. It is a thorn in one place; at another it is a flower. At one place it is sour like vinegar and at another it is wine. It is fear in one place and hope in another. At one place it is miserliness, and at another it is generosity. It is poverty and riches at the respective places; and at another place wrath, and at another it is getting pleased. At one place it is cruelty and at another, it is consonance. It is denial in one place and generosity at another. It is residue in one place and at another it is distilled and pure. Somewhere it is mud and somewhere it is alchemy. Somewhere it is a defect and somewhere it is an art. Somewhere it is a stone, and somewhere it is a pearl. Somewhere it is a sour fruit and somewhere, it is sugar. Somewhere it is dry and somewhere it is rainy. Somewhere it is torture and somewhere it is justice. Somewhere it is ignorance and somewhere it is absolute wisdom. Though it causes loss to life somewhere, and when it reaches that very point, it becomes a cause of health.

Juice of the unripe grape is sour. When it reaches ripeness it becomes sweet and delicious. At some place when it reaches a stage, it becomes bitter and prohibited as wine, and also makes a tasty dish as vinegar. In this manner there are differences in all matters; and a perfect man clearly understands them.

chapters.title: Good for one, bad for another
chapters.subtitle: To Explain: What the Perfect Master does becomes Misbehaviour for disciples and Should not be Done: as Sweet dishes do not Cause harm to the Physician, but Cause to the stickmen. Winter and snowfall cause damage to unripe grapes and not to the ripe ones, as they are still in the path and not at destinations: Liyaghfira laka allahu ma taqaddama min zanbika wa maa ta-akhkhara: that God may forgive you for your faults of the past and those to follow(Fath 48:2)

paras: If a saint eats poison, it becomes antidote for him; and if a disciple eats it, he will go unconscious. H. Sulaiman prayed to God: O my lord! Forgive me and grant me a kingdom which may not suit another after me for you are the Grantor of bounties: Qala Rabbighfirli wa habli mulkan la yanbaghi li ahadin min ba‘adi, innaka anta alwahhaabu (Swad: 38:35). That is, it has come from Sulaiman that “no one else be given that power and dominance after me as given to me. Do not show such benevolence and grant to anybody else”.

This prayer appears to be one of jealousy for others, but it is not. Think of the phrases “it may not suit another” and “after me”; and it is also not out of his miserliness. It was because, he had seen a hundred risks in rulership; and that the rulership of the world is as risky as the number of hairs in the body; as such I can bear great burdens, but others cannot. He did not want others to be under such a burden and risk. It was out of concern for the other persons.

sections.heading: Great risks of Rulership
paras: It involves such risks for head, for the soul and for the faith, which cannot be a trial for those like us. It requires the courage of Sulaiman to pass out safely from the hundreds of thousands of colours and fragrances. Despite having such a power to protect himself, the rising waves of rulership were choking his breaths. Read also the phrase: “ alqainu ‘ala kursiyyiti”  in ayat : wa laqad fatanna sulaimana wa alqaina ala kursiyyiti jasadan th(s)umma anaab: and we did try Sulaiman: we placed on his throne a body (without life); but he did turn to us in true devotion (Swad:38:34). Despite all his great rulership, might and dominance, coupled with his piety and devotion to God, he was deprived of it for some time (as a dead body on his throne). When the dust of dominance fell upon him, he felt a pity for all the kings of the world and thought that no king should suffer as he suffered. This prayer was a recommendation to God for other kings, that such grants and authority may be given, along with that perfectness that was given to him. Whoever is provided with this grace as provided to Sulaiman, is like Sulaiman. Someone who possesses them will not be after him but along with him. What is the meaning of being with him? It is he only without any other claimant. This aspect requires to be explained further; but let me return to the narrative of the husband of wife.

chapters.title: Demands of Self and Wisdom
chapters.subtitle: Summing up of the affairs of the Arab and his wife about their complaints on Poverty

paras: The explanation of the affairs of that couple is being searched by a sincere spirit. The wife and husband are only an example. They may be considered as yourself full of desires and wisdom, respectively. Women and men like desires and wisdom are necessary for differentiating between good and bad. Both of them are bound by this lowly material world. They are continuingly in arguments and clashes day and night.

sections.heading: Conflicts Between Desire and Wisdom
paras: Woman goes after the necessities of life and home. That is to say: she is after honourable status, food, wealth and self-respect. And the self, like the woman is anxious, and always thinks about those material things; and to get them; sometimes she becomes humble and at times commanding. But wisdom is not aware of these thoughts. It contains nothing but the thoughts of God. Though the truth about this matter is like the grain and appearance is like the net, I would like you to know the details.

If the hidden secret becomes clear and well known, the creation of the world itself will be considered as meaningless and purposeless. If your thoughts and love were purely internal (secret, spiritual) affairs, the form and shape of your salat and fasting would be unnecessary. Your love for your friends is hidden within you, but you give gifts, and exhibit your love through apparent actions. Without love they would be only physical acts. Gifts are given to friends as tokens and evidences of your love for them. Apparent acts are witnesses of your love hidden within you.

sections.heading: Actions Indicate Mind
paras: But your witness sometimes tells the truth and sometimes lies. Sometimes it is intoxicated with costly wine and sometimes with sour curd (or toddy sap). One who drinks sour curd, sometimes exhibits his intoxication by swinging and talking this and that. An ostentatious (showy) performer of salat and fasting exhibits these acts with great showiness, so that the onlooker’s way mistake that he is in the intoxication of the commitment of devotion to God. But, if you see his inside, you will see that it is not real but ostentatious. Yet, apparent physical acts become the marks and signs and guides of what is hidden inside. But guides are sometimes right and sometimes wrong; sometimes perfect and sometimes useless. O my Lord! Give us that discriminating capacity that would make us know what is right and what is wrong!

Do you know as to who can discriminate between right and wrong? It is he, who has a light from God through which he sees (yanzuru bi nuurillah). Sometimes a cause does not cause effect, yet it becomes visible as in the case of family relationship which is a messenger of love. It is the light of God (Nuura Allah). One for whom the light of God becomes the leader, does not remain as a slave of causes and effects. When the light of God enters into his mind, he ceases to be guided by causes and effects; and sees things beyond them. When love spreads its flame in the soul, it gains great power and moves away fast from the effects. It will not be in need of showing itself. Its light reaches the heights of heavens. There are many details of these matters, which cannot be explained by others. You will have to think, study and search for yourself. Goodbye!

sections.heading: Things Distant, Yet Nearby
paras: Though the meanings of love are expressed in the form of actions, yet they are extremely near and distant. For example: they are witnesses of each other in the form of water and tree. If you think over, they are faraway from each other, but they are together. Look at a seed. With the impacts of mud, water and sun, very soon it comes about in the world as a tree. If you look at their realities independently, they are faraway from each other.

Now, you may stop talking about the properties and qualities of things. Tell us about those two seekers of the means of livelihood. Tell us again the narrative of that man and his wife, as it has not yet come to end.

chapters.title: Sincere love causes good impacts
chapters.subtitle: The Bedouin’s acceptance of his Beloved’s demands and swearing that his acceptance is not a design or trial but sincere

paras: The husband said: “I am now disgusted of opposing you. You have got every right to command me. Remove your sword form the scabbard. I shall obey whatever order you give me. If good and bad qualities come upon them, I shall ignore them. I shall get lost in you as I am in love with you and love is blind and deaf”.

sections.heading: Adam Granted all Knowledge
paras: The wife said: “What am I to think. Are you thinking of doing good to me or trying to know my secrets through these designs”?

He said:” God is in the knowledge of all hidden and secretly kept things, who has created the chosen Adam as a clean person from out of clay. In that three yards of body he has created, he has kept all those things that were there in the souls, and in the protected sheet (lowhe-mahfooz) on which is written everything about everything of the universe. He put into Adam’s memory everything that was in it, in such a way that he became fully aware of all that is in it, from the beginning to end. This he did, by teaching him all His names as stated in the Quran: Wa allama Adama alasma’a kullaha: And he taught Adam the nature of all things (Baqara:2:30)

The angels became semi unconscious upon this teaching and said: “Glory to You: of Knowledge we have none: subhanaka la ‘ilma lana illa ma allamtana: (Baqara 2:32). Those informations that they got from Adam were not received by them from the heavens. In comparison with Adam’s clean soul, the expanse of all the seven heavens became short in size. The noble Prophet in a Qudsi Hadith(s) has said: “God Said: My dear, believe in me: I cannot be occupied in any place above and below. Even in the earth, heavens and the empyrean (‘Arsh, the place far above the universe). But strangely I occupy the hearts of the faithful. If you want to search me, search me in their hearts”. He has said in the Quran: Fadkhulii fi i‘baadi wa adkhuli jannati: enter you then among my devotees; and certainly, enter in my heaven: (Fajr:89: 29,30). That is, if you mingle with my devotees, you will find me among them.

sections.heading: Meaning Important; Not Words
paras: The empyrean (arsh), despite its great height and large expanse, upon looking at Adam got out of control. The large expanse is very clear to grasp. But a shape has no value when the meaning comes about. (Words are just sensory objects to explain the reality: the meaning). Every angel was telling earlier; “We were in love with earth. We sowed the seeds of service in earth and we were in surprise about this connection. We were thinking as to what is our connection with earth, when we were made of heavenly qualities. We, as creatures of light, felt surprised at our connection for this dark earth. We were thinking; how can we live along with darkness. But now O, Adam! We feel that our connection with earth was due to your fragrance as your body is made of the warp and weft of earth. We found your clayish body here, but you got the light of knowledge: and we took you to that world where knowledge originates and exists. What all our soul received, is from your soul, which already existed on earth. We were on the earth but were not aware of its worth and of those treasures that were in its depths.

“When we were told earlier to go away from it, we were highly upset and found it to be too bitter to swallow and obey. We even started arguing with God: “O God! Who will come in our place after our departure? We are engaged in glorifying and repeating your name. Do you want to convert this light into quarrels and fights”? But God’s indulgence and pleasing nature spread itself fully and permitted us to speak out clearly: “Speak out to me of whatever that comes to you without any fear just as children speak to the fathers without formalities. I myself know what is within you, but I love to hear your voice, as these simple matters are not worthy of Our grandeur. Yet My mercy preceeds before My wrath. O angels! To show that My mercy preceeds my wrath, I am Myself creating these doubts and suspicions in you, so that you may speak out and I may hold you responsible; and that one who does not believe in My indulgence may not be bold enough. Hundreds of fathers and hundreds of mothers are there in my indulgence. Every moment it comes forward and gets lost. Nobody can count them and grasp them.

“Their indulgence in comparison with Ours is like the foam formed on the ocean of our indulgence. Foam forms and vanishes, but the ocean remains intact in its place. What can I say about even the oyster and the pearl? Oyster has no worth before the pearl. It is nothing but foam before it in worth”.

The Bedouin continued: “I swear upon this foam and upon the ocean. What all I am telling is neither for trial nor it is nonsense. This is all due to my love, concern and submission. I swear upon God to whom I have to return. If you feel that it is for trial, do bear with me for some time for this trial. Do not hide your secret, so that my secret also may come clearly before you. Give me an order to do that which I can do. Do not hide what you think of in your heart. Speak it out so that I am accept what I am capable of accepting. Tell me what I should do and what I am, capable of doing. Think over well as to what I am fit to do!

chapters.title: Coordination between husband and wife
chapters.subtitle: The Wife’s Fixing a means of Livelihood and the Husband’s acceptance of it

paras: The wife said: “Sun is bright, and the world receives its light. Representative of God, the Calif lives in Baghdad as a cause of spring season. If you get attached to the king, you will also become a king. How long do you want to roam about with misfortune? Company of those fortunates, accepted by God is like alchemy. Even their looks are like alchemy. The Prophet’s eyes fall on Abu Bakr and with one confirmation of his prophethood, he became a Siddiq (Truthful).”

sections.heading: Recommendation / Tools Needed to Proceed
paras: The husband asked: “How can I become an acceptable one by the king; and without any recommendations, how can I go to him? I need some means or a scheme to go to him. Have you seen any profession without tools? It is like the case of Majnun who heard from someone that Laila, his beloved, has fallen sick. He said: ‘How tragical? How can I go to her without any credentials? And what will happen to me if I remain without enquiring about her health? Alas! I should have been a good physician so as to be able to go to her with hope”.

God has said: Ta ‘aalaow: “Come”, for this purpose only that we should not feel shy of going to Him and go in obedience to His command of “come”. If the bats had the tools of the eyes and sight, they would have moved about during the day with pleasure”. She said: “When the generous king strolls into the fields, he does not carry any materials; and this empty handedness becomes a cause of pleasure. Possessions as tools and materials speak of reliance upon them and a cause of pride, and lack of self-confidence. Real work of a man is in lack of possessions and lowly state”.

sections.heading: Good Records Needed even before God
paras: He said: “How can I ignore lack of possessions until I become so confident of myself without worry about non-possession. I do not have so much of self-confidence. There should be some witness with me to say that I am poor and destitute, so that the king may feel pity on me for my poverty. Therefore, you should also present a witness to speak of your poverty before the king other than your own words and self-projection. There has to be an evidence for everything. Even when you go to God, you should be with an evidence of your sincerity, as mere words and verbal pleadings become crippled before God, the Commander of all commanders. Before him also a witness of sincerity of heart is required. I need some inner witness to take me before the king. I do not need someone to be a witness of my needs. Truth alone should be the witness of my conditions, so that its light may brighten the situation without words.

chapters.title: Poor man’s Gift to the King
chapters.subtitle: Carrying a Pot of Rainwater Collected from the Forest to be Presented to the Calif at Baghdad Under the Impression that there is scarcity of Water there

paras: The wife said: “The truth is in one’s ignoring one’s own self and one’s struggles. We have got rainwater in our pot, which is your property, capital and means. Carry this pot and consider it as a gift and go to the king. Tell him that we do not have anything other than this and there is no better water than this in the forest. The king’s treasury may be full of gems and pearls, but it may not have such water. This a very rare water”.

sections.heading: Man’s Soul, like Water in Pot
paras: What is that pot? It is nothing but our body surrounding our soul. Water in it is like our saltish senses. O God! I too offer this pot and container before You. Pray accept it from me with Your grace, as You have said: God has purchased of the believers their persons and their goods for theirs (in return) is the garden of paradise. Innallaha alshatara min almuninina anfusahum wa amwalahum bi anna lahumul jannata (Tauba: 9:111). This pot of our body has five holes which are its five sense organs. Keep the water of this pot unpolluted from all kinds of pollutants; so that this pot may face toward the ocean of yourself; and adopt the character of the ocean of yourself. So that, when you present this gift before the klng, he should see it clean enough. There is the possibility that the king may purchase it from you. Therefore, this water will become precious and it will be filled with so much money that would fill a hundred worlds. Close the mouth of the pot and let it be full. God has said: “Lower your eyes from lust”.

The Bedouin was thinking: “Who has such a wonderful gift. It is worthy only of a king like you”. He was not aware that on the way there was the river Tigris in which water, sweet like sugar was flowing. It was flowing in the middle of the city large like a sea and full of boats and fishermen engaged in fishing with hooks.
She continued to tell him: “Go before the king and witness his activities and look at the beauty of the “gardens beneath which rivers flow”. (Jannaatin tajri min tahtihal anhaar)

In this manner, knowledge and feelings are just a drop from that clean ocean (of God). Seek them, observe them and get them. From whom? From the One who has the protected tablet, written on it everything about everything: that is, it is with Him alone in this mother of all Books: with him is the mother of Book: wallahu indahu ummul kitaabi (Ra’ad:13:39)

chapters.title: Extra care for the water pot
chapters.subtitle: The wife’s sewing of the pot with Woollen Fabric and Putting a Seal on it

paras: The husband said: “This is right. Seal the mouth of the pot. Definitely this pot will be a good gift from us to give us a good reward. Seal its mouth with the woollen fabric, so that the king may keep it with him to break his fast. There is no such a gift to be found from any part of the world. It is nothing but the wealth of the tastiest of the drinks. The Bedouin was under the impression that people by drinking water from the forest always remain sick and semi blind.

Birds that make their place of residence on saltish water cannot know the worth of the place of clean sweet water. One living around a fountain of saltish water will not be aware of the banks of the rivers Jaihun of Iran and Euphrates of Iraq and their water. One who does not give up this destructible temporary residence of the world will not know about greatness of discarding petty, mean, human qualities and pleasures of the intoxications available in getting lost in godliness, and the expansion of the soul that is caused by heavenly bliss. Even if you believe in these matters to some extent it is by hearing from your father and grandfather; and these words are like the combinations of alphabetical letters of Abjad.

sections.heading: Abjad letters and their numbers (Translator’s Note)
paras: Twenty-eight Arabic letters in the form of eight words: Abjad, Huwwaz, Hutti Kalman, sa’fas., qarashat, saqaz, zazhagh) contain great operational and calculative values. The first letter alif(a) is numbered as one, followed by 9 other letters with number two to ten: and the eleventh letters carrying numbers from twenty thirty, forty onwards up to hundred, and the next letters carrying numbers as two hundred, three hundred and so on, up to one thousand. That is alif=1, ba=2, jeem=3, dal=4, hi=5, wa=6, zal=7 ha=8, twa=9(I)=10 and thereafter, kaf=20, lam=30, mim=40, nun=50, sin=60, ain=70,  fay=80, the(s)=90, qaf=100 and_further, re=200, shin=300, t=400, siin=500, khe=600, zi=700, duad=800, za=900 and finally ghain =1000.

This numbering is used to make words to signify dates of births, deaths and other important events and used in totems and words of spiritual healings. The ninety-nine names of God are used to infer hidden meanings and also to contain the history of Adam in full. These letters of Abjad have various uses, as per the followers of different esoteric interpretations etc – Translator].
The combination of the letters in the form of abjad, huwwaz etc; are clear to the children, but they are not aware of their meaning and values.

The Arab bedouin lifted the pot and went on the long journey carrying it with him. He was much afraid of the troubles he would meet on the way more to the pot while passing through forests to the city, day and night. The women spread her prayer carpet and prayed to God in all humility seeking God’s protection for her husband and seeking protection to the water carried by him saying: “O God! Take this pearl in the form of water to the river. Though my husband is well informed of the world and aware of the means of protection, but pearls have thousands of enemies in the form of thieves and dacoits. This is not just a pearl but the water from the fountain of kauth(s)ar of paradise. A drop from its water is like a pearl”.

With the support of the wife’s cryings and prayers to God, with his own hard work, and pain-bearings, getting protected from the attacks of thieves and pelting stones, at last the bedouin reached the capital without any specific hurdles. There he saw a grand court of the calif full of graces, grants and awards. Those in need had spread their nets for them. Every moment the needy from all sides were coming and receiving grants and royal apparels. For the Muslims and infidels, good and bad people, this grand court appeared like the sun and rain felling their blessings equally on all, rather like paradise. He saw a group of people heading before the king and another group in wait to follow them when they passed out. All big and small from an ant to H. Sulaiman had all risen up to present themselves as if the bugle of suur has been blown for the entire world. Men of the world were full of gems and gold on their bodies and those of the other world having found the oceans of all truths. One who was lacking courage, became bold here; and the courageous became rich. There was a loud cry: “O those in need! Come forward. The generous are in need of the seekers and seekers are in need of the generous”.

chapters.title: Generous and Needy wait for Each Other
chapters.subtitle: To Explain: Just as a Beggar is in Love with the generous; The Generous also are in love for the Beggars. If the Beggar has patience, the Generous comes to his Door; and if the Generous has patience, the Beggar comes to his door, But Patience is a virtue of the Beggar and a vice of the Generous

sections.heading: No Generosity without Beggars
paras: Generosity is in poverty. It needs someone who seeks it, just as repentance loves the one who repents. Generosity searches for the beggars and the weak just as the beautiful search for mirrors to see themselves. The faces of the beautiful become more beautiful with the mirrors. The faces of gratefulness appear from the faces of the beggars. That is to say that the beggar is a mirror of the generous, but be careful not to blow your breath on the mirror as its vapour dulls its reflective capacity. That is why God told Muhammad in Surah Duhaa not to drive away the beggar saying: wa amma alsaa’ila fala tanhar (Surah Duhaa 93:10).

There is a person whose generosity is exposed by the beggar and there is another who gives more than what is expected by the beggar. Thus, beggars are the mirrors of the generosity even of God; and those saintly ones, connected with God are personified generosity. There are yet, other types of people who are different form the above mentioned.  They are dead people. They are not on this path, but they are like curtains on the door.

chapters.title: Difference between Essence, Attributes and Acts of God
chapters.subtitle: Difference Between the one who begs to God Being Thirsty of God’s Grace; and the one who has no concern and Thirst for God

paras: [Darvish means one who holds to the door. Darvesh holds on to the door of God. He expects nothing from anybody except God. Durvish is an imposter of Darvish, puts on the garb of the Darvish to mislead people to take him as a godly man (Darvish) so that, out of reverence, they may give money and materials. –Translator]

That beggar who is thirsty of God has all his jobs always right due to God’s grace. But the beggar who is thirsty of those other than God is worthless, foolish and devoid of goodness of any kind. He is only a painting of a Darvish and not a living Darvish. Do not give him anything as you do not throw a bone in front of a dog’s picture. He is a beggar of a morsel of food, and not of God. He is dead. He shows himself as a man of God only for the sake of food and materials. He is dead at heart. He is like a painting of a dead man. Do not keep a plate of godliness and esoteric spiritual matters before him. A beggar for the bread is like a model of fish made out of clay. It has only a shape of the fish and is far away from the river. A painting of the fish cannot be a beggar for water as it is not destroyed for lack of water, as against real fish, which gets destroyed without water.

sections.heading: The Darvish Imposter
paras: He is like a domestic bird which feeds upon delicious food given by his master. He cannot become a seemurgh flying high in the air: (Seemurgh is the legendry bird which has thirty different colours). He never goes in search of spiritual foods of grace from God. He is a lover of God only to receive gifts from others for his falsely exhibited love. His heart has no capacity even to appreciate the beauty of nature and fall in love with it. Understanding and appreciating the beauty of God is quite a different matter for him. He talks of the essence of God and of the love for it, without even knowing the meanings of God’s attributes and actions through which only one can reach the essence. God has to be thought about through His attributes; that is His qualities.

sections.heading: God’s, Essential, Attributive and Functional Names
paras: [As per a hadith(s) narrated by H. Abu Huraira, God has ninety-nine names. This list is not exhaustive. Apart from these ninety-nine names other names are also taken such as Ahad, Qahir, Shakir; as close to these ninety-nine names and not so close like Kafi, Hadi, Bari, Jamiil; and also not matching, but are in the Quran like Mawla, Rabb, Qarib, Nasir etc. and compound expressions like Duljalal, Ghafiri al zanbi, Yulijullaili wal alnahar, Yuhyi wa Yumit.
All these names are generally classified as Zaati (Relating to essence; essential); Sifaati (relating to His qualities and attributes; Faa‘ilii (relating to actions: Actions).

There are disparities in these classifications among different Sufis. Some consider all to be the same; some consider except the seven attributes of life, knowledge, power, will, hearing, seeing and talking as essential (relating to essence: zaati) as they are not relational to creation and were there even before the creation. The rest are either attributes of God’s character (sifaati) and his actions (Faa‘ilii) or combination of both. This is a very vast unexhaustive discussion leading to many disputations.
