One need not go into all these details; but this much must be known, as the zaat, sifaat and af‘aall come about very much in Sufi discussions and discourses. Yet, these lead to correctly understand the Divine and Divinity. Citations from H. Imam Ghazali in “Al Maqsadal asna fi sharh asma Allah al husna” translated as ninety-nine beautiful names of God by David B. Burrel and Nazih Daher. Islamic Texts Society, Cambridge 1995 –Translator]

sections.heading: Thoughts About God and Creatures
paras: Our thoughts and imaginations about God are created things and based upon our perceptions of the created things. They cannot lead you to understand God as He is not created. That is: He is the Creator of everything; and even your thoughts are created. One in love with pictures (or imaginations of mind cannot be a lover of God. However, if one is sincere and genuine in his love for the unreal thoughts and imaginations taking them as paths to go to God, the Lord, full of grace, will lead one toward the truth of Himself. This requires an elaborate discussion, and I am afraid of old thoughts as they will bring about hundreds of wrong thoughts in the minds of short-sighted fellows.

sections.heading: Cleaning of heart: Precondition to Know God
paras: Everyone is not capable of hearing the truthful matters just as figs are not the food of all birds. Particularly a dead and rotten bird. So also, a mentally-blind-fellow cannot understand these things. Whether it is water or dust; it is the same for a painting of fish. Soap and alum have the same effect on the colour of the Hindu (black) cannot become fair coloured by these. You may make a mourning face on paper, but it has no effect of happiness or sorrow upon itself, even though those who look at it may feel sorrowful. Only its face is sorrowful; but it has no concern. Similar is the case of a happy face on paper. It only appears to be happy but actually it does not feel happiness. So also, the happiness and sorrow that are hidden in the hearts of people are quite different from those that are on their faces. Joyful pictures are there for your sake, so that they may set aright your inside; mourning pictures are for our sake to show us the right path. The situations of expansion and constriction in the hearts of the saints are to lead them to the right destination. All the things in the world are unreal for them just as paintings are for others. All apparent things are like your clothings which cannot lead you to bathing and cleaning. In order to have a bath you have to remove your clothings. Similarly, you have to remove your passions for the worldly things in order to achieve spiritual attainments. With these worldly desires you cannot see the way to truth as worldly attainments have nothing to do with spiritual attainments.
Now, I turn toward the narrative of that bedouin which will explain many secrets and wonders.

chapters.title: Great Men Treat the Lowly Well
chapters.subtitle: Approach of the Royal Announcers and Guards to the Bedouin, and Acceptance of His Gift

sections.heading: When the bedouin from that distant forest entered the capital city through its gate, the royal announcers came nearer to him and sprinkled the rose water of concern upon him. They found out his need without his telling, as it was their job to grant people even before their asking. They told him: “From where have you come, O, Arab Leader? You seem to be tired. How do you feel?”
paras: He said: “If you meet my need, certainly I am a leader and if you turn your back from me, I am a worthless fellow. O announcers, your faces speak of your greatness and your grandeur is brighter than the purest Jaffary Gold. Looking at you is like looking at many things that deserve to be honoured with sprinkling of dinars upon the head. You are the ones about whom the noble prophet said: they look through the light of God as said in the Hadith(s): ittiqu min firaasati almumini fa innahu yanzuru bi nuurillahi” Fear the sharpness of the wisdom of the faithful, as he looks at things with the light of God. You have come to me to grant awards from God, so that you may cast such alchemic sight upon the copper of men that it may become gold.

sections.heading: Grants beyond expectations
paras: “I am a traveller having come from the forest in the hope of receiving the king’s graces. The fragrance of his benevolences has spread out in the forests. Grains of the dead sand have become living with that. I came here to receive dinars, but having come, I got inebriated with the sighting of this place. A person ran towards a bakery for bread, but upon looking at the beauty of the baker he fell in love with the baker and gave up all pleasures of life. A person went to the garden for the sake of refreshment, but the beauty of the gardener became the cause of his refreshment. A bedouin put his bucket into the well for the sake of water, he drank the life-giving water from the face of the handsome  Yusuf. H. Musa went toward the mount to fetch a little fire, but saw that fire, which made him give up all thoughts of fire. H. ‘Ia jumped up to take himself out of the grip of the enemies, he reached upon the fourth heaven. An ear of wheat became the net for Adam to be caught, upon which he became an ear of all human beings. A falcon flies toward the net to pick up grains but gets caught and gets the fortunate status of sitting upon the wrist of the king. Upon the hope of catching a sparrow or the favours of his father, a child goes to the school and becomes a scholar. H. Abbas came before the noble Prophet to fight with him, kill him and uproot his religion. But became a backbone of his religion and for an empire to be called as khilafat-e Abbasia after his name; and his descendants sat as rulers on the throne. H. ‘Umar went to Mustafa Muhammad to kill him with a sword in his hand and many more determinations; but came to be called as the commander of the faithful and became a leader to be followed by them. A grass scrapper went towards the forest without any expectations but happened to step upon a hidden treasure. A thirsty fellow went to drink water from a stream but happened to see the reflection of his own moon-like face in it and got pleased.

“I came to this door to get something, but upon reaching, I became an honoured chief. For the sake of bread, in order to get some money, I have brought a gift of water. In the desire of getting bread, I have come up to the ruler of the world. In reality, with the desire for the bread of wheat, man has been chased away from paradise, but the bread has brought me back to paradise. Having come here I got myself delivered from the need of bread like the angels. I have no value for the world and I circumambulate around, like the sky without doors, after coming up to this level.

chapters.title: Connection Between Part and the Whole
chapters.subtitle: To explain that the lover of this world is like the lover of a wall which is bright with the reflection of sunlight. He failed to notice that the brightness is not of the wall but of the sun which is in the fourth heaven. He fell in the love of the wall in entirety. When the sun’s reflection went back to the sun, he was disappointed, as stated in the Quran: And a gulf is set between them and that which they desire: wa haala bainahum wa baina ma yashtahun: (Sabaa:34:54)

paras: Movements of the people are never purposeless in the world, except of the lives and bodies of those in love. They are the lovers of the whole and not the parts.

sections.heading: Love should be of worthy things
paras: One who loves a part, gets away from the whole. On the contrary when a part of the whole falls in love with a part, the beloved part drags the loving part towards the whole very soon. Such lover becomes a fool and slave of another. He gets lost, as he has hit upon a weak part. He is dependent upon the beloved either in doing his own work or in doing the beloved’s work. He is a totally helpless and dependent fellow. That is why, it is stated that one should be independent in doing any act. Even in the case of the sinful act of fornication, one should do it with a free woman and not with a slave-maid. Even if somebody has to commit theft, he should do of a precious pearl. Falling in love with a maid causes loss as she goes away with the master. A slave who goes towards his master, does so, because of his helplessness, and always remains so. It should be noted that the fragrance of lovers remains with them and goes away with them. But the thorn remains unaffected. Valueless things remain intact. This matter is like a fool who loves a bright wall thinking of its brightness as its own, without knowing that its brightness is an impact of sunlight. When the sunlight vanishes from the wall, it becomes dark, but remains it its place, as against the sun that has moved away. He gets far away from his desired object; his efforts go waste and become useless; he gets injured in his feet. This is like a hunter who goes after the shadow of the bird, and hunting it is a useless effort. This is the case of the people who stick to the perishable world, which cannot be their wealth.

sections.heading: Go after the Whole, not Part
paras: A hunter very strongly holds on to the shadow of the bird and the bird is sitting amazed on the branch of the tree. But this senseless hunter feels pleased with his worthless unclear situation. If you still stick to the point that the part is connected with the whole and you are satisfied with it, you may become a little more foolish to eat the thorn, as it is a part of the branch that has both thorns and flowers. A part is not entirely connected with the whole. It is just a particle without full connection. If the part were to have the same qualities as a whole, there was no need for God to send prophets to make people differentiate between things. The prophets were sent to make people go with God, the whole of everything. People are parts of the whole of God and they must remain connected with God. O my boy! There is no end to this discussion, as this has a very interesting and attractive connection of the part with the whole and has plenty of scopes to understand. Tell us about the affairs of the bedouin; it has taken the whole time of the day to complete. Tell the rest of the story and put an end to it.

chapters.title: Humble gift Respectfully Taken
chapters.subtitle: The Bedouin’s giving of his Gift to the King’s slaves and Other Details

paras: The bedouin narrated his affairs to the royal announcers and found them to be curious about his gift. He presented the water pot to them and thus sowed the seed of service in the farmland of the king. He told them: “Take this gift to the king and get this beggar of the king rid of his needs. Water in it is sweet, the pot is fresh and green. It contains the rainwater that had collected in a pit”.

sections.heading: As is the King, so are the subjects
paras: The announcers felt like laughing at this, but they accepted the gift as so precious one as life, as the impacts of the well-informed generous king put their impacts on all his servants. Habits and conduct of the kings penetrate into the hearts of the subjects just as the green sky makes the earth also green. Consider the king as a fountain and his servants as the pipes. Water reaches through the pipes to smaller tanks. When the entire water of the fountain is clean, every pipe passes pleasing water through it. And if the water in the fountain is saltish and polluted, the same water passes out of the pipes, as every pipe is related to the fountain.

Consider the meanings of all these words with keen attention. Think of the grand impacts of the soul upon the entire body as it is like its emperor; and it is also called as an ally as it comes into the clayish body form the different world of spirits. Cleanliness and purity of wisdom, upon the cleanly born and good natured, make the entire body well-cultured and noble. On the contrary mischievous, disturbed and impatient love put the entire body into madness. Clean water from a clean river is like the water from the stream of paradise (kawth(s)ar) and the pebbles on its banks are like gems and pearls.

sections.heading: Teachers teach only what they Know
paras: Every teacher is known for a subject of study. The character and knowledge of his disciples go on the teacher’s type. The disciple of a teacher well versed in the fundamentals of sciences learns the same from his teacher and becomes well versed and successful. Student of jurisprudence from a jurist learns jurisprudence and not the fundamentals of sciences and the lexicography. With a teacher well versed in grammar, one becomes a good grammarian. And then the teacher who is engaged in the study of God, makes the soul of his disciples absorbed in God. As against all these various branches of learning, it is only the wisdom of voluntary poverty that shows the path and provides the materials of journey on the day of death.

chapters.title: Pride of Learning is Donkish
chapters.subtitle: Story of a Grammarian Laughing at the Ignorance of Grammar of the Boatman in the Boat

paras: A grammarian sat in a boat and looked at the boatman contemptuously and enquired with him whether he learnt anything of grammar. The boatman said: ‘no’. Then the grammarian said: ‘You wasted half of your life’.

The boatman felt grieved. He had no answer to the point and kept quiet. After some time, the wind pushed the boat into a whirlpool and the boatman asked the grammarian in a loud voice whether he knew swimming. He replied: “Do not expect swimming from me”. Then the boatman said: “Your entire life is lost as the boat is sinking in the currents of the whirlpool”.

sections.heading: Do not make Fun of Lowly People
paras: In such a place ignoring of the grammatical mistakes or total devotion to God is needed. If you know swimming you may jump into the flowing water. River water pushes the dead body upon its surface and carries it. But a living man, not knowing swimming, cannot escape from the river. If you want to be upon the surface of water, better it is to be dead. Similarly, if you are dead in respect of your human qualities, the ocean of the secrets of God will carry you on its head. O the one thinking lowly of the people as donkeys, you will get caught like the donkey slipping upon ice. If you are a great scholar in the world, you may now look at its destruction.

sections.heading: Knowledge of one subject, ignorance of Another
paras: We have attached this story of the grammarian to teach you the grammar of self-destruction in the path of God. The spirit of jurisprudence can be obtained through jurisprudence and the spirit of grammar through grammar. You should give up the pride of your knowledge of jurisprudence and grammar and destroy yourself in the knowledge of the spirit of every science. Our learning and wisdom are like the pot of water; and that calif is like the river Tigris of God. Like the bedouin, we are carrying the pot of water to river Tigris. By doing such a foolish act, if we do not consider ourselves as donkeys, we are certainly donkeys. Our sense of pride of our knowledge is utter foolishness as our knowledge is nothing before God’s knowledge.

Consider the bedouin to be helpless as he was ignorant of the river Tigris and far away from it. Were he to be aware of the river, he would not have carried the water pot from one destination to another? Rather, upon his knowledge of Tigris, he would have smashed the water-pot on a rock. That pot full of shame and disgrace, became a curtain before the ocean of the gnosis of God. Smash it on the rock.

chapters.title: Great Character of the Great
chapters.subtitle: The Calif’s Acceptance of the Gift and Granting despite Dissatisfaction

paras: When the calif looked at the bedouin and heard his story, he filled the pot with gold coins and gave still more than that. He gave him relief from his poverty and gave more grants and royal apparel. And that world of grants and the ocean of offerings told the royal announcers to fill up the pot with gold coins; and when he decides to return to his place, take him to the river Tigris. He has come here through the land route full of hardships. This journey through the river is short and comfortable. He will forget all hardships of the journey if he goes via this route in the boat.

They did as commanded and gave him the pot full of gold coins and with greater pleasure took him towards the river. When he sat down on the boat and saw the great river, he felt highly obliged and started bowing his head and telling: “So astonishing are the grants of that generous king; and more astonishing is the matter in accepting the gift of water. How is it that, that river of generosity has accepted his counterfeit coin”.

sections.heading: Entire world is an Earthen pot
paras: Therefore, my son! Consider the entire world as an earthen-pot which is full up to its mouth with pleasures and delicacies. This pot is a drop from river Tigris of the bedouin’s good nature, which feels extremely elated upon it getting filled up. God was a hidden treasure and burst forth to exhibit Himself because of His own excessive qualities which made the earth brighter than the heavens. The bedouin was also a hidden treasure, which burst forth to make the mud around him honourable, like a king wearing silken apparels.

If someone happens to see a drop from the Tigris of God, he will completely destroy the pot of his own mental achievements and submit oneself in entirety to God. Such of those who have seen this drop have gone out of control and shattered the pot of their own achievements on a rock. Such a person ignored his individual identity by shattering his pot, and after breaking, merged with God and attained finality. The pot broke up, but the water from it did not flow out and this breaking up became of cause of hundreds of corrections and rectifications. Every piece of this shattered pot dances in ecstasy, but one with imperfect wisdom cannot see this dance. In this ecstatic mood, he neither sees the pot not its pieces nor water. Know this well and know that God alone knows the truth of everything.

sections.heading: Not words; but Meanings. Your Food is dust
paras: If you tap at the door of the meanings of words, it will open, and the feathers of thoughts will flutter and make you a high-flying bird like the falcon. The feathers of your thoughts have become heavy because of their admixture with mud as you are an eater of dust in the form of bread which comes out of mud. Both products of the mud like bread and flesh of animals are mud only. Eat a little of them, so that you may not become immobile like mud and remain at it. We eat in this manner all through our life and finally mud eats us in our graves. You become a dog when you are hungry, with wrathful character, indecency and ill temper. And when your belly becomes full, you become dead like a painting on the wall, unaware of everything. Thus, at one time you are a dead body and at another time, a dog. Therefore, you cannot become like a decent, majestically walking lion. And to be like this, one should neither remain in hunger for a long time nor well fed. Both of these are harmful.

sections.heading: Keep Desires in Control
paras: You have many means of achieving objects which are like your game animals. Do not consider those means as anything more than a dog as the hunter does. Just put a little bone before this dog of your desires. Because, if the dog becomes well fed, it gets out of control and fails to run behind the game in proper manner.

Helplessness and poverty dragged the bedouin and put him in motion so much that he reached the king’s court and obtained wealth. If you also become helpless and poor, you can also go to God. In this narrative, I have referred to the grace shown by the king to that poor helpless person. Whatever a man in love says has a fragrance of love; and the streets of love also become highly fragrant. This is not in respect of love of man for man only, but also in respect of the love of God. And the stories and narratives that we have made and of sciences and leaning, are to explain this.

sections.heading: Gains of Voluntary Poverty (faqr)
paras: A man resorting to voluntary poverty (faqr) remains engaged in the esoteric aspects of faith (tasawwuf) as against jurists (faqihs) who speak of apparent exoteric aspects. Yet, if the faqr speaks of jurisprudence, the fragrance of tasawwuf comes about. Even if he talks of infidelity, the fragrance of faith comes, and of certainty in matters of suspicious nature. Any matter appearing wrong will be right and beautifully decorated with truthfulness. Even indepth matters that cannot be generally understood by common men become clear to him, as the foam formed on a clean water body is also clean, as it is part and product of clean water. Consider such words and statements as true and correct like the harsh, unpalatable words of the beloved. Even her abusive words become pleasing because of her beautiful face. Similarly, as the words of the saints are based upon truth, they are always pleasing and full of meanings.

sections.heading: Temporary Forms do not Matter
paras: If you prepare a bread with sugar and then taste it, you will find the taste of sugar and not of wheat. What is seen is only bread apparently, but deep inside, it is sugar. If a faithful man finds an idol made of gold, he sees its inner quality as gold. Only its appearance is of the idol. Therefore, he will lift it for gold, without leaving it for the idol worshipper to worship it. He will also not leave it to its priest to prostrate before it. He will take it and put it in fire and break its temporary form of idol, so that the marks of the idol may not remain on it, as marks are not gold. It is the form of idol that is prohibited which misleads the people. The essence of that idol is gold, which is given to man by God, and the symbol of the idol is only a mark, temporary and man-made.

Do not put your blanket in fire because of its being smitten with fleas; and do not stop going out during the daytime due to the fear of flies. You are an idol-worshipper if you just keep yourself engaged with the apparent shapes. Therefore, ignore the spoken words of the great men and concentrate upon their meanings. If you want to go on hajj join the company of other hajis and do not see whether they are Indians, Turks, or Arabs. Do not look at a painting and its colours but look at the intentions and motives behind them. A black person with thoughts similar to yours may be considered as a fair-coloured one like you, as the inner thoughts are worth-consideration. And on the contrary, if he is fair coloured like you but with different thinking, he may be kept away from your company as the colour of his heart is different from yours. What all has been said here appears to be incoherent, just as the words of the lovers which are also incoherent.

sections.heading: Sufi’s thoughts are not static
paras: Thoughts and speeches of the lovers are incoherent as they are eternal and everlasting; that is; they are from the times earlier to the creation of the world and last even after its annihilation, because they are related to God, who is Eternal. They are like water, every drop of which has head and feet and also without head and feet. May God protect me! What I am saying is not an imaginary story. This is a narration of my affairs and yours at the present situation, which you will know if you think over. You may consider the narrative of the bedouin and his wife in full, to clearly realise this point, that it is as our own narrative. I say this as our present situation because the affairs of Sufis become known for their glory and grandeur not during their lifetime but only when they are no more. A Sufi is always in progress. His today is different from yesterday and an improved one, with greater achievements. He remains so much engrossed in his present that he is not bothered about his future and his end. He has no time also to think of the next moment.

sections.heading: Giver, Taker, Things given, are Relative
paras: In this manner, we are the bedouin, his pot and the king all rolled into one. All these are the same, prevented and put into motion, as stated in the Quran:  yu’faku‘anhu man ufika: he is made to turn away  from it who is himself opposed ( al Zurriyat:51:9). Consider the wisdom as the husband and the self (nafs) and instinct as wife. Bedouin needed money for his self; his wife advised him to meet his needs. But the self and instinct are both in darkness like the need and advice and do not see virtues. But wisdom is like a lamp which sees and shows. In this respect what we must note is that we offer prayers to God as gifts as the bedouin did by giving water. God does not need our prayers. Yet He accepts them to please as the king did. Despite the bedouin, his pot as the king, rolled into one, as stated above, a question arises as to why they appear as different and we reject their oneness. This question can be answered by taking the one (all in all) as having different parts. But this is only a base to start in the process of thought. The fact is that a part is neither an entirety, nor is it connected with it. Therefore, man cannot be part of God. It is not even like the relationship between the fragrance and the flower; because relationship involves equality which cannot be a dominance of one upon the other. It is dependent upon thinking and feeling. It is like the smelling of the fragrance along with the observance of the greenery of the garden. Both of them taken together give us that pleasure which one of them alone cannot give. The sound made by the dove and the bulbul can be considered to be relational to the taste of the hearers. All those things are relational to us.

sections.heading: Patience, Key to Spiritual Elevation
paras: If I go on engaging me in answering to the objectors, I shall not be in a position to serve water to the thirsty; because you know something and want to eliminate doubts, but others do not know. If you are not satisfied with what I said and still remain in confusion and unclearness, you should be patient, and go slow in thinking, as patience is the key to the expansion of breast and reliever of doubts. You should follow a strict mental regimen and protect your mind from insinuations, as your mind is like a bush in which the lions are hidden. They will cause many insinuations. Regimens are many a times more helpful than medicines to cure physical sicknesses. Scratching increases scabies and itchiness. Regimen, in fact, is the root of medical treatment. Therefore, follow the regimen strictly and see the power of your soul. The therapeutic value of regimen is greater than that of medicine; and if the medicine gets digested without curing, it results in a fresh sickness. Be an acceptor of what has been said and hear carefully, and develop the faculty of understanding esoteric matters, so that I may say more and make golden rings for your ears. What to speak of the golden earrings, you will become a gold mine of such great worth as to become more elevated than moon and pliades.

sections.heading: Men with Different Deeds and Desires
paras: Hear, first of all that, all men are different possessing different realities in them from A to Z. All alphabets have different sounds and different connotations, even though all of them together from one point of view and serve common purpose from head to foot. From one angle, they are opposed to each other; and from another they are together, just as a sentence is pleasing in one way and silly in another. The day of resurrection is a day of great trial and presentation of deeds. One who has great achievements will present one’s deeds with great pride. And whoever is ugly like the Hindu with confusions will face great disgrace.

One who does not have a bright sun-like face, will not desire for anything other than a dark night against his face as a curtain. He is like a thorn which does not have a single flower petal, which considers the spring season as an enemy which exposes his secrets. The other person whose deeds are grand like the original flowers from top to bottom, will have the spring season like two bright eyes.

A worthless thorn desires only for autumn, so that it may remain alongside the garden, so that the autumn season may wrap up its defects and ugliness, and may not be visible. Autumn is like the spring and life for it, which shows the stone and the ruby alike. The gardener also knows about its autumn, but his looking at it is better than the looking of the entire world. The perfect master is like the gardener who can look at and find out of defects of the unvirtuous. And therefore, they should expose their defects to him to become good.

sections.heading: Search for a Perfect Master
paras: The perfect master is like an entire world. Everyone can take benefits from him. He is like the moon in the sky whose light is greater than that of all the stars. He is a world in himself and all other masters are his followers and recipients of his virtues. He is a world in himself and is alone in this regard and possesses the truths of humanity in his hands. Every painting and image tells upon his arrival: here has come the spring season with an announcement of the happy news that the flowers are coming, wearing shining coats of mail on their bodies in order to bring forth hanging fruits

When the petals of the flower fall off, the fruit comes about. When the body dies, the soul makes its appearance. Fruit is the meaning and truth; and the flower is only its apparent form. Flower is a happy news and fruit is its grant. When the flower falls down, fruit appears; and also, when the flower gets reduced in size, size of the fruit increases. So long as the bread is not crushed and consumed, it cannot give energy to the body. Grapes that are not plucked from the vine cannot become wine. So long as the myrobalan is not powdered and mixed with other medicines, it cannot make the lungs healthier.

chapters.title: Greatness of Character of Saints
chapters.subtitle: Character of a Guide and obedience to him

paras: Take one or two papers in your hand, O Husamuddin, and write down on them something more about the character of the saints. Though your body is very fragile and weak, yet my worldly jobs cannot be done without you. Though your body does not have enough strength, but you are the only sunlight for us. Though you are a lamp kept in a glass enclosure, but you are a presenter and leader of the heart. When the starting and presenting of the heart is by your hand and wish, the granting of the prize of the necklace of pearls is also by you. Therefore, white down the affairs of the elderly master and saint well aware of the path and hold on to his lapel and find out the right path.

The master (saint) is a spring season, and the people are an autumn season. They are like the night and the master is like the moon. I have called him as elderly, despite his being quite young, because he is an elder due to his connection with God and not with days and years. He is such an elder who has no beginning like the shadow of the Prophet and a single large-sized unique pearl from a large oyster. The noble Prophet has said that he was already a prophet at the time when Adam was just a figurine. He is stronger in intoxicating than the old wine. That is: the intoxication that one gets with the knowledge directly from God alone. The old age of a master is not his weakness but an old wine as it is well known that old wine is stronger.

sections.heading: Guide to lead in search of God
paras: Resort to the intervention of the elderly saint in your search for God as this journey is full of dangers, difficulties and hazards. You have passed on this path many times alone, and therefore, you are in distress, with nobody to guide you. Yet, there are many paths that you have not seen. Be careful! Do not dare to go alone. Do not ignore the guide. One who goes on this path without a guide, is misled and put to loss by the devils. The devil’s voice will cause anxieties in you, if you have no guide. The devil will certainly misguide you, as well before you, many more intelligent than you have been misguided. Read the stories of the misguided from the Quran and know as to what the devil did to them. He took these unfortunates, hundreds of thousands of distances (miles) away from the path and put them to disgrace and shame. You can see their bones and hair and take lessons from their fate. Your self-pride will put you in great self-confidence to go alone like a donkey. Catch hold of this donkey’s neck, and do not leave it to mislead you as it goes in search of green grass. On the contrary, drag it on the right path of those who are well aware. Be careful never to leave the donkey free. Even if you leave it free for a short time carelessly, it will go on the long and wide-green-grass-field up to an exceptionally long distance. The donkey, as a lover of grass is an enemy of the right path and has destroyed many untrained fellows.

sections.heading: Do the opposite of the Demands of Self
paras: If you do not know the path, at least do the opposite of what your donkey says. That itself becomes the right path. Consult it and do the opposite of what it says. One who obeys it is put to destruction. Do not ever befriend your desires and ambitions, because they misguide you from the path of God as stated in the Quran: Follow not desire that it will mislead you from the path. Wa ta tattbi‘al hawa fayudi llaka an sabilillaah (Swad:38:26). The desire of the vicious self is not crushed by anyone in the world except by your own disobedience to it.

chapters.title: Impacts of the Wise are Greater
chapters.subtitle: The Prophet’s advice to H. Ali: “When everyone seeks the Nearness of God Through Obedience, you may Seek the Nearness of a wise and Special Servant of God so that you may remain ahead of them”

sections.heading: Greatness of Wise Man as Guide
paras: The Prophet spoke to H. Ali: “O Ali, you are a true lion of God, brave and strong-hearted. But do not rely upon bravery and come under the shadow of the tree of hope. If everyone presents his obedience to go nearer to the Presence of the One beyond space and time (God), you may seek nearness to Him through your wisdom and the understanding of your own secrets, and not on the basis of your own perfectness and good acts. Come under the shadow of that wise man, who cannot be deviated from his path by anyone. Search for the nearness of God through him; and never turn your head from him at any time as he can make a flower of every thorn and make every blind eye, see. His shadow engulfs the entire world like the mountain of Qaaf (which in poetical imagery is supposed to surround the world). His soul is a seemurgh in the matter of flying all around. Hold on to the hand of the special bondsman of God as he is capable of taking the seekers of God to the court of God. Even if I speak of his praises till the doomsday, do not consider them to be over and came to end. He is a sun for the souls but not like the sun in the sky, as it is because of his light that humans and angels survive. This sun is hidden in the body of man; and know that; only God knows the whole truth.

sections.heading: Do not go away Even if he Rebukes
paras: O Ali, as against all the obediences of the path, hold on to the shadow of the special bondsman of God.  Everyone is running toward obedience of (apparent commands, seeking deliverance in them. But you may go under the shadow of the wise so that you may fight against the hidden enemy of your soul. Of all the obediences, this is the worthiest for you. You will be ahead of all those who have gone forward. When you hold on to a peer (elderly guide), go under his command as H. Musa went under the command of H. Khizr. Have patience without any demur upon whatever Khizr does, so that he may not tell you to go away. Even if he breaks the boat you should not make any remark; and not grieve, if he kills a child. It is like God having called his hand as his own hand when he said: Yadullahi fawqa aidihim: the hand of God is over their hands: (Fatha: 48:10). [ This part of ayat refers to the Prophet’s keeping of his hand over the hands of his followers under a tree and therefore called as baiat ur Ridhwan (Fealty of God’s good pleasure), the Prophet’s hand was called ‘hand of God’]

“Whomsoever God’s hand kills becomes alive. This life is nothing before the everlasting life. A co-traveller is needed. Do not go alone into this forest. It is exceedingly rare that one can pass on this path alone. Yet, he is not alone. The hidden support of the great souls accompanies. The hand of the saint is not short in respect of those who are faraway. His hand is nothing but the hand of God. When they give their support to those faraway ones, those in attendance are certainly better placed than them. When they spread their dining sheet before those faraway; imagine how many different kinds of food they will give to those who go to them and become their guests. There is a great difference between the one who stands before the king and the one standing at his door. There is a great difference, which cannot be accounted for. Those nearby are ahle - kashf (those who get revealed of the light of God clearly) and others are ahle - hijab (those revealed from behind the veil).

“Try your best to go into their inner circle, as otherwise you will be like the chain attached on the outer side of the door. And once you make a great man as your master, do not be hypersensitive to say ill of any unpalatable thing. Do not be like a mixture of clay and water (slush) which is slow to move and spread. Whether the master speaks softly or harshly, it must be accepted with pleasure, so that you may be made as a leader of leaders. If you feel every hardship as disgusting, you will not get your heart purified just as a mirror becomes perfect only upon dusting and cleaning.”

chapters.title: No Talk of Bravery
chapters.subtitle: Story of a man from Qazwain who got his Shoulder Tattooed and Regretting upon the Needle’s Injury

paras: Hear this story from a storyteller, which is about the habit and fancy of the people of Qazwain, a city in Iraq. They get the images of lions and jaguars tattooed on the hands and shoulders. They get such images tattooed, without any hesitation and sense of pain with the points of needles.
One Qazwaini went to a barber and asked him to make a tattoo mark on payment of the charges. The barber asked him: “O brave man, tell me what image I shall make?”
He said: “Make the image of a ferocious lion. My constellation is Leo. Go ahead and make to full satisfaction”. The barber asked: “On what part of the body shall I make”.
He said: “On my shoulder so that in both the battlefield and pleasurable gatherings, I may be strong in my will and conduct with the image of a ferocious lion”.
When the barber started pricking his needle, he felt much pain on the shoulder and started crying and said: “O good man, you are killing me. What image are you making”?
The barber said: “You asked me to make an image of the lion. I am making that”.
He asked: “You have started with what part of the lion’s body”.
He said: “I have started with the lion’s tail”.

He said: “O the light of my eyes! Stop making the tail. The tail and the tail’s place have stopped my breath. The place of its tail has choked the pace of my breathing. Make a lion without a tail, O lion maker! The pricks of your instrument have tired my heart”.

The barber started tattooing from another part of the lion’s body without any pity and concern for his client. He shouted and asked:” What part of the lion’s body is this?”. He replied: “Gentleman, this is the lion’s ear”. The client said: “Give up the ear, let not the lion have the ears and finish the work fast”.
Then the barber started pricking from some other place and again the Qazwaini started shouting: “What organ of the lion is on the third side”. He replied: “It is the lion’s belly”.
The Qazwaini said: “Let not the lion have a belly. What need does a lion have for the belly? Leave it for God’s sake. The pain has increased very much. Let not the lion have a belly”.

The barber got puzzled and stood for a long time with his finger between the teeth. Then he threw away the needle and said: “Has it ever happened in the world? Has anybody seen a lion without tail, ear and belly? God Himself has not created such a lion. When you do not have the strength to bear with the pricks of the needle, do not ever talk of a ferocious lion”.

sections.heading: Forget yourself to Achieve Spiritual Success
paras: O my brother, have patience on the pain of the needle’s pricks so that you may escape from the pricks of your unfaithful-vicious-self. Because, such of the people who make their existence free of their self, get worshipped by the heavens, sun and moon as stated in the Quran: wa sakhkhara lakum ma fis sama wati wa alardh:  God has subjected to your use all things in the heavens and on earth. (Luqman: 31:20).

In whosesoever’s body the arrogant self is dead, he will be obeyed by the sun and clouds. When his heart learns to brighten patience, sun will cease to burn him. God has said that the bright sun passed off bypassing the cave. Wa tar alshamsa iza tala’at tazawaru an kahfihim zata alyamiini: you would have seen the sun when it rose declining to the right from the cave (Kahaf: 18:17). Those in sleep, whose affair was with God, found the sun bypassing them.

The thorn becomes pleasing like the flower before that part (man) who gets connected with the whole (God). Expression of the greatness of God is by means of making oneself humble and mud-like. The learning of the oneness of God is by annihilating oneself before Him, considering Him alone as existing. If you want to be bright like the day, set fire to the existence of your dark night. Allow your copper-like body to melt with the alchemy of the existence of the Granter of existence of all. You, very strongly hold on to the two existences of “I” and “We” and it is these two existences, that are the cause of all problems.

chapters.title: Company of Brave, Cunning and Greedy
chapters.subtitle: Going of the Wolf and Fox for Hunting with Lion

sections.heading: Mean Fellows Remain Mean, even with Great Ones
paras: A lion, wolf and a fox went together in search of a prey and reached the hill. All the three of them had decided to go deep into the forest for a good prey, so that the help of each other might exert pressure on the game to catch it. Though it was a matter of shame for the brave lion to seek their support, yet he joined with them to honour them. Though for such a great king, it was troublesome to take their help, he joined with them as it is well known that companionship is a mercy. In similar manner, the moon feels ashamed of the stars, yet she remains with them to honour them. The command came to the Prophet from God: And consult them in affairs: wa shaawirhum fil amri: (Al Imran: 3:159). This was inspite of the fact that no opinion could be above his own.

A grain of millet became a companion of gold in a balance not to become brilliant like gold. So also, the soul has joined the company of the body; and the dog has been watchful at the door of the master. All these situations do not elevate the value of these mean things.

When the group of lion, wolf and fox went upon the hill with the grandeur of the lion, they caught a hilly sheep, a forest cow and a fat rabbit, and they met their joint object. Whoever happens to be in the company of the brave lion will not feel any deficiency of meat at night or day. When they brought them dead, full of wounds and blood to the forest, the wolf and the fox desired the booty to be divided among them as per royal justice among the kings. The lion found out the reflection of greed on their faces and the reason thereof.

Whoever happens to be a lion and leader of the field of secrets recognises whatever is there in the hearts. Therefore, while in the company of such persons, do not allow insinuations to come into your heart. Keep it clean of all bad thoughts. He knows, yet he remains silent and hides his own thoughts in smiles just as one does not bother about the donkey’s movements. Despite this, the lion did not express openly, and showed consideration to their thoughts. Yet he decided in his mind that he would punish those mean beggars. He said in his mind: “You are not satisfied with my generosity. You think in your own mean fashion. Remember the existence of your opinion is dependent upon mine which is decorative to the world. How can a painting teach the painter, which is coming into existence due to the painter’s thinking, observing and working? Your suspicion on my generosity is because of your own shameful nature for the world. It is like what God said: they imagine an evil opinion of God. On them is a ground of evil: Zannina billahi zonal alsawi; ‘alaihim dairatus saaw: (Fath: 48:6). If I do not finish them off; it would be a mistake. I shall save the sky from the disgrace of your existence, so that what I do may be an example for others”.

sections.heading: Be cautious upon Great Men’s Smile
paras: The lion was laughing at these thoughts. One should not remain uncautious upon the smiles of a great lion-like man. The possessions of the world are like the smiles of God which have made us drunk, arrogant and rotten. O keen observer, understand the risks involved in them and know that poverty and sickness are like a paradise in comparison with them, because they uproot the nets of smiles.

chapters.title: Great Men Test the Lowly
chapters.subtitle: The Lion’s Testing of the Wolf by Telling him to divide the Booty

paras: The lion told the wolf to divide the booty. He said: “O old wolf! Revive the principles of justice. Become my assistant in this act of dividing so that your worth may become known”.
The wolf said: “The forest cow is your share as it is big in size and you are big, great and mighty. The sheep is my share as it is in between and of middle value; and the fox may take the rabbit”.

sections.heading: No Equality with the Mighty
paras: The lion said: “What nonsense do you speak of. When I am there amongst you, there is no question of you, me and he. What kind of a dog you are that you look at yourself in the presence of an unmatchable, wonderful lion like me. O self-loving donkey come before me”.

The wolf came before the lion, and he hit him with his paw and tore him to pieces. When the lion did not see a good opinion in his brain, he punished the wolf with a punishment that pulled out his skin. Then the lion said: “By looking at my greatness, why you did not wipe off your proud existence (and asserted your own opinion instead of leaving it to me alone), you do not deserve to live. It was necessary for me to finish you off when you did not kill yourself (but stood independent before me as an equal). Though I am dominant in the act of grace and grant, yet sometimes, I must resort to justice and punish the wrong doers. Everything other than God is to perish and therefore, if you have to remain alive, you should merge yourself with Him. God has said: kullu shaiin halikun illa wajhahu:  Everything that exists will perish except His own face: (Qasas: 28:88). Whoever gets annihilated in Our essence, will not get into the category of “everything will perish” (halikun). This is because he gets into none (illa) for himself leaving everything into “except for God” (wajhu). One who enters into the ‘except God’ does not perish. Whoever makes an announcement of ‘Me’ and ‘You’ at the door of God, is chased away from the door and remains in the grade of ‘none’ (illa) for himself.

chapters.title: No — I and You
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of one who tapped at the Friend’s door; From inside a Question Came;” who is it?”. He said, “It is me”. Then came another voice: “if you say, it is you”, I shall not open the Door for the one who says it is me to himself: Please Get back”

paras: A person tapped at the door of a friend, and the friend asked from inside: “Who is it?  Do not tap the door”. He replied: “It is me”. The friend said: “Go away. It is not a time to meet anybody. There is no place for a raw fruit on my table”. That is to say: the caller was still a raw fruit not having understood the taste of friendship. Such a raw fruit ripens only if it suffers the heat of separation and aloofness. No one can teach him the worth of friendship, which does not keep the difference of ‘you’ and ‘me’. When your own self continues to exist in you, it is better that it is put into burning fire to destroy it in full.

chapters.title: When “I” and “You” Become one
chapters.subtitle: Feeling Ashamed of the one Who said: “It is me”. And his going away from the Place on Journey and Undergoing sufferings for One year; and then Returning to the Friend. The one in house asked: “Who is it’; and he said: “It is you only at the door”. He denied his self by himself

paras: That person left the place on a journey for one year burning himself in the flames of his friend’s separation. Getting burnt in this manner, he returned and went toward the house of his friend. And then tapped on his door with utmost fear and respect so that any uncourteous word may not come from his mouth. His friend said from inside: “Who is at the door”. He replied: “My friend. It is you only at the door”. Then the friend said: “Now that you are not ‘you’ anymore, come inside”.

sections.heading: Only One Thread Enters the Needle’s eye
paras: There is no place for two persons claiming ‘I’ or ‘Me’ in one house. When they become one, there will be no duality, and the states of ‘you’ and ‘I’ get lost. There is no scope for two separate threads for entering into the needle’s eye. When already one thread is there, the other thread cannot penetrate but when both are joined, both can penetrate as one. Now that you have entered into oneness, you may enter the needle’s eye. There is a connection between the needle and the thread, but the needle’s eye does not suit for a camel to enter. That is the impossibility that is cited in the Quran: nor they can enter the paradise until the camel can pass through the eye of the needle: La yadkhuluna al jannata hatta yaliju al jamalu fi sammial kaiyat (A’raf: 7:40)

The camel’s body, like the vicious self cannot become thin other than through the scissors of hard performances, and austerities of rejections of physical comforts and crushing of vainglories. But at the same time be careful enough to note that these cannot be possible without the support of His hand through His order of ‘kun’ (be) when it comes into being ‘fikaan’.

sections.heading: Three armies of God
paras: Every impossibility is possible through His hand and every mischief becomes inactive. The born blind and leper become normal, and even the dead get life upon His whisper of ‘kun’. Such of those non-existents, who are worse than the dead in the matter of life, lose their qualities of non-existence at His hands and come to life. Read the ayat: every day in new splendour does He shine: kullu yawnim hawa fi shanin: (Al Rahman: 59:29), and do not consider him to be without work and activity. His most ordinary job is that: every day He sends three armies towards our side. One army (of semen) moves form the backs of the fathers toward the mothers so that it may reach the ova and develop there. Another army marches from the embryos of the mothers toward this bowl of earth so that it may be full of males and females. And a third army takes the men and women from the earth’s bowl toward death, so that everyone may look at his good deeds. Yet even before these three armies, another army from God enters into the mind as lust and passes into the soul. This (lust) from the soul enters into the heart and from there to the whole body.

Thus, you will see that God’s armies are uncountable as has been said: None can know the armies of your Lord, except Him. And this is no other than a warning to mankind: Wamaa ya‘lamu junuuda rabbika illa huwa wama hiya illa zikra lilbashari (Muddaththi(s)r: 74:31). There is no end to this discussion. Let us go toward those two clean hearted friends.

chapters.title: Acts Different, Object same as between Friends
chapters.subtitle: The Friend’s calling of the Other Friend after the Latter’s Training

sections.heading: Different Acts and Appearances with same Object
paras: He said: “My friend, you may enter into me in full as now we are not opposed to each other just as the flower and the thorn are not opponents but live together in the garden. Now the two threads are joined together. They are not two anymore. You see two letters Kaf and Nuun (K and N) distinctly, but together they form a word kun. Those letters mingled with each other and became one word (kun) like the bow to drag nonexisting things from the world of nonexistence into this world of existents after making them as existents with the sound of ‘kun’ by God. Though the bow has two different ends in shape, but the function and effect of both are one, by slightly moving toward each other. Whether it is by two legs or four legs, the object of movers in both cases is to move on the way. Like the scissors despite being two cause cutting together. Look at two washer men; they appear to act differently. One puts the clothes in the stream; another takes them out and dries. Then the latter wettens the clothes once again as though he is doing acts opposing to the former’s acts. Though both appear to act against each other, their heart is one and their object is one. Every prophet and saint shows his own way, but they are the same in taking the people toward God.

chapters.title: Inattentive Fellows are Deprived
chapters.subtitle: Speaker’s Hesitation to Talk to Audiences Inattentive

sections.heading: Gardens with Underneath streams
paras: As the hearers in the audience fell into sleep, God stopped the supply of water (of thoughts) to the water mill bringing halt to the grinding stones. This water is the flow of the knowledge of secrets which passes from the heart up to the grinding stones of lips, and from these grinding stones the secrets flow out for the purpose of teaching you. When you were not in need of the grinding stones of the lips, the water of secrets of God that started flowing from the heart, took a reverse path and went back to the heart, the place of its origin. Speaking is for the sake of your education, as otherwise, the stream of this water of heart flows within the heart itself. This water flows slowly and continuously without making any sound, towards those gardens which have streams underneath, as stated in the Quran as many as thirty-six times: jannatin tajri min tahtahal anhar. These are spoken words and phrases made of letters.

sections.heading: Bodyless Verb Producer of Nouns.
paras: O God, show to our souls that place, where soundless speeches come about without letters and words (soundless), so that the soul may be made to move with its head toward that vast field that has no physical barriers. That is the world of revelations. That field, which is large and pleasurable, the spiritual field, from which this visible and cognisable, physical world gets its materials. This visible, cognisable world of existence of matter, despite its large size is exceedingly small, and therefore its gains are full of pain and hardship, and its losses cause grief. Again, this world of matter is smaller than the world of imagination and mental perception. It is because of this anxiety that the moon becomes a thin and weak crescent. This world of sensation and colour is very narrow; rather a small prison because of its being a compound of elements with limited quantity, which attracts the senses.

But the world of oneness is hidden and entirely different. You may turn toward this if you have a taste for it. The command of kun (be) was a bodyless verb. It was just a command and dressed itself with letters kaf and nuun when the world of matter came into existence. There is no end to this discussion and therefore return to talk about the wolf.

chapters.title: Submission to Authority is Good
chapters.subtitle: Lion punished the Wolf for its Indecency

paras: The lion, as a leader, smashed the head of wolf, so that there be no secondary leadership and distinction. O old wolf, We have taken revenge of you as you have not submitted yourself in entirety to the leader, as was done by God in respect of Pharaoh: we exacted retribution from them: we drowned them in the sea: fa antaqamna minhum fa aghraqnahum fi alyammi: (A’raf:7:136).

After this, the lion turned toward the fox and asked it to divide the food. The fox bowed its head and said: This fat forest cow is for your breakfast, my great king. The sheep is for your lunch to be used later by the victorious king. The rabbit is for the dinner of your generous and gracious lordship”.

sections.heading: Learning from the Fate of Others
paras: The lion said: “O fox, you have a brightened sense of justice. From whom did you learn this type of division. You are great! From where you learned this?”
The fox said: “O lord of the world! I learnt this from the fate of the wolf”.

The lion said: “You have mortgaged yourself to our love. Take all the three in your possession and go off. O fox, you have become ours in entirety. When you have joined us and become one in us, we cannot harm you anymore. We are yours and all these hunted animals are yours. Keep your legs on the seventh heaven and exhibit your greatness. When you have learnt the lesson from that mean wolf, you are not a fox, you are my lion!”

He is wise, who learns from the fate of others, their death, and from the avoidable problems. Then the fox expressed thanks for the fact that if was called upon to distribute the food after the wolf. It thought within itself: had I been told before the wolf to distribute, who could have saved my life?”

chapters.title: When Late comers are Fortunate
chapters.subtitle: Object of the Story: Those Born in later times are Fortunate

paras: Thanks to God that He has created us in this world at a later stage than the earlier people; so that we could hear of the punishments they have undergone and learn lessons from the past periods. So that, we can protect ourselves well like the fox from the fate of the earlier wolf. It is for this reason that we have been called as the “blessed community” by that truthful Prophet, everspeaker of truths, as we are the last of the communities, having come in the end. Look at the bones and hair of those wolves (earlier people) with great care and learn from their fate. A wise man removes arrogance and pride from his head, when he hears of the narratives of Pharaoh and the people of ‘Aad, who were destroyed for their arrogance and pride. If he does not remove these things from his head, others will take lesson from his fate.

chapters.title: Great should not be Dishonoured
chapters.subtitle: Noah’s warning to his People not to entangle with him saying: “I am the Veil of God. By Entangling with me you are entangling yourselves with God”

paras: As an advice, Noah told his people: “Accept the grants of God. Think over, O arrogant fellows! I am not I. I am dead from my own point of view, but I am alive through my beloved God. When this is so, I have no death for myself. I am to live for ever. I am dead with regard to human sensibilities. God has become my ears, eyes and realisation. As I am not I: what I am telling is not from me but from God; and whoever takes objection to this is an infidel. My physic is like that of the fox and within me it is God as lion. Therefore, do not show your valour before this fox. If you cannot accept this face, be prepared to face the roar of the lion.”

If Noah’s hand had not got the support of God, then how could he have upset the established order through the deluge. Hundreds of thousands of lions were there in his body. He considered both the worlds as a grain of millet. He had separated himself from the sense of “I” and “We”. He was like fire and the world was like a heap of harvested crop. It was obligatory on the heap of crop to pay its one tenth share to him, but when it refused to give that share, he set the entire heap on fire. Lion will tear up the wolf and recite upon him fantaqamna minhum; we took revenge of them. He will receive the injury like the wolf from the lion. One who tries to show his valour before the lion is ill-witted. It would have been very good if the injury had been on the body; so that the heart and faith would have remained protected. After reaching at this stage, my (Rumi’s) strength and courage came to end; I do not know how to reveal the secret behind this.

sections.heading: Submission to God in full
paras: However, I give a hint, from which, perhaps you may know of it. Eat less like that fox and do not make fun of the lion. Keep all your feelings of “I” and “We” before God and leave everything to Him. He is the master of the country; and let Him alone rule it. Keep yourself aloof. Make yourself a beggar and go on His way, so that the lion and his hunt may be yours. He is clean, unique and uncomparable in His nature. He has no concern for the rind and pulp of the fruit. All the hunts and the provisions of the world are meant for the slaves of this king. He has said: Is not God enough for his servants. Alaisallahu bikafin ‘abdahu (Zumar 39:36); so that his bondsmen may not search here and there. Whoever relies upon Him, actually does good for himself. He has not created things for Himself as He has no need for all that but has made for His creatures. All these are pleasing for one who realises. Of what use are all these countries and kingdoms, far one Who has made them all.

Therefore, keep your heart protected and clean before the uncomparable, so that you may not have to feel ashamed due to your suspicions, before God, as well as, before your true guide. He sees all your secrets, thoughts and searchings, as clearly as a hair in seen by you in pure milk. One who has a plain, unpolluted and unimpressed heart, becomes a mirror of all hidden things of the hidden world. Certainly, your master coverts your suspicions into certainties because, a faithful person is a mirror of the faithful as has been said by the Prophet: almu’minu miratul mu’min. Definitely, you are a mu’min and so also your master. Yet there is a great difference between you two. When the master rubs your gold on his touchstone, he separates the suspicions from certainties. When one’s soul becomes the touchstone, the genuine gold and counterfeit become clear.

chapters.title: Why Sufis held in Greater honour
chapters.subtitle: Kings Make the Sufis sit Before them so that their eyes may become Brighter

paras: It is a habit of the kings, you might have heard and remembered, that they keep their generals and army commanders on their left side, as the heart lies in the left side of the chest. They keep the nobles and learned men on their right side as the acts of taking notes, making entries in books and writing is done by the right hand. They make the Sufis sit before them, facing them as they are the mirrors of the soul and better than the visible worldly mirror.

sections.heading: Sufi’s Have Clean and Polished Hearts
paras: Know this my son! Sufis are the guards and protectors of the kings. They are simple and free with their heads looking downward. They keep their breasts cleansed and polished with the remembrances and thoughts of God so that the mirrors of the hearts may receive fresh impressions. Whoever is born beautiful in the natural process, should keep a mirror before himself. It is only the beautiful who love to be looking at the mirror. Cleaning and polishing of the heart comes about with the piety of the heart: taqwal qulub: as stated in the Quran to whoever that holds in honour the symbols of God.

Whoever has a beautiful symmetrical face goes for the mirrors (to appreciate himself and through him to appreciate God). May security be upon you. In this connection, you may hear a citation so that you may not go toward the apparent aspects anymore.

chapters.title: Humble beginning and Great End
chapters.subtitle: A Friend’s coming to H. Yusuf to look at him After a Journey

paras: A well-wishing friend of H. Yusuf came from a long distance, and became his guest, as they were childhood-friends and relied very much upon their friendship. He made H. Yusuf think of the jealousy, and atrocities committed by his brothers upon him and said: “They were a chain, and we are lions. Lions do not have any hate for chains. We should not have any grievance with God’s wish. Though the lion had a chain around his neck, yet he was the most prominent among all other prisoners”. He asked him:” What was your condition in the prison and the well”. H. Yusuf replied: “Just like the condition of the waning moon. Even though the new moon is completely bent, when it is newly born, it grows little by little every night and becomes full moon. A pearl may be crushed in mortar, still its powder becomes a cause of brightness for the eyes and heart. Wheat grain is put under the soil, but it comes out from there as ears of the wheat. Once again when it is powdered between the grinding stones, its value increases: it becomes bread, and increases life. Then the bread is crushed between the teeth, when it becomes the life of wisdom, understanding and lively consciousness. And when the man’s soul got absorbed in the love of God, the seed of wheat fell in amazement as to what it started with, and what became its end.  Then again, when the soul was lost in God, it came out of its amazement, and went back to its sense and consciousness. One world got the fruits of this soul’s goodness, without any expectation, and another community got the hope of getting some benefits. There is no end to this talk. Let us go to see what H. Yusuf did to him.

chapters.title: Gifts to Friends and Gifts to God
chapters.subtitle: H. Yusuf’s Demanding of Gifts from Friend, after discussions with him

paras: After telling all this, H. Yusuf said to his visitor. “What gift have you brought for me”?

sections.heading: Visit Friends with Gifts
paras: I tell you wiseman, do not go to friends with empty hands. Do not go to the flour mill without wheat. Going up to the door of friends with empty hands is like going to the flour mill without wheat. God will ask the people on the day of resurrection as to what is the gift brought for that day. He will say: “Behold! You came to Us with bare hands and alone, as We created you for the first time”: Wa laqad ji’tumuna furada kama khalaqnakum awwala marratin: (An’am: 6:94).

“You have come to Us empty handed just as We had created you empty handed. Come tell Me!  What records you have brought with you for the day? Or is it that you had no hope of returning to Us; and this promised day appeared wrong to you?”

sections.heading: Visit God with Gifts of Good Acts
paras: You did not believe in the promise of this invitation for feasting. Therefore, you will have to eat dust and ash from His kitchen. Had you been a believer of this invitation, you would not have gone to His door with empty hands. Reduce your sleeping and eating to some extent and save some time for service to Him to present it as a gift. Become one like among those who used to sleep but little of the night, and at each day seek forgiveness: kanu qalilam minal laili ma yahja‘uun: wa bil as-haarihum yastagh firuun. (Zurriat: 51:17,18)

Move yourself a little in the foetus, so that you may get the senses that see the light. And if you get the eyes to see the far-off things, you can keep your steps on the seventh heaven. When you go out of the world which is like the foetus of mother, you enter into a large wide field, which is called as the earth of God — spacious enough for you to move yourself here and there: Ardullahi wasi’a tan fatuhajiruna fiiha. (Nisa: 4:97), This is the one wide field where the prophets have gone. Heart never fears in this large field and the date-palm never dries up there, as against this world where you carry the burden of your senses, and therefore, you feel tired, slack and reversed.

sections.heading: Complete rest in Sleep
paras: During your sleep you do not carry the burden of your senses but ride upon your senses and remain at rest. Consider the condition of your sleep as the condition of the saints, in which they ride upon their senses. They are like the companions of the cave who slept for a long time in the cave, who appeared awake but, in fact, they were asleep: tahsabuhum aiqazhan wa hum ruqud: (Kahaf 18:18). They were turned toward the right and left by God without their feeling about it: We caused them to turn over to the right and the left: wa tuqallibuhum zatal yamiini wa zatalshimaali (Kahaf 18:18).

sections.heading: Saints rest even when Awake
paras: What is the meaning of turning to the right? It is good acts. And turning to the left is physical engagements. You see the saints in difficulties but for them there is no grief, as stated in the Quran: Behold! Verily on the friends of God there is no fear, nor shall they grieve: Alaa inna awliya allahi la khawfun alaihim wala hum yahzanuna: (Yunus:10:62). But their acts appear to be as of humans, but they are absolutely unaware of them. These actions that appear from the prophets when they are awake, are like the echoes from the hills, but these are not caused by the hills. You may feel the echo from the hills as good or bad, but the hills are not aware of them.

chapters.title: Gift suitable for H. Yusuf
chapters.subtitle: The Guest’s telling: I have brought the gift of a Mirror for you, so that you may Think of Me whenever you see Yourself in it

paras: H. Yusuf said: “Come on! Give me your present”. His friend felt grieved and took a long sigh and said: “I searched for a few presents to give to you, but I was not satisfied with any. How can I take a grain toward a mine and a drop toward the sea of Oman? It will be like taking cumin flowers to Kirman (which is well known for it). Even if I keep my life and soul before you, they are worthless. There is no seed which is not present in this lot excepting your own beauty which has no next. Therefore, I thought it wise to present to you a mirror so that you may see your own beauty, bright like the sun and moon. O beauteous light! I have brought a mirror for you, so that, whenever you look in it, you may remember me”.

sections.heading: Look into Yourself for Success
paras: So saying he took out a mirror from his possessions.

Engaging oneself with the mirror is what the beautiful should do. What is the mirror of existences? It is getting lost. Therefore, get lost, if you are wise. Life can be seen in getting lost. The rich lose their money by giving to the poor. The hungry man is himself a mirror for the bread. The small lump of cotton that is set on fire with the help of the sparks of flint sets fire to the wood is a mirror of the sparks. The place of annihilation and defects of temporary and mean materials is an exhibitor of the beautiful and lasting things. This existence is pollution in entirety and its loss results in cleanliness of the heart.

sections.heading: Defects Lead to Perfectness
paras: When the clothes are already well stitched, they need no tailor to show his skill. The log of wood has to be uncut so that the carpenter may cut it to pieces of small and large sizes to meet his requirements. The bone setter goes to the place where the one with broken legs is living. If a person does not fall sick, there will be no scope to show the beauty and expertise of the physician. The low level and cheapness of copper can be known only in comparison with alchemy. All defects are a mirror of the deficiency of perfectness; and disgrace is a mirror of honour and grace. Opposites clearly speak of the truth of things: honey becomes quite clear in comparison with vinegar. Whoever looks at himself and finds out defects runs fast toward his perfection. That is why one who is suspicious of his perfectness but does not rectify, cannot fly up to the lord of Majesty and Honour.

sections.heading: Superiority Complex: A Common Sickness
paras: There is no greater sickness than the arrogance of one’s own superiority. This happens when the soul is empty of good qualities. Much blood requires to be shed from heart and eyes in order to get rid of misguided arrogance. The sickness of Iblis was his sense of superiority, which he expressed by saying about Adam: ana khairum minhu; “I am better than He”: (Sad: 38:76). This sickness is in the self of every man, though he considers himself to be very considerate to others. Think of yourself as clean water, but at the same time, be sure that at the bottom of every stream there is dirt. If you stir it to test it, you will see the change of its colour. Be sure, young man, every stream has filth in its bottom, even though the water appears clean and clear. So also, is the fact about the inside of your heart, which you cannot remove, on your own.

sections.heading: Seek the Help of Elders
paras: A wise and learned master of the ways can clean the streams of the gardens of the body and soul. The stream cannot clean itself. The knowledge of the learned elder is beneficial as it is from God. Just as water of the stream cannot clean its filth at its bottom, man’s knowledge cannot clean his self of the filth of ignorance. You cannot treat the wounds yourself on your back; you have to go to a surgeon. Because of your carelessness, flies have covered up your wounds so that none can see the puss of the wounds. Those flies are your fond hopes and improper thoughts, and your wounds are the darkness of your wrong affairs. If the elderly saint applies his balm on these wounds, you will be rid of your pains and cries. You should not think that you are completely cured of sickness, as it is not the balm but its healing impacts that have fallen on the wounds. O the one wounded on the back, do not turn yourself from the balm, and consider the relief you got as only the reflection of healthiness and not as total cure. O young man: there is no end to this discourse; however, you may hear an incident in this context.

chapters.title: Misleading by Over Confidence
chapters.subtitle: Deviation from Faith of the Writer of Revelation due to the Falling of its Shadow; He Recited the Ayat earlier than the Prophet saying the revelation was upon him

paras: Before H. Usman, there was a writer of revelations to the noble Prophet, who was well engaged in the work. (Abdullah b. Sa’ad b Abi Sarah). Whenever the Prophet recited a revealed ayat, he wrote it down on a sheet. The impacts of the revelation fell upon him and he felt himself to be extraordinarily wise, yet he was busy in writing. He was so much obsessed of his wisdom that he said: “Whatever the Prophet said was already in his heart”. The Prophet realised the reflection of his thought; and God’s wrath too fell on his heart, which resulted in his not getting even a word of wisdom. He got rid of the work of writing as well as of his faith; and out of ill will he became an enemy of the Prophet and the faith. The Prophet told him: “You mischievous hard-hearted fellow: how have you become black-hearted if you had a light in the heart. Had you been a fountain of God’s light, such black water would not have flowed from you”.

sections.heading: Even repentance from You Not Provided
paras: With this he was burning inside, yet it was amazing that he did not repent, so that he could protect his honour, and from people’s speaking this and that of him. He got his mouth choked. He could take only sighs, but they were of no benefit. The sword of fate came and severed his head. Many times, a man becomes weighty of a hundred maunds and avoids protecting his honour by not accepting his mistake. This is a hidden chain that deprives him of his freedom. So, his arrogance, and rejection closed the path of repentance. He could not even regret. God has said: we have put yokes round their necks right up to their chins, so that their heads are forced up (and they cannot see): Inna ja ‘alna fi a ‘naaqihim aghlalan fahiya ilal azqani fahum la muqmahuna (Yasin:36:8).

But these yokes are not external. Behind them, there is a wall and we have covered them up: we have put a bar in front of them and a bar behind them, and further we have covered them up; so that they cannot see; wa ja’alnaa min baini aidihim saddan wa min khalfihim saddan faaghshainahum fahum la yubsiruun (Yasin :36:9). He cannot see even the wall that is in front and back of him.

sections.heading: Invisible Yokes, Walls and Chains
paras: The wall there, is like a desert, which has no up and down. He does not know that it is a wall of God’s decision. Your love is a wall before the face of your beloved. You do not dare see the face. Your possessions are a wall before the words of your guide. They will not allow you to hear him. There are many infidels, who have love for the faith; but they cannot accept it as they are chained by shyness, arrogance or by this and that. These chains are hidden but are worse than iron chains, because iron chains can be broken by the axes meant for cutting iron. But these invisible chains cannot be broken. When a man is stung by a beatle, his instinct readies him to get rid of it; but the injury caused by the sting of arrogance causes greater pain, which does not get reduced. The explanation of all this is getting out of the breast; and I am afraid, this may cause hopelessness, and discouragement. But do not be unhappy, and keep yourself pleased, before that Hearer of grievances saying: “O admirer of the seekers of pardons and, O physician of old chronic injuries.” The reflections of wisdom (philosophy) have misguided this unfortunate man. You may cease to look at yourself as great so that you may not be destroyed. The wisdom that is coming out of you is the wisdom of abdals which they have granted to you.

sections.heading: All Qualities are Borrowed
paras: Know this: you are finding some light in your house; but it is not yours. It is coming from the neighbour’s house. Be thankful! Do not be proud and reject the good thing. Hear me! Do not ever be proud. How regretful, this temporary thing has kept the proud people away from the community. I am a slave of one, who at every midway station, seeks fresh information. One must pass through many midway stations before reaching the final destination. Many things that we get are not ours but are taken from others.

Though iron has become red but not by its own qualities. Its colour is borrowed from fire. There is no light in the house on its own; it is entirely from the sun. If the doors and walls tell that they are bright on their own, and nobody has shed any light on them, the sun will say: “You are misled. You will know the truth, when I set at night”. If the greeneries say we are green of our own, we are very happy, smiling and beautiful, then the spring season will say: you may see at yourself when I pass off. Man’s body feels proud of its beauty and appearance, but the soul has kept its wings and feathers hidden within it. It says: “What are you, O dust bin! You are so, for a few days because of me. All your styles and pomp cannot remain in the world. Just wait and see as to what happens when I go away from you.
